content.sanskrit:
vande 'haṁ śrī-guroḥ śrī-yuta-pada-kamalaṁ śrī-gurūn vaiṣṇavāṁś ca
śrī-rūpaṁ sāgrajātaṁ saha-gaṇa-raghunāthānvitaṁ taṁ sa-jīvam
sādvaitaṁ sāvadhūtaṁ parijana-sahitaṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devaṁ
śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādān saha-gaṇa-lalitā-śrī-viśākhānvitāṁś ca
content.translation: I offer praṇāma unto the lotus feet of my [śikṣā and dīkṣā] gurus, my entire guru-varga, and to all Vaiṣṇavas, to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, his elder brother Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, to Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, and all their associates, to Śrī Advaita Ācārya, the avadhūta Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all their associates, and to the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and to Their companions, Śrī Lalitā, Śrī Viśākhā, and all the other sakhīs.
content.wbw: vande — I offer praṇāma to; 'haṁ — I; śrī-guroḥ — of my revered guru; śrī-yuta-pada-kamalaṁ — the beautiful lotus feet; śrī-gurūn — the revered gurus; vaiṣṇavāṁś — the Vaiṣṇavas; ca — and; śrī-rūpaṁ — Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī; sāgrajātaṁ — together with his elder brother; saha-gaṇa-raghunāthānvitaṁ — accompanied by Raghunātha and their associates; taṁ — him; sa-jīvam — together with Jīva Gosvāmī; sādvaitaṁ — together with Advaita Ācārya; sāvadhūtaṁ — together with the avadhūta Nityānanda Prabhu; parijana-sahitaṁ — accompanied by Their associates; kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devaṁ — Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu; śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādān — the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; saha-gaṇa-lalitā-śrī-viśākhānvitāṁś — accompanied by Śrī Lalitā, Śrī Viśākhā and all Their companions; ca — and.

content.sanskrit:
oṁ ajñāna-timirāndhasya jñānāñjana-śalākayā
cakṣur unmīlitaṁ yena tasmai śrī-gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I am blinded by the darkness of ignorance, but śrī guru has mercifully opened my eyes, anointing them with the salve of divine knowledge. I offer praṇāma to that śrī gurudeva.
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; ajñāna-timirāndhasya — of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance; jñānāñjana-śalākayā — with the salve of divine knowledge; cakṣur — eyes; unmīlitaṁ — opened; yena — by whom; tasmai — to that; śrī-gurave — to śrī gurudeva; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
nārāyaṇa-parāyaṇa jadāhaṅkāra-nāśana
rūpānugāmṛta prema prayojanāya te namaḥ
content.translation: O you who are always absorbed in loving service to your spiritual master, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī! O you whose causeless mercy completely destroys the inert material ego! You are the embodiment of the immortal nectar of pure divine love (prema) in subordination to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, which is the highest goal of life (prayojana). I offer my praṇāma unto You, Śrī Prema Prayojana Prabhu.
content.wbw: nārāyaṇa-parāyaṇa — always absorbed in loving service to your spiritual master; jadāhaṅkāra-nāśana — destroyer of the inert material ego; rūpānugāmṛta — immortal nectar in subordination to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; prema — pure divine love; prayojanāya — the highest goal of life; te — unto You; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
nama oṁ viṣṇu-pādāya rādhikāyaḥ-priyātmane
śrī-śrīmad-bhaktivedānta-nārāyaṇa iti nāmine
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhikā.
content.wbw: nama — praṇāma; oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; viṣṇu-pādāya — to him who is at the feet of Viṣṇu; rādhikāyaḥ-priyātmane — who is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhikā; śrī-śrīmad-bhaktivedānta-nārāyaṇa — Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa; iti — thus; nāmine — to him who is named.

content.sanskrit:
śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlā-kathane su-dakṣam
audārya-mādhurya-guṇaiś ca yuktam
varaṁ vareṇyaṁ puruṣaṁ mahāntaṁ
nārāyaṇaṁ tvāṁ śirasā namāmi
content.translation: O Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, you are most expert in describing kṛṣṇa-līlā and are fully endowed with the qualities of magnanimity and sweetness. You are the best of all great souls. I bow my head to you.
content.wbw: śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlā-kathane — in describing Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s līlā; su-dakṣam — most expert; audārya-mādhurya-guṇaiś — with the qualities of magnanimity and sweetness; ca — and; yuktam — fully endowed; varaṁ — the best; vareṇyaṁ — most worshipful; puruṣaṁ — person; mahāntaṁ — great; nārāyaṇaṁ — Nārāyaṇa; tvāṁ — you; śirasā — with my head; namāmi — I bow.

content.sanskrit:
tridandīnām bhakta-śiromaṇiṁ ca
śrī-kṛṣṇa-padābja-dhṛtaika-hṛdi
caitanya-līlāmṛta-sāra-sāraṁ
nārāyaṇaṁ tvaṁ satataṁ prapadye
content.translation: Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, the jewel among tridaṇḍī-sannyāsīs, holds the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa within his heart and experiences supreme bliss when Kṛṣṇa renders service to Śrīmatī Rādhikā. He is always absorbed in thoughts of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the confidential reasons for His divine descent. With deep reverence, I offer my prostrated obeisances at the lotus feet of Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, who is endowed with innumerable transcendental qualities.
content.wbw: tridandīnām — of the tridaṇḍī-sannyāsīs; bhakta-śiromaṇiṁ — the jewel among devotees; ca — and; śrī-kṛṣṇa-padābja-dhṛtaika-hṛdi — whose one-pointed heart holds the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; caitanya-līlāmṛta-sāra-sāraṁ — the essence of the essence of Śrī Caitanya’s nectar-like pastimes; nārāyaṇaṁ — Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī; tvaṁ — to you; satataṁ — always; prapadye — I offer my prostrated obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
nama oṁ viṣṇu-pādāya kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhāya bhūtale
śrīmate bhaktivedānta-svāmin iti nāmine
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja (Śrīla Prabhupāda), who in this world is most dear to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
content.wbw: nama — praṇāma; oṁ — the sacred syllable oṁ; viṣṇu-pādāya — to Viṣṇupāda; kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhāya — to him who is most dear to Śrī Kṛṣṇa; bhūtale — in this world; śrīmate — to the illustrious; bhaktivedānta-svāmin — Bhaktivedānta Svāmī; iti — thus; nāmine — to him who is named.

content.sanskrit:
namas te sārasvate deve gaura-vāṇī-pracāriṇe
nirviśeṣa-śūnyavādi-pāścātya-deśa-tāriṇe
content.translation: My respectful obeisances unto you, O servant of Sarasvatī Gosvāmī. You preach the message of Śrī Gaurāṅga and thus deliver the Western countries, which are filled with voidism and impersonalism.
content.wbw: namas — respectful obeisances; te — unto you; sārasvate — O servant of Sarasvatī Gosvāmī; deve — O divine one; gaura-vāṇī-pracāriṇe — who preaches the message of Śrī Gaurāṅga; nirviśeṣa-śūnyavādi-pāścātya-deśa-tāriṇe — who delivers the Western countries filled with voidism and impersonalism.

content.sanskrit:
nama oṁ viṣṇu-pādāya ācārya-siṁha-rūpiṇe
śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-prajñāna-keśava iti nāmine
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to the lion-like ācārya, oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja.
content.wbw: nama — I offer praṇāma; oṁ — the sacred syllable oṁ; viṣṇu-pādāya — to oṁ viṣṇupāda; ācārya-siṁha-rūpiṇe — to the lion-like ācārya; śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-prajñāna-keśava — to Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava; iti — thus; nāmine — to the one named.

content.sanskrit:
atimartya-caritrāya svāśritānāṁ ca pāline
jīva-duḥkhe sadārttāya śrī-nāma-prema-dāyine
content.translation: His character and activities are transcendental to the modes of nature, and he protects and nurtures those who take shelter of him. He is always aggrieved to see the suffering of the living entities, and he bestows love for śrī nāma.
content.wbw: atimartya-caritrāya — whose character and activities are transcendental to the modes of nature; svāśritānāṁ — of those who take shelter of him; ca — and; pāline — the protector and nurturer; jīva-duḥkhe — at the suffering of the living entities; sadārttāya — always aggrieved; śrī-nāma-prema-dāyine — the giver of love for śrī nāma.

content.sanskrit:
gaurāśraya-vigrahāya kṛṣṇa-kāmaika-cāriṇe
rūpānuga-pravarāya vinodeti-svarūpiṇe
content.translation: He is the shelter of love for Gaurāṅga, and his every action is solely to fulfil the desires of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. He is best among the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, and his internal identity is that of Vinoda Mañjarī.
content.wbw: gaurāśraya-vigrahāya — to him who is the shelter of love for Gaurāṅga; kṛṣṇa-kāmaika-cāriṇe — whose every action is solely to fulfil the desires of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; rūpānuga-pravarāya — who is the best among the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; vinodeti-svarūpiṇe — whose internal identity is Vinoda Mañjarī.

content.sanskrit:
prabhupādāntaraṅgāya sarva-sad-guṇa-śāline
māyāvada-tamo-ghnāya vedāntārtha-vāde namaḥ
content.translation: He is an intimate associate of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Prabhupāda, and he is endowed with all auspicious qualities. He eradicates the darkness of māyāvada and reveals the true meaning of Vedānta. I offer praṇāma to him.
content.wbw: prabhupādāntaraṅgāya — to the intimate associate of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Prabhupāda; sarva-sad-guṇa-śāline — endowed with all auspicious qualities; māyāvada-tamo-ghnāya — to the eradicator of the darkness of māyāvada; vedāntārtha-vāde — to the revealer of the true meaning of Vedānta; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
nama oṁ viṣṇu-pādāya kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhāya bhūtale
śrīmate bhaktisiddhānta-sarasvatīti-nāmine
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda, who, in this world, is most dear to Kṛṣṇa.
content.wbw: nama — obeisances; oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; viṣṇu-pādāya — to oṁ viṣṇupāda; kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhāya — who is most dear to Kṛṣṇa; bhūtale — in this world; śrīmate — to the glorious; bhaktisiddhānta-sarasvatīti-nāmine — named Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.

content.sanskrit:
śrī-vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayitāya kṛpābdhaye
kṛṣṇa-sambandha-vijñāna-dāyine prabhave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-dayita dāsa, the manifestation of an ocean of mercy, who grants realization of our eternal relationship with Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
content.wbw: śrī-vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayitāya — to Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayita dāsa; kṛpābdhaye — to the manifestation of an ocean of mercy; kṛṣṇa-sambandha-vijñāna-dāyine — who grants realization of our eternal relationship with Śrī Kṛṣṇa; prabhave — to the master; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
mādhuryojjvala-premāḍhya-śrī-rūpānuga-bhakti-da
śrī-gaura-karuṇā-śakti-vigrahāya namo 'stu te
content.translation: O Śrīla Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, you deliver śrī rūpānuga-bhakti, which is enriched with ujjvala-mādhurya-prema. You are the embodiment of the mercy potency of Śrī Gaurāṅga. I offer praṇāma unto you.
content.wbw: mādhuryojjvala-premāḍhya-śrī-rūpānuga-bhakti-da — giver of śrī rūpānuga-bhakti, enriched with ujjvala-mādhurya-prema; śrī-gaura-karuṇā-śakti-vigrahāya — to the embodiment of Śrī Gaurāṅga’s mercy potency; namo — obeisances; 'stu — may there be; te — unto you.

content.sanskrit:
namas te gaura-vāṇī-śrī-mūrtaye dīna-tāriṇe
rūpānuga-viruddhāpasiddhānta-dhvānta-hāriṇe
content.translation: I offer obeisances to you, the embodiment of Śrī Gaurāṅga's message. You deliver the fallen and remove the darkness of philosophical misconceptions that are opposed to the precepts taught by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
content.wbw: namas — obeisances; te — to you; gaura-vāṇī-śrī-mūrtaye — embodiment of Śrī Gaurāṅga's message; dīna-tāriṇe — deliverer of the fallen; rūpānuga-viruddhāpasiddhānta-dhvānta-hāriṇe — remover of the darkness of philosophical misconceptions opposed to the precepts taught by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

content.sanskrit:
namo gaura-kiśorāya sākṣād-vairāgya-mūrtaye
vipralambha-rasāmbhodhe! pādāmbujāya te namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to Śrī Gaura-kiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who is the direct embodiment of renunciation. O you who are an ocean of vipralambha-rasa, I offer praṇāma unto your lotus feet.
content.wbw: namo — praṇāma; gaura-kiśorāya — to Śrī Gaura-kiśora; sākṣād-vairāgya-mūrtaye — to the direct embodiment of renunciation; vipralambha-rasāmbhodhe — O ocean of vipralambha-rasa; pādāmbujāya — to the lotus feet; te — your; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
namo bhaktivinodāya sac-cid-ānanda-nāmine
gaura-śakti-svarūpāya rūpānuga-varāya te
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to you, Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, the foremost of rūpānugas and the personal manifestation of Śrī Gaurāṅga's śakti [Gadādhara Paṇḍita].
content.wbw: namo — obeisances, I offer praṇāma; bhaktivinodāya — to Bhaktivinoda; sac-cid-ānanda-nāmine — named Saccidānanda; gaura-śakti-svarūpāya — the personal manifestation of Śrī Gaurāṅga's śakti; rūpānuga-varāya — the foremost of rūpānugas; te — to you.

content.sanskrit:
gaurāvirbhāva-bhūmes tvaṁ nirdeṣṭā sajjana-priyaḥ
vaiṣṇava-sārvabhauma śrī-jagannāthāya te namaḥ
content.translation: You indicated the place of Śrī Gaurāṅga's appearance, and you are most dear to the saintly. O Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, leader of the Vaiṣṇavas, I offer praṇāma unto you.
content.wbw: gaurāvirbhāva-bhūmes — the place of Śrī Gaurāṅga's appearance; tvaṁ — you; nirdeṣṭā — indicated; sajjana-priyaḥ — very dear to the saintly; vaiṣṇava-sārvabhauma — O leader of the Vaiṣṇavas; śrī-jagannāthāya — unto Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja; te — unto you; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
vāñchā-kalpa-tarubhyaś ca kṛpā-sindhubhya eva ca
patitānāṁ pāvanebhyo vaiṣṇavebhyo namo namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma again and again to the Vaiṣṇavas, who are the saviors of the fallen, who are just like wish-fulfilling desire-trees and who are oceans of mercy.
content.wbw: vāñchā-kalpa-tarubhyaś — to those who are like wish-fulfilling desire-trees; ca — and; kṛpā-sindhubhya — to the oceans of mercy; eva — indeed; ca — and; patitānāṁ — of the fallen; pāvanebhyo — to the saviors; vaiṣṇavebhyo — to the Vaiṣṇavas; namo — obeisances; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
namo mahā-vadānyāya kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya te
kṛṣṇāya kṛṣṇa-caitanya-nāmne gaura-tviṣe namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to that greatly munificent Lord who bestows kṛṣṇa-prema. He is Kṛṣṇa Himself, who has assumed a golden complexion and accepted the name Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya.
content.wbw: namo — obeisances; mahā-vadānyāya — to the greatly munificent Lord; kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya — who bestows kṛṣṇa-prema; te — to You; kṛṣṇāya — to Kṛṣṇa Himself; kṛṣṇa-caitanya-nāmne — who has accepted the name Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya; gaura-tviṣe — who has assumed a golden complexion; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
he kṛṣṇa karuṇā-sindho dīna-bandho jagat-pate
gopeśa gopikā-kānta rādhā-kānta namo 'stu te
content.translation: O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, You are an ocean of mercy, the friend of the fallen, Lord of the universe, master of the cowherds, beloved of the gopīs, and [above all] the beloved of Śrī Rādhā. I offer praṇāma unto You.
content.wbw: he — O; kṛṣṇa — Śrī Kṛṣṇa; karuṇā-sindho — ocean of mercy; dīna-bandho — friend of the fallen; jagat-pate — Lord of the universe; gopeśa — master of the cowherds; gopikā-kānta — beloved of the gopīs; rādhā-kānta — beloved of Śrī Rādhā; namo — praṇāma; 'stu — may there be; te — unto You.

content.sanskrit:
tapta-kāñcana-gaurāṅgi rādhe vṛndāvaneśvari
vṛṣabhānu-sute devi praṇamāmi hari-priye
content.translation: O Śrī Rādhā, O Gaurāṅgi, whose complexion is like molten gold, You are the queen of Vṛndāvana, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, and the divine goddess, who is most dear to Śrī Hari. I offer praṇāma unto You.
content.wbw: tapta-kāñcana-gaurāṅgi — O Gaurāṅgi, whose complexion is like molten gold; rādhe — O Śrī Rādhā; vṛndāvaneśvari — O queen of Vṛndāvana; vṛṣabhānu-sute — O daughter of Vṛṣabhānu; devi — O divine goddess; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma unto You; hari-priye — O most dear to Śrī Hari.

content.sanskrit:
jayatāṁ su-ratau paṅgor mama manda-mater gatī
mat-sarvasva padāmbhojau rādhā-madana-mohanau
content.translation: All glories to the supremely merciful Śrī Rādhā-Madana-mohana! Although I am lame and foolish, They are my sole refuge. Their lotus feet are everything to me.
content.wbw: jayatāṁ — all glories to; su-ratau — the supremely merciful Ones; paṅgor — of the lame; mama — my; manda-mater — of the foolish; gatī — refuge; mat-sarvasva — my everything; padāmbhojau — lotus feet; rādhā-madana-mohanau — Śrī Rādhā-Madana-mohana.

content.sanskrit:
dīvyad-vṛndāraṇya-kalpa-drumādhaḥ
śrīmad-ratnāgāra-siṁhāsana-sthau
śrīmad-rādhā-śrīla-govinda-devau
preṣṭhālībhiḥ sevyamānau smarāmi
content.translation: In the shining land of Śrī Vṛndāvana, in a temple composed of jewels, Śrī Rādhā-Govinda are seated on an effulgent throne beneath a kalpa-vṛkṣa tree, accepting service from Their beloved sakhīs. I meditate upon Them.
content.wbw: dīvyad-vṛndāraṇya-kalpa-drumādhaḥ — beneath a kalpa-vṛkṣa tree in shining Śrī Vṛndāvana; śrīmad-ratnāgāra-siṁhāsana-sthau — seated on an effulgent throne in a temple composed of jewels; śrīmad-rādhā-śrīla-govinda-devau — Śrī Rādhā and Śrīla Govinda-deva; preṣṭhālībhiḥ — by Their beloved sakhīs; sevyamānau — being served; smarāmi — I meditate upon.

content.sanskrit:
śrīmān rāsa-rasārambhī vaṁśīvaṭa-taṭa-sthitaḥ
karṣan veṇu-svanair gopīr gopīnāthaḥ śriye 'stu naḥ
content.translation: Standing on the river-bank at Vaṁśīvaṭa, Śrī Gopīnātha, the initiator of the transcendental mellow of the rāsa-dance, attracts all the gopīs with the sound of His veṇu flute. May He confer auspiciousness upon us.
content.wbw: śrīmān — glorious Śrī; rāsa-rasārambhī — the initiator of the transcendental mellow of the rāsa-dance; vaṁśīvaṭa-taṭa-sthitaḥ — standing on the river-bank at Vaṁśīvaṭa; karṣan — attracting; veṇu-svanair — with the sound of His veṇu flute; gopīr — all the gopīs; gopīnāthaḥ — Śrī Gopīnātha, Lord of the gopīs; śriye — auspiciousness; 'stu — may He confer; naḥ — upon us.

content.sanskrit:
vṛndāyai tulasī-devyai priyāyai keśavasya ca
kṛṣṇa-bhakti-prade devi! satyavatyai namo namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma again and again to Śrīmatī Tulasī-devī, who is most dear to Śrī Keśava and who is also renowned as Vṛndā-devī and Satyavatī. O Devī, you bestow kṛṣṇa-bhakti.
content.wbw: vṛndāyai — to Vṛndā-devī; tulasī-devyai — to Śrīmatī Tulasī-devī; priyāyai — who is most dear; keśavasya — to Śrī Keśava; ca — and; kṛṣṇa-bhakti-prade — who bestows kṛṣṇa-bhakti; devi — O Devī; satyavatyai — to Satyavatī; namo — praṇāma; namaḥ — obeisances again and again.

content.sanskrit:
pañca-tattvātmakaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ bhakta-rūpa-svarūpakam
bhaktāvatāraṁ bhaktākhyaṁ namāmi bhakta-śaktikam
content.translation: I offer praṇāma unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu in His five features as bhakta-rūpa (Mahāprabhu), bhakta-svarūpa (Nityānanda Prabhu), bhakta-avatāra (Advaita Ācārya), bhakta (Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura) and bhakta-śakti (Gadādhara Paṇḍita).
content.wbw: pañca-tattvātmakaṁ — manifest in five features; kṛṣṇaṁ — Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu; bhakta-rūpa-svarūpakam — as bhakta-rūpa and bhakta-svarūpa; bhaktāvatāraṁ — as bhakta-avatāra; bhaktākhyaṁ — known as bhakta; namāmi — I offer praṇāma; bhakta-śaktikam — as bhakta-śakti.

content.sanskrit:
śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya prabhu-nityānanda
śrī-advaita gadādhara śrīvāsādi-gaura-bhakta-vṛnda

hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare
hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare

arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīr guruṣu nara-matir vaiṣṇave jāti-buddhir
viṣṇor vā vaiṣṇavānāṁ kali-mala-mathane pāda-tīrthe 'mbu-buddhiḥ
śrī-viṣṇor nāmni mantre sakala-kaluṣa-he śabda-sāmānya-buddhir
viṣṇau sarveśvareśe tad-itara-sama-dhīr yasya vā nārakī saḥ
content.translation: One who thinks the Deity in the temple to be made of wood or stone, who thinks of the spiritual master in the disciplic succession as an ordinary man, who thinks the Vaiṣṇava in the Acyuta-gotra to belong to a certain caste or creed or who thinks of caraṇāmṛta or Ganges water as ordinary water is taken to be a resident of hell. (Padma Purāṇa)
content.wbw: arcye — in the Deity; viṣṇau — Lord Viṣṇu; śilā-dhīr — the conception of it as stone; guruṣu — in the spiritual masters; nara-matir — the conception of them as ordinary men; vaiṣṇave — in a Vaiṣṇava; jāti-buddhir — the conception of him as belonging to a caste or creed; viṣṇor — of Viṣṇu; vā — or; vaiṣṇavānāṁ — of the Vaiṣṇavas; kali-mala-mathane — in that which destroys the contamination of Kali; pāda-tīrthe — in the water that has washed the feet, caraṇāmṛta; 'mbu-buddhiḥ — the conception of it as ordinary water; śrī-viṣṇor — of Śrī Viṣṇu; nāmni — in the holy name; mantre — in the mantra; sakala-kaluṣa-he — which destroys all contamination; śabda-sāmānya-buddhir — the conception of it as an ordinary sound; viṣṇau — in Lord Viṣṇu; sarveśvareśe — the Lord of all lords; tad-itara-sama-dhīr — whose conception is that He is equal to anything else; yasya — of whom; vā — or; nārakī — a resident of hell; saḥ — he is.

sections.title: The Emblem of the Gauḍīya Maṭha
sections.subtitle: vidhiḥ — rāgaḥ

content.content:
This chapter draws on Gurudev's lecture “Gaudiya Math Logo — the Essence of Mahāprabhu's Vichar-Dhara” (no. 7894, 15 August 2024)
and on lecture no. 1480 (1 September 2016)

On the cover of this book is the emblem of the Gauḍīya Maṭha. It was personally designed by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda, who expressed in its form a profound understanding of siddhānta—what Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu gave. The emblem opens this book on Deity worship because it shows the place of arcana within the entire sādhana of a Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava: on the left is the path of ⟦vidhi⟧, the path of rules and arcana; on the right is the path of ⟦rāga⟧, the path of spontaneous love; in the centre is the holy name; at the top is Mahāprabhu; and at the bottom is Guru.

First, it is worth simply examining what is depicted here, what each detail points to and what it recalls, and then entering more deeply into the topics themselves. Click on an item in the list to highlight that element in the illustration.

⟦oṁ — nāma⟧: the holy name in the Gopāla-yantra
Bhagavān’s six opulences at the points of the yantra
⟦yaśaḥ⟧ — fame
⟦śrīḥ⟧ — beauty
⟦jñānam⟧ — knowledge
⟦vairāgyam⟧ — renunciation
⟦aiśvaryam⟧ — majesty
⟦vīryam⟧ — strength
the book Pāñcarātra
the book Bhāgavatam
⟦vidhiḥ⟧ — the path of rules and prescriptions
⟦rāgaḥ⟧ — the path of rāga
⟦arcanam⟧: incense, dīpa, bell
⟦kīrtanam⟧: printing press and mṛdaṅga
tilaka and the inscription ⟦guruḥ gauḍīyaḥ⟧
⟦Śrī Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu⟧
⟦Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧
⟦Śrī Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa⟧

⟦Maṭha⟧ is a place where disciples live to study transcendental spiritual science; the Gauḍīya Maṭha is a place where the science revealed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is studied. The word “Gauḍīya” can easily be taken to refer to a region in Bengal, but this is merely a material, geographical understanding, limited by time and space. ⟦Gauḍa⟧ is natural, genuine sweetness, and the natural sweetness of the love of the gopīs of Vṛndāvana is the goal and purpose of the Gauḍīyas. One of Śrīmatī Rādhikā’s names is Gaurī; the Gauḍīyas are those under Her protection.
How, then, can this highest goal—shelter in the service of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa—be attained? Under the guidance of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī in his Vraja-svarūpa. This is the purpose of the Gauḍīya Maṭha.

subsections.title: The Holy Name and the Six Opulences

content.content: At the very centre of the emblem is written “Oṁ”, and beneath it, “nāma” (1). Oṁ is the holy name. The ṛṣis of the Ṛg-veda pray:

content.sanskrit:
oṁ āsya jānanto nāma cid viviktana
mahas te viṣṇo sumatiṁ bhajāmahe
oṁ tat sat
content.translation: “O Lord, we do not know You fully: we know that You exist, but we are not completely acquainted with You. Yet how wonderful it is: simply by chanting the syllables of Your name, we shall attain a perfectly clear and beautiful realization.”

content.content: Why is this so? Because ⟦oṁ tat sat⟧: Oṁ is the holy name, ⟦tat⟧ is the Absolute Truth, and ⟦sat⟧ means that the name is ⟦svataḥ-siddha⟧, self-existent, and ⟦svayaṁ-prakāśa⟧, self-manifesting. It is impossible to comprehend ⟦aprākṛta-vastu⟧, transcendental reality, by one’s own efforts; but to one who serves the holy name by chanting its syllables, the name reveals Itself.

The holy name is placed within the Gopāla-yantra—a six-pointed star (2). At its six points, beginning at the top and proceeding clockwise, are written Bhagavān’s six opulences: ⟦yaśaḥ⟧—fame (2.1), ⟦śrīḥ⟧—beauty (2.2), ⟦jñānam⟧—knowledge (2.3), ⟦vairāgyam⟧—renunciation (2.4), ⟦aiśvaryam⟧—majesty, the ability to be both the greatest and the smallest (2.5), and ⟦vīryam⟧—strength: He is ⟦sarva-śaktimān⟧, almighty (2.6). The Gopāla-yantra corresponds to the Gopāla-mantra and reminds us that the Gopāla-mantra reveals six kinds of ⟦svarūpa-jñāna⟧.

Above the holy name is Śrī Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu: Kṛṣṇa Himself, who distributes kṛṣṇa-prema through the holy name in the age of Kali. Opposite Him, in the lower part of the emblem, is Guru: Nityānanda Prabhu and the spiritual master, ⟦guru-tattva⟧. A tilaka mark is depicted there, with ⟦guruḥ gauḍīyaḥ⟧ written beneath it (9).

subsections.title: Two books and two paths: vidhi and rāga

content.content: On closer examination, the parts of the emblem form a shape resembling the letter X. At the top, on either side of Mahāprabhu, are two śāstras, two books. The one on the left is labelled “Pāñcarātra” (3), and the one on the right, “Bhāgavatam” (4). These are the scriptures on which the two paths are based: the path of arcana, ⟦vaidhī-bhakti⟧, and ⟦bhāva-mārga⟧, the path of ecstatic mood, ⟦rāgānugā-bhakti⟧.

Below, on the same level as one another, are the Deities. On the left, on the Pāñcarātra side, are Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa in Vaikuṇṭha, and beneath Them is written ⟦vidhiḥ⟧ (5): bhakti expressed according to the rules and prescriptions of the scriptures. On the right, on the Bhāgavatam side, are Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa beneath a desire tree in Vṛndāvana, and beneath Them is written ⟦rāgaḥ⟧ (6).

At the bottom left, on the Pāñcarātra side, are articles for arcana—a bell and a dīpa—and the inscription ⟦arcanam⟧ (7). On the right, on the path of rāga, the path of ⟦bhāgavata-mārga⟧, is written ⟦kīrtanam⟧; there are a mṛdaṅga and a printing press as it was in the 1920s—a “printing yantra”, a machine for printing books (8).

An example of perfection through kīrtana is Śukadeva Gosvāmī. Rather than singing, he spoke Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam—all day and all night, continuously, for seven days. When kīrtana comes from the lips of such pure devotees, it can be recorded, printed and distributed everywhere. Therefore Śrīla Prabhupāda called the printing press ⟦bṛhat-mṛdaṅga⟧, the great mṛdaṅga: its sound spreads throughout the world.
The essence of the entire emblem is expressed in a verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (11.21.2):

content.sanskrit:
sve sve 'dhikāre yā niṣṭhā
sa guṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
viparyayas tu doṣaḥ syād
ubhayor eṣa niścayaḥ
content.translation: Steadiness at one’s own level of qualification is called a virtue; the opposite is a fault. Thus both are defined.

content.content: The measure of a person’s virtues and faults is ⟦niṣṭhā⟧: how steadily one follows one’s ⟦adhikāra⟧ and the practice appropriate to one’s level. If someone who began with a practice meant for absolute beginners is still doing exactly the same thing many years later, this is a fault. And if a person at the beginning of bhakti attempts to practise as someone who has attained a very high level practises, this is also a fault.

One person practises at a beginner’s level, another at an advanced level, and one cannot say that one is better than the other: it is better when each practises at their own level. Therefore, the best path is not the same for everyone, and the guidance of a spiritual master is necessary so that, following ⟦ānugatya⟧, one can practise bhakti according to one’s stage and, when ready, rise higher, step by step. These principles are embodied in Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura’s design.

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explained that the Vedic scriptures mention various ⟦hari-jana⟧, “people of God”—Sātvatas, Vaikhānasas, Bhāgavatas, Vaiṣṇavas, Pāñcarātrikas and others. Many of these groups gradually disappeared, and by Kali-yuga essentially two traditions remained: the Pāñcarātrikas and the Bhāgavatas. ⟦Pāñcarātrika-mārga⟧ is the same as ⟦arcana-mārga⟧, Deity worship according to rules and prescriptions, vaidhī-bhakti. The Bhāgavata tradition is the school of ⟦bhāva-mārga⟧, the path of spiritual feeling, rāgānugā-bhakti.

Of the four present-day sampradāyas, Madhvācārya (Brahma-sampradāya) and Nimbāditya (the sampradāya of the four Kumāras) primarily gave bhāgavata-mārga, while accepting the path of arcana for beginners, ⟦kaniṣṭha-adhikārī⟧. Rāmānujācārya (Śrī-sampradāya, which worships Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa) and Viṣṇusvāmī (Rudra-sampradāya, whose iṣṭadeva is Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṁha) taught pāñcarātrika-mārga and accepted kīrtana as part of the rituals of arcana.

This gives rise to much confusion: many do not distinguish between the two paths and do not see how arcana supports beginners on bhāgavata-mārga. This is partly a matter of terminology. “Bhāgavata” means “related to Bhagavān”, so both vaidhī-bhakti and rāgānugā-bhakti are called ⟦bhāgavata-dharma⟧, and great devotees of both paths are called bhāgavatas or mahā-bhāgavatas. Even the three levels of devotees—kaniṣṭha, madhyama and uttama—are described in both Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and the Padma Purāṇa, but these descriptions do not coincide: the Padma Purāṇa speaks in the context of the pāñcarātrika tradition, and the Bhāgavatam in the context of the bhāgavata tradition.

On the pāñcarātrika-mārga, some rely on varṇāśrama-dharma, karma, and jñāna. On the bhāgavata-mārga, a person may perform certain activities related to karma, but without faith in them—and bhakti remains ⟦anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyaṁ jñāna-karmādy-anāvṛtam⟧, free from extraneous desires and not covered by jñāna and karma.

In the time of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura—and to some extent even today—caste-minded smārta-brāhmaṇas asserted: only a brāhmaṇa can be a guru and ācārya, and my son will be the next ācārya; as soon as he is born, he will receive the titles “Prabhupāda” and “Gosvāmī.” In this way, the values of worldly varṇāśrama-dharma were imposed on rāgānugā-bhakti.

The understanding of smaraṇa also became confused. Arcana, too, includes remembrance: before worshipping Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, one recites meditation mantras—⟦tato vṛndāvanaṁ dhyāyet⟧—and envisions Vṛndāvana, the waters of the Yamunā, a gentle breeze, and a golden throne beneath a wish-fulfilling tree. But this smaraṇa is performed because śāstra says, “Now remember this,” and the mind keeps track of which mantra comes next. The intelligence still depends on śāstra and ⟦buddhi⟧—this is not a sign of awakened longing, ⟦lobha⟧. Smaraṇa on the rāga-mārga, as described by the six Gosvāmīs, is something entirely different.

All of this—the pāñcarātrika system, varṇāśrama-dharma, and rāgānugā-bhakti—was mixed into something that made it convenient to collect money. “Only we, brāhmaṇas by hereditary lineage, can be gurus,” some said, and then gave siddha-praṇālī: your name is such-and-such, your form is such-and-such, your age, the colour of your clothing, your service in the kuñja—now go and remember this. This understanding of smaraṇa belongs to arcana, where there is a mantra but no realization; in the Bhāgavata school, which rests primarily on realization, there is no such practice.

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura did not approve of this. Those who give siddha-praṇālī as a form of pāñcarātrika-dīkṣā, and moreover initiate people for money, he called mantra merchants: they stand alongside the potters and cobblers in the marketplace. To clarify all this and remind people, he created the emblem; it was present in every Gauḍīya Maṭha—and it is no wonder that many tried to kill him.

subsections.title: Arcana on the Path of Rāga

content.content: For those who worship Kṛṣṇa through vaidhī-bhakti, the scriptures prescribe ⟦āvaraṇa-pūjā⟧: the Lord is worshipped not alone, but together with the circles of His associates—the cowherd boys, the queens of Dvārakā, Vasudeva and Devakī, Nanda and Yaśodā, the gopīs, the wish-fulfilling trees, the guardians of the directions, and even the Lord’s weapons (Hari-bhakti-vilāsa 7.362–375). This is how pūjā to Kṛṣṇa is actually performed on the pāñcarātrika-vaidhī-mārga. For beginners on the rāga-mārga, the ācāryas established a somewhat modified procedure for arcana: although the neophyte has not yet reached the level of rāgānugā-bhakti sādhana and remains on the platform of vaidhī, his worship is arranged so that everything will be favourable for him when he rises higher.

Therefore, in Rāga-vartma-candrikā, Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura says that those following the path of rāga should not perform ⟦ahaṅgrahopāsanā⟧, imagining themselves to be identical with the Deity, or ⟦nyāsa⟧, although both are found in the scriptures; on this path, one does not meditate on the moods of Dvārakā or perform pūjā to Rukmiṇī and the other queens. Vaidhī-bhakti leads to Vaikuṇṭha; only rāgānugā-bhakti leads to Vraja. Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are served only through rāgānugā-bhakti; therefore, when arcana is performed for the Deities of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, this sevā is accepted by Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, who reside within Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa.

And yet the emblem shows not only the distinction but also the connection between the two paths: we follow the bhāgavata-mārga, while accepting the help of the pāñcarātrika-mārga in the beginning. From the very outset there is ⟦nityaṁ bhāgavata-sevayā⟧, service to the book Bhāgavata and the person Bhāgavata. But people are prone to ⟦kādarya-śīla⟧, unvirtuous behaviour, and ⟦vikṣipta-citta⟧, a distracted mind—so pāñcarātrika-dīkṣā helps in the beginning. When one’s conduct becomes good and the mind steady, the ⟦svarūpa⟧ of bhakti manifests in the pure heart.

The way from vidhi to rāga is a way of ripening: to hear hari-kathā patiently and with the greatest honour, gradually to increase the chanting to one lakh of names, sixty-four rounds a day, and to enter rāgānugā-bhakti on the basis of internal realization, not speculation. This requires patience and humility. As Gurudev says: “If you try to jump by force up to grab the fruit from the tree, then there'll be the ruination.” But to one who humbly reaches down, the fruit comes into his hand by itself.

Thus the emblem brings us back to the verse ⟦sve sve 'dhikāre yā niṣṭhā⟧: a devotee’s true merit lies in steadfastness at his own level, from which he will naturally rise higher; acting beyond one’s qualification is a fault.

Over the years, the profound conceptions of the great ācāryas, ⟦gambhīra-bhāva⟧, became mixed together like khichri. Fortunately, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda came into this world and very carefully untangled this knot, so that we could understand pure bhakti as Mahāprabhu and Rūpa Gosvāmī gave it—not ⟦viddha-gauḍīya⟧, the distorted Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavism that remains so popular today. He said that there are Gauḍīyas, agauḍīyas, and viddha-gauḍīyas: agauḍīyas do not even call themselves Gauḍīyas, whereas viddha-gauḍīyas sincerely consider themselves Gauḍīyas, but their entire understanding is riddled with misconceptions.

Gurudev says: “It is not so easy for the general person to enter deeply into the vicāra, the profound conception of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura. But that conception is the same as the conception of Mahāprabhu and Rūpa Gosvāmī and all the great ācāryas.” It was to embody this conception that Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura made the emblem.

Sarasvatī means ⟦sa-rasa⟧, full of rasa; he was like an embodiment of the goddess of knowledge in all ⟦bhakti-siddhānta⟧, the conclusions of pure bhakti, and he came to bestow pure Gauḍīya-darśana. Therefore, every morning before maṅgala-ārati, his glories are sung in Prabhupāda-padāṣṭaka. In our time, it is very difficult to approach pure bhakti without studying his explanations.

content.quote: And today we want to discuss the glories of vigraha-tattva, the glories of the deity. Caitanya Mahāprabhu has taught the glories of the deity by His own life and example.

content.content: This chapter was written at Gurudev's request: he wanted the book on arcana to include the truth about the Deity — ⟦vigraha-tattva⟧. It is based on his lecture “Vigraha-tattva,” given on the second day of the Puruṣottama-māsa festival in Durham (North Carolina, USA) on May 23, 2026 (lecture no. 10183). The chapter follows Gurudev's line of thought; his words are quoted verbatim in “Gurudev's Mood” in each section.

Mahāprabhu Himself demonstrated the glory of the Deity through His own life: “I shall accept the mood of a devotee and, by My own example, teach everyone bhakti” (Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi 3.20). One cannot teach without practising oneself — this is what the Bhagavad-gītā and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam teach (ibid., 3.21).

subsections.title: The Deity Is Not an Idol

content.quote: So, what is arcā-vigraha, the deity? The deity is not called an idol because idolatry means to imagine some speculation of what God is like and then to carve an image and worship that and think that it's God or think that it represents, it's a symbol of something higher. So all of these people have these different ideas, but none of these ideas are correct in regard to the vigraha. So we want to discuss this. The word vigraha means vi means viśeṣa and graha means grahaṇa, to accept. So vigraha, the form of the Supreme Lord who appears in this world, especially to accept our loving services is called vigraha. So in Caitanya-caritāmṛta it is said,

more.quote: There's a famous deity. You know Him? Gopāla, Śrī Gopāla, or He's famous now all over the world as Śrīnāthajī. So, He had been established by the great grandson of Krishna, Vajranābha, thousands of years ago, 5,000 years ago. But He was lost for a very long time. And after many years, about 500 years ago, He came in the dream of Mādhavendra Purī and said, "Oh, I am in the jungle here. I've been lost. I'm buried in the jungle here. Please come and take me out." And he woke up and went there with so many villagers and they cut away and they discovered (..) the deity of Gopāla, Krishna, in this pose, lifting Girirāja Govardhana. So Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī says, "jāra prema (..) preme vaśya haya," why did He appear? Because He was prema-vaśa, controlled by the love of Mādhavendra Purī. So the deity only appears in this world because Śrī Krishna is controlled by the love of His devotee.

content.content: Someone entering a temple for the first time sees “statues” and may think this is primitive idol worship. But service to the Deity is one of the aṅgas of transcendental bhakti and a profound science. Idol worship means imagining what God is like, carving an image, and considering it God or a symbol of something higher. None of these ideas applies to the vigraha (lecture no. 10183).
The word ⟦vigraha⟧: ⟦vi⟧ means ⟦viśeṣa⟧, especially; ⟦graha⟧ means ⟦grahaṇa⟧, to accept. The vigraha is the form of the Lord that appears in this world especially to accept our loving service.

content.sanskrit:
yāṅra preme vaśa hañā prakaṭa ha-ilā
sevā aṅgīkāra kari’ jagata tārilā
content.translation: Subdued by his love, He appeared and, accepting service, delivered the world (Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya 4.173 — about Gopāla, who appeared to Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī).

content.content: Gopāla, Śrīnāthajī, was installed by Kṛṣṇa's great-grandson Vajranābha five thousand years ago; the Deity was lost, and about five hundred years ago He appeared in a dream to Mādhavendra Purī: “I am here, in the jungle — dig Me out.” Why did He appear? ⟦Prema-vaśa⟧ — subdued by Mādhavendra Purī's love. The Deity comes into this world only because Kṛṣṇa is subdued by His devotee's love. Similarly, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī saw Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in a dream — Kṛṣṇa bound by the ropes of Rādhā's love — carved Dāmodara with his own hands, and gave Him to Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī; Rādhā-Dāmodara is still in Vṛndāvana today, in Sevā-kuñja (lecture no. 10183).

content.quote: And so, what is vigraha? The deity is not stone. The deity is not wood or metal. But rather, the sat-cit-ānanda-vigraha, the eternal, conscious, blissful form of the Supreme Lord.

more.quote: And then those devotees, (..) dīkṣā, initiation. They give initiation. And then engage the conditioned souls, those who are in the illusion of this world, those souls who are lost in bodily identification, but who are approaching, they want to surrender to God. He gives dīkṣā. And by that dīkṣā, they become connected to the deity. So, this is why no one can engage in the service of the deity without dīkṣā. We'll discuss this in more detail later, but without dīkṣā, it's not possible. Because there is no difference between the vigraha in the heart of the pure devotee and the vigraha he manifests outside and the vigraha which is (..) the adhiṣṭhātrī-devatā of the mantra given by guru. So, guru gives that same deity through mantra into the heart of the disciple. And when the disciple is remembering his dīkṣā mantra every day, then he'll look and see the deity of his mantra is there on the altar and can directly serve Him with all senses. So, the vigraha appears in this world to engage us in His service so that we can attain pure bhakti. Pure devotion, transcendental love.

content.content: The Deity is not stone, wood, or metal, but ⟦sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha⟧, the eternal, conscious, blissful form of the Lord:

content.sanskrit:
īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ
anādir ādir govindaḥ sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam
content.translation: The Supreme Lord is Kṛṣṇa; His form is eternity, knowledge, and bliss. He has no beginning, but He Himself is the beginning of everything; He is Govinda, the cause of all causes (Brahma-saṁhitā 5.1).

content.content: God “hides”: He is shy and does not play with the proud and selfish — only with those who are humble and full of love. When a devotee's heart is full of pure, selfless love, Kṛṣṇa can no longer hide:

content.sanskrit:
premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena
santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti
yaṁ śyāmasundaram acintya-guṇa-svarūpaṁ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
content.translation: I worship Govinda, the original Lord, Śyāmasundara, whose qualities are inconceivable, whom pure devotees always see in their hearts with eyes of devotion anointed with the balm of love (Brahma-saṁhitā 5.38).

content.content: Then, out of kindness to everyone, the pure devotee manifests the vigraha from his heart externally so that everyone can receive darśana: the treasure of his heart, ⟦prāṇa-dhana⟧, comes forth in the form of the Deity. He then gives dīkṣā, and through it conditioned souls become connected with the Deity. Therefore, no one can serve the Deity without dīkṣā: there is no difference between the vigraha in the pure devotee's heart, the vigraha he has manifested externally, and the Deity of the mantra given by the guru. Remembering the dīkṣā mantra, the disciple sees the Deity of his mantra on the altar and can serve Him with all his senses (lecture no. 10183).

subsections.title: The Fourth Form — Accessible to Us

content.quote: So, we can know that Paramātmā is there, but still in our condition state, we cannot hear Him. We cannot see Him. We cannot interact with Him. So, God in the spiritual world is merciful. His avatāras are merciful, and Paramātmā in the heart, these three svarūpas, they are all there, and they're merciful, but they're not accessible to us. Therefore, the Lord appears in the fourth form, that is, arcā-vigraha. The deity. How kind. The deity appears in this world in such a way that we can interact with Him using the resources which are even available to us in our conditioned state. So we should know that in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, there it is said,

more.quote: In Kūrma Purāṇa, it is said, for the ordinary person, there's a difference between the body and the embodied, the soul and the body. But for God, there's no difference. God's body is His soul. So God does not have a body in the same way that we have a body. Tat-pradhānatvāt means tad, that form of God, he pradhāna, is prominent. In other words, He does not have a form, He is His form. His form is not a possession which is different from Himself. He is His spiritual form. And so, the vigraha is not a form of God or a form that God has, but it is directly Krishna Himself and we can He's accessible.

content.content: At every moment, our knowledge — everything conveyed by our eyes, ears, tongue, and skin — is given by Paramātmā in the heart (Bhagavad-gītā 15.15); we depend entirely on Him. But in our conditioned state we neither see nor hear Him. God in the spiritual world, His avatāras, and Paramātmā are merciful, but inaccessible to us. Therefore, the Lord appears in a fourth form — ⟦arcā-vigraha⟧, the Deity — in such a way that we can interact with Him through the means available to us even in our conditioned state (lecture no. 10183).

content.sanskrit: pratimā naha tumi — sākṣāt vrajendra-nandana
content.translation: “You are not a statue — You are the son of the king of Vraja Himself” (Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya 5.96).

content.content: This is what the young brāhmaṇa said to the Deity when he asked Kṛṣṇa to witness a promise; and Kṛṣṇa, subdued by his love, followed him — the brāhmaṇa heard the jingling of His bells behind him (Sākṣī-gopāla). Anyone who judges the vigraha through material senses will fall into error and fail to understand His mercy; a connection with the Deity is established through hearing and dīkṣā. The Padma Purāṇa warns: one who considers the Deity to be stone and the guru to be an ordinary person is on the path to hell (⟦arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīr guruṣu nara-matir…⟧).

The Vedas say that God has no form (⟦arūpavad eva hi tat-pradhānatvāt⟧, Vedānta-sūtra 3.2.14). The meaning is not simple: our soul and body are different, whereas God's form and He Himself are one (⟦deha-dehi-vibhāgo 'yaṁ neśvare vidyate kvacit⟧). He does not “have” a form — He is His spiritual form. Therefore, the vigraha is not “a form of God,” but Kṛṣṇa Himself, accessible for service (lecture no. 10183).

content.quote: We can easily approach Him and serve Him. Even if a person is poor, they may think, but I cannot offer so many opulent things. I don't have hundreds of flowers to offer (..) many garlands every day. I don't have so many gold and jeweled ornaments. But vigraha is so kind. Even if you'll serve the vigraha in your mind. You may only have some simple rice and dal. But when you offer it, it's free. You can think, I am offering Krishna the rasagullas and gulābjāmuns and pakorās and so many. (..) If you can afford to make them all yourself, you should do this. If you don't, then it becomes aparādha, the fault of miserliness. If a person has the facility but they don't use their wealth in the service of the deity, becomes aparādha, the fault of miserliness. But if a person is a virakta, very poor, simple sādhu, renounced person, then they may offer simple things. Krishna said,

content.content: Everyone can serve the Deity. Those who have the means should offer the best; otherwise, their stinginess is an offence. A simple, poor sādhu, however, may offer something simple: “If someone offers Me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water with devotion, I accept it” (Bhagavad-gītā 9.26). In the mind, one can offer Kṛṣṇa everything — even His kaustubha jewel, more precious than cintāmaṇi; the Deity is so merciful that He will accept this too (lecture no. 10183).

subsections.title: The Full Taste: Service with All the Senses

content.quote: So, it is only when the sarvottama-vastu, when the highest reality is the mādhurya, the sweetness of the highest reality is relished through all three types of senses, antaḥkaraṇa, jñānendriya and karmendriya, that the āsvādana, that means tasting is pūrṇa. you see? So, there is a pūrṇa-āsvādanam.

content.content: Bhakti is ⟦rāja-vidyā, rāja-guhyam⟧ (Bhagavad-gītā 9.2): only through it can ⟦sarvottama-vastu⟧, the highest reality, be understood. Knowledge of God is not gathered piece by piece, as at a university, but is ⟦advaya-jñāna⟧: everything comes from God, everything is in God, and God is everything (⟦abhinna-nimittopādāna⟧, like a spider spinning a web from itself). Kṛṣṇa instructed Brahmā to know His ⟦svarūpa⟧ together with ⟦vijñāna⟧ — how He interacts with His energies, His devotees, in His own world; the realization of this sweetness is ⟦mādhurya-anubhava⟧ (lecture no. 10183).

We have three levels of senses: ⟦antaḥkaraṇa⟧ — the inner sense (the mind, ⟦manas⟧, intelligence, ⟦buddhi⟧, false ego, ⟦ahaṅkāra⟧, and ⟦citta⟧); the five knowledge-acquiring senses, ⟦jñānendriya⟧; and the five working senses, ⟦karmendriya⟧. The taste of the highest reality is complete — ⟦pūrṇāsvādana⟧, ⟦pūrṇāmṛtāsvādanam⟧ (Śikṣāṣṭaka 1) — only when all three levels of senses taste its sweetness; and only then does a strong desire to serve, ⟦sevā-abhilāṣa⟧, manifest. This is precisely what service to the Deity gives us (lecture no. 10183).

subsections.title: “Nādevo devam arcayet”: Why Dīkṣā Is Needed

content.quote: So all those who have received dīkṣā from a sad-guru, and they those who are sat-śiṣya, real disciples who have received dīkṣā from sad-guru, real guru, they have transcendental bodies in which they serve the Supreme Lord and they have the pūrṇa-āsvādana, (..) pūrṇa-mādhurya-āsvādana, the full taste of the sweetness of the supreme truth by serving the vigraha and by chanting Harināma. So, something to note here, which is so important. Śrī Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, he said,

more.quote: Now, just as it said, alakṣita, (..) that spiritual form of the devotee is invisible to others. It may be, it depends on the level of the advancement of the devotee. But when you receive initiation, it's even invisible to you. It's invisible to you also. But what happens is, as you begin to use these mind and senses in the service of the deity, the more your eyes behold the deity, the more your hands are decorating, bathing, massaging, cooking, and serving the deity in all ways, and your tongue is chanting, your ears are hearing harikathā, then to that degree we become absorbed in bhakti, then that invisible spiritual body becomes awakened and we become aware of it. And it is only through those transcendental senses that one can actually experience the sweetness of the holy name. Only through those transcendental senses, one can experience the sweetness of the deity of Rādhā and Krishna, not by material senses. So

content.content: The śāstra says: ⟦nādevo devam arcayet⟧ — one who has not become divine cannot serve the Divine. The vigraha is sac-cid-ānanda, whereas our senses are material. How, then, can the material serve the transcendental? Mahāprabhu said to Haridāsa Ṭhākura, who was born in a Muslim family: “Your body is dearer to Me than My own; we belong to the same caste,” because both were sac-cid-ānanda. Only one who has risen to the transcendental level can serve the transcendental Lord—and this is attained through dīkṣā (lecture no. 10183).

content.sanskrit:
dīkṣā-kāle bhakta kare ātma-samarpaṇa
sei-kāle kṛṣṇa tāre kare ātma-sama
sei deha kare tāra cid-ānanda-maya
aprākṛta-dehe tāṅra caraṇa bhajaya
content.translation: At the time of dīkṣā, the devotee offers himself to Kṛṣṇa, and at that very moment Kṛṣṇa accepts him as His own. He makes the devotee’s body spiritual and full of bliss, and in this indisputable body the devotee serves His feet (Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Antya 4.192–193; Mahāprabhu’s words to Sanātana Gosvāmī).

content.content: Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains that, according to the logic of the touchstone, ⟦sparśa-maṇi-nyāya⟧, the body, mind, and senses become ⟦aprākṛta⟧ through contact with bhakti. At the moment one receives instruction in the mantra, by the inconceivable power of the Lord, the devotee is given a body, mind, senses, and prāṇa beyond the guṇas—⟦alakṣita⟧, invisibly to others. The physical body itself does not become sac-cid-ānanda: the Lord invisibly gives a spiritual body within it, and the surrendered devotee’s prārabdha-karma is neutralized in such a way that the physical body does not obstruct the spiritual one (lecture no. 10183).

At first, this spiritual body is invisible even to the devotee himself. But the more the eyes look at the Deity, the hands decorate, bathe, prepare offerings for, and serve Him, the tongue chants, and the ears listen to hari-kathā, the more it awakens. The sweetness of the holy name and of the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Deity can be perceived only by these transcendental senses (⟦ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmādi na bhaved grāhyam indriyaiḥ⟧). Therefore bhakti is ⟦rāja-guhya⟧: it is concealed, invisible even to us ourselves, until we immerse ourselves more deeply (lecture no. 10183).

subsections.title: Not a symbol, not the universe, not “I am Brahman”

content.quote: Then the second type of path which is done by the jñānīs who have an impersonal knowledge, (..) they want impersonal knowledge, that is called pratīkopāsanā. So pratīka is the idea that if you're worshiping something with a form, then (..) you should do this because that is just like a technique to control your mind. Because it's very difficult to concentrate on the emptiness, on empty light. So let me have a statue or a maṇḍala or something, some crystals or something like that. Or I can worship the sun, or the earth, or the fire, or water, or (..) air, space, is everywhere. It's big. So people accept something to be a pratīka, that's a representative of God, and they try to focus their mind on that. So, this will also not give any ānanda, any joy, because all of these things that they're meditating, they are inert and limited material objects. So there'll be no the mādhurya-āsvādana at all, what to speak of a pūrṇa-mādhurya-anubhava. It's impossible. So, we don't worship pratīka, a symbol. And it should be understood in Vedānta-sūtra it is said,

content.content: Impersonalists have three forms of worship, and none of them gives sweetness (lecture no. 10183):

⟦ahaṅgrahopāsanā⟧ — “I am Brahman”: worshiping oneself as infinite light. To taste sugar, one cannot become sugar; for pure devotees, such liberation is like hell (⟦kaivalyaṁ narakāyate⟧).
⟦pratīkopāsanā⟧ — worshiping a symbol as a means of concentration: a statue, maṇḍala, the sun, or fire. These objects are inert and limited—there is no sweetness. The Deity is not ⟦pratīka⟧: ⟦na pratīke na hi saḥ⟧ (Vedānta-sūtra 4.1.4).
⟦viśvarūpa-upāsanā⟧ — worshiping the universe, “service to people is service to God.” The object consists of the guṇas—and consciousness remains within the guṇas. Only service to that which is beyond the guṇas, to the sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha, elevates one beyond the guṇas (Bhagavad-gītā 14.26).

Even meditation on the universal form in the “Second Canto” of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is only an initial stage, until loving service awakens (2.2.14). To meditate on what has not been seen means intensifying imagination, ⟦kalpanā⟧, and the fluctuations of the mind; Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī says that meditation on what has been seen diminishes imagination (⟦dṛṣṭa-kalpanā-lāghavāt⟧). Therefore the vigraha has appeared: Kṛṣṇa can be seen directly. There is no other way to rise beyond the false ego, “I am the enjoyer, I am the doer,” than the path of arcana—the service of the Deities (lecture no. 10183).

Impersonalists say: ⟦sādhakānāṁ hitārthāya brahmaṇo rūpa-kalpanā⟧ — “For the benefit of the sādhakas, imagine a form for Brahman.” This is incorrect, just as “imagine a form of God” is incorrect. Kṛṣṇa has mercifully appeared as the vigraha—without imagination or speculation (lecture no. 10183).

subsections.title: The Four Sweetnesses of Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana

content.quote: But even that Krishna in who (..) on driving the chariot of Krishna, He does not have the four mādhurīs of Krishna in Vṛndāvana. So our ācāryas are so kind, so merciful, and they have manifested that Krishna of Vṛndāvana who has the rūpa-mādhurī, (..) of His form, veṇu-mādhurī, the sweetness of His flute, the prema-mādhurī, the sweetness of His loving associates because Krishna is not alone. His most loving associate is there, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Who has more prema than Rādhikā, no one. And līlā-mādhurī, that Krishna has the all the sweetest pastimes. And so we see that in the service of the deity, there is the pūrṇa-mādhurya-āsvādana and not in any other path or any other (..) object of service.

content.content: Our ācāryas reveal not Nārāyaṇa, but Kṛṣṇa of Vṛndāvana; Gurudev (Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja) revealed Rādhā-Śyāmasundara in the āśrama in Vṛndāvana. Nārāyaṇa has sixty qualities, while Kṛṣṇa possesses four additional qualities that Nārāyaṇa does not have (⟦līlā premṇā priyādhikyaṁ mādhuryaṁ veṇu-rūpayoḥ⟧, Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya 23.84–85):

Even Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna’s charioteer, who drove the chariot out of love for him, does not possess the four sweetnesses of Vṛndāvana. And Bhagavad-gītā (11.50) shows that after the universal and four-armed forms, Kṛṣṇa again became two-armed—His humanlike pastimes give the highest taste. Therefore, in the service of the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Deity there is ⟦pūrṇa-mādhurya-āsvādana⟧, the complete taste of sweetness, which is found on no other path (lecture no. 10183).

content.quote: This is darśana of the vigraha. But we would not know it unless we hear. Now that's the topic we were discussing. That serving, seeing the deity, the sweetness of the deity, along with hearing, these two together, they're so effective for awakening greed. Hearing can be effective by itself. But only darśana of the deity will not be effective by itself. But if it's performed along with hearing and every time you come before Rādhā and Krishna and the saṁskāras of this sweet kathā are raised in the heart, then the greed will intensify every day. So how merciful is the vigraha.

more.quote: So this is very important because sometimes devotees may come into the temple room and look and see the deity is here. The deity is here again, saw them yesterday. Or they may think here is Bhagavān, here is God, it's aiśvarya-darśana. But we should aspire for mādhurya-darśana. Aspire for mādhurya-darśana. That means that we see that Krishna is playing His flute. Why? Because He has so much love in His heart, He cannot express it. If He'll try to express, His throat will become gadgada, His throat will be choked in emotion. And so the only way He can express His love is through the music of the flute, so He has taken His flute. Rādhikā is there. Rūpa Gosvāmī has said,

content.sanskrit:
śrī-mūrter mādhurīṁ prekṣya tat-tal-līlāṁ niśamya vā
tad-bhāvākāṅkṣiṇo ye syus teṣu sādhanatānayoḥ
content.translation: Those in whom, after seeing the sweetness of the Deity or hearing about His pastimes, a longing for the moods of the devotees of Vraja has awakened are qualified for rāgānugā-sādhana (Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu; lecture no. 10183).

content.content: Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī explains that if one only looks at the Deity and does not listen, longing for the love of the vraja-gopīs will not awaken; hearing about Kṛṣṇa’s līlās from pure devotees has an effect even by itself; and hearing together with darśana and service to the Deity is especially powerful. Therefore, when coming to the temple, do not think, “The Deity is the same as yesterday,” and do not limit yourself to ⟦aiśvarya-darśana⟧—aspire for ⟦mādhurya-darśana⟧: Kṛṣṇa plays the flute because He cannot otherwise express His love; Rādhikā is nearby, and their love, ⟦rati⟧, never ceases (⟦naiva vicchidyate ratiḥ⟧, Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu 3.5.21) (lecture no. 10183).

This is how Paurṇamāsī-Yogamāyā sees Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa (Lalita-mādhava 1.23): Kṛṣṇa’s glances are dark waves, like the Yamunā; Rādhikā’s smile is a bright wave of nectar, like the Gaṅgā; and the invisible third river, like Sarasvatī in Triveṇī, is the satisfaction in the hearts of the devotees who see Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa meet. A single drop of this river carries away all suffering and transports one beyond the seven worlds to Goloka Vṛndāvana. Such is the darśana of the vigraha—but we will not understand this if we do not listen. With each darśana, the saṁskāras of the sweet hari-kathā we have heard rise in the heart, and longing grows day by day (lecture no. 10183).

content.quote:
So one day, Krishna, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he came to Yameśvara-ṭoṭā and he was sitting on the earth in the sand. It's very sandy there in the sand dunes by the ocean.

Mahāprabhu was sitting in the sand and he was drawing in the sand with his fingernail. And as he was drawing in the sand, tears were flowing from his eyes like the Ganges, like Gaṅgā. And his eyes were so filled with tears, he could not see anything. Aśru-gaṅgā netre vahe, kichu nāhi dekhi. And he could not see anything. He was only feeling around in the sand and drawing with his fingernail. And as he was touching the sand, he touched something. And then he began to move some sand with his hands. And then he was so surprised. And he got up and went to Gadādhara Paṇḍita who was nearby and said, "Hey Gadādhara, I want to give you something from my heart. Will you accept it?" Gadādhara Paṇḍita said, "Surely I must accept it." Mahāprabhu said, "Oh, Gadādhara, come with me." And he took the hand of Gadādhara and brought him to that place. And he began to remove the sand, and there was Gopīnātha. The vigraha of Gopīnātha in Yameśvara-ṭoṭā, so his name is Ṭoṭā-gopīnātha.

content.content: In Jagannātha Purī, Mahāprabhu listened every day to Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam from Gadādhara Paṇḍita—Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī Herself—learning to play the role of Rādhikā, which at night He performed in Gambhīrā with Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda, Lalitā, and Viśākhā (⟦rādhikāra prema — guru, āmi — śiṣya naṭa⟧, Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Ādi 4.124).

One day, in the garden of Yameśvara, Yameśvara-ṭoṭā, where Gadādhara Paṇḍita had accepted kṣetra-sannyāsa, Mahāprabhu sat on the sand and traced it with His fingernail; tears flowed from His eyes like the Gaṅgā, and He could see nothing (⟦bhūmira upara vasi’ nija-nakhe bhūmi likhi…⟧). His fingers touched something in the sand. He called Gadādhara: “I want to give you something from My heart—will you accept it?” He brought him over, brushed away the sand, and there was Gopīnātha. This Deity is therefore called Ṭoṭā-Gopīnātha (lecture no. 10183).

sections.title: Daily Duties performed in the Brāhma-muhūrta

content.content: Right after awaking chant ⟦pranama mantra⟧ to Your ⟦Gurudeva⟧.
⟦Śrī Śrī Guru-Gaurāṅga Gāndharvikā-Giridhārī Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārījī kī jaya⟧
And chanting the ⟦pañca-tattva-mantra⟧ and the ⟦mahā-mantra⟧. With heartfelt devotion, chant the following prayers:

content.sanskrit:
jayati jana-nivāso devakī-janma-vādo
yadu-vara-pariṣat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam
sthira-cara-vṛjina-ghnaḥ su-smita-śrī-mukhena
vraja-pura-vanitānāṁ vardhayan kāmadevam
content.translation: All glories to that Yaśodā-nandana -- around whom a controversy arose because He seemingly took birth from the womb of Devakī, although later, that became uncertain -- who resides within the heart of all. His assembly is decorated with the presence of the exalted Yādavas, and He destroys irreligion with His own might and the help of His devotees. The chanting of His name removes inauspiciousness from all living entities, both moving and stationary. All glories to Vrajendra-nandana Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who's softly smiling lotus face always enhances the transcendental lust of the vraja-gopīs. [Śrī-mad-Bhāgavatam 10.90.48]
content.wbw: jayati — all glories to; jana-nivāso — He who resides within the heart of all; devakī-janma-vādo — around whom a controversy arose because He seemingly took birth from the womb of Devakī; yadu-vara-pariṣat — whose assembly is decorated with the presence of the exalted Yādavas; svair — with His own; dorbhir — arms; asyann — destroying; adharmam — irreligion; sthira-cara-vṛjina-ghnaḥ — He who destroys the inauspiciousness of all living entities, both moving and stationary; su-smita-śrī-mukhena — with His beautiful softly smiling face; vraja-pura-vanitānāṁ — of the women of Vraja; vardhayan — enhancing; kāmadevam — transcendental lust.

content.sanskrit:
vidagdha-gopāla-vilāsinīnāṁ
sambhoga-cihnāṅkita-sarva-gātram
pavitram āmnāya girām agamyaṁ
brahma prapadye navanīta-cauram
content.translation: I take shelter of He whose relish of rasa is topmost, the Supreme Absolute Truth, Gopāla Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who bears on different parts of His body signs of amorous union with the expert gopīs, who steals butter, and who is incomprehensible through Vedic statements.
content.wbw: vidagdha-gopāla-vilāsinīnāṁ — of the expert gopīs with whom Gopāla sports; sambhoga-cihnāṅkita-sarva-gātram — whose entire body is marked with signs of amorous union; pavitram — the pure; āmnāya — Vedic; girām — statements; agamyaṁ — incomprehensible through; brahma — the Supreme Absolute Truth; prapadye — I take shelter of; navanīta-cauram — the butter thief.

content.sanskrit:
udgāyatīnām aravinda-locananaṁ
vrajāṅganānāṁ divam aspṛśad dhvaniḥ
dadhnaś ca nirmanthana-śabda-miśrito
nirasyate yena diśām amaṅgalam
content.translation: As it mixes with the sound of churning yoghurt, the vraja-gopīs' loud singing of sweet and melodious songs that glorify the name, form, qualities and pastimes of lotus-eyed Śrī Kṛṣṇa pervades the entire atmosphere and removes inauspiciousness in all directions.
content.wbw: udgāyatīnām — of the singing; aravinda-locananaṁ — of the lotus-eyed Śrī Kṛṣṇa; vrajāṅganānāṁ — of the vraja-gopīs; divam — the sky; aspṛśad — touched; dhvaniḥ — the sound; dadhnaś — of churning yoghurt; ca — and; nirmanthana-śabda-miśrito — mixed with the sound of churning; nirasyate — removes; yena — by which; diśām — of all directions; amaṅgalam — inauspiciousness.

content.content: Then one should brush one's teeth, wash face and then bathe after passing stool and put on clean clothes. Pujari do not go to the toilet in clean clothes!

Long nails are dirty and contaminated. Therefore, it is a general practice of pūjārīs to keep their fingernails short, to avoid contaminating the ⟦bhoga⟧ and other articles meant for offering to the Lord. Even during the four months of ⟦Cāturmāsya⟧, pūjārīs keep their nails short. Brush their teeth even on fast days.
Mantra for taking bath by mind (mānasa-snāna)

content.sanskrit:
oṁ apavitraḥ pavitro vā
sarvāvasthāṁ gato 'pi vā
yaḥ smaret puṇḍarīkākṣaṁ
sa bāhyābhyantara-śuciḥ
content.translation: Whether one is contaminated, pure or in any condition or stage of life, if one remembers the lotus-eyed Lord, Puṇḍarīkākṣa, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, one becomes pure both externally and internally. [Garuḍa Purāṇa]
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; apavitraḥ — contaminated; pavitro — pure; vā — or; sarvāvasthāṁ — in any condition; gato — having entered; 'pi — even; vā — or; yaḥ — whoever; smaret — remembers; puṇḍarīkākṣaṁ — Puṇḍarīkākṣa, the lotus-eyed Lord; sa — he; bāhyābhyantara-śuciḥ — pure both externally and internally.

content.content: After bathing, comb the hair and tie the ⟦śikhā⟧ while remembering the ⟦brahma-gāyatrī⟧, along with the syllable ⟦oṁ⟧.
The ⟦śikhā⟧ is not braided or kept untied and disheveled. It is preferable to tie it with a slip knot.

Do not enter the deity room or the kitchen with contaminated cloth or touch the deity paraphernalia and kitchen pots. Do not clean the deity's paraphernalia or wash the deity's pots while wearing cloth in which one has defecated or slept the night before.
Tīrtha-āvāhana-mantra

Set an empty ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ in place and fill it with fresh water. After pouring a few drops of water from the ⟦ācamana-pātra⟧ or a spouted waterpot onto the fingers of your right hand, purify the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ by ⟦prokṣaṇa⟧:
Chanting ⟦oṁ astrāya phaṭ⟧, sprinkle water on the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧.
Invoke the ⟦Gaṅgā⟧ and other holy rivers by showing the ⟦aṅkuśamudrā⟧ and chanting:

content.sanskrit:
gaṅge ca yamune caiva
godāvari sarasvati
narmade sindho kāveri
jale 'smin sannidhiṁ kuru
content.translation: O Ganges, O Yamunā, O Godāvarī, O Sarasvatī, O Narmadā, O Sindhu, O Kāverī, please become present in this water.
content.wbw: gaṅge — O Ganges; ca — and; yamune — O Yamunā; caiva — and indeed; godāvari — O Godāvarī; sarasvati — O Sarasvatī; narmade — O Narmadā; sindho — O Sindhu; kāveri — O Kāverī; jale — in the water; 'smin — this; sannidhiṁ — presence; kuru — please make.

content.quote: This is the desire. This is the desire of all the Rūpānuga Vaiṣṇavas, only that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa will meet together. This is why we put tilaka on every day, you see? One side is Rādhikā, one side means Kṛṣṇa. They're parallel lines, so the parallel lines don't meet. But these parallel lines are meeting where, here, this is a tulasī leaf, represents Vṛndā.

source.title: Power of Sadhu-Sanga and Vrindavana Lila - 2023-05-12 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: So, once a devotee asked Śrīla Gurudeva, "Every morning we're putting on our tilaka, and we say the mantras: oṁ trivikramāya namaḥ, madhusūdanāya namaḥ. We say all these names, and among them also Vaikuṇṭha-mūrtis, forms of Nārāyaṇa in Vaikuṇṭha. So, what should we, if we are supposed to be one-pointed to Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, then what should we think about when we put on our tilakas?" Śrīla Gurudeva said, "Outwardly, you should say each one of the names, but inwardly you should only say one name: 'Oṁ rādhikāyai namaḥ, I offer myself to Rādhārāṇī.'" So, then that devotee was he was confused. (..) So, Gurudeva said, "Well, you say 'oṁ keśavāya namaḥ', but in your heart you say, 'Oh, oṁ rādhikāyai namaḥ. Oh, Rādhikā, I am Your dāsī.' Always remember this. Even when you chant Kṛṣṇa-nāma, always remember the service of Rādhikā."

source.title: 2021.01.07 Srila Bhaktivedanta Narayana Gosvami Maharaj Tirobhava Tithi

more.quote:
I mentioned that the significance of tilaka represents Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, the desire that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa should meet in Vṛndāvana. So these are the (..) bhāvas of the devotees in Rāga-mārga. Like Gurudeva said, when he puts on tilaka and says the various names, oṁ keśavāya namaḥ, oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ, mādhavāya namaḥ, oṁ govindāya namaḥ, though he said Kṛṣṇa's (..) he says Kṛṣṇa's name, but because he is in the bhāvollāsa-rati where the love for Kṛṣṇa is the sthāyi-bhāva, but it nourishes the suhṛd-rati, love for Rādhikā, therefore, when he remembers Kṛṣṇa's names, he actually remembers Śrīmatī Rādhikā, how that name of Kṛṣṇa is related to Rādhikā, always Rādhikā, Rādhikā, Rādhikā.

So keśavāya namaḥ, Keśava means what? Keśān vāyate iti keśavaḥ. He who decorates the hair of Śrīmatī Rādhikā in Śṛṅgāra-vaṭa is Keśava. Nārāyaṇa, (..)? Nara means water, ayana means one who rests, one who rests on the water, Lord Nārāyaṇa. He's resting on the water on Ananta Śeṣa. So here it means that form of Kṛṣṇa who is floating in the ocean of Rādhā-prema. Oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ. Mādhavāya, Mādhava means who is the beloved of Rādhikā, who is Mādhavī. Mādhavī is a the special type of heroine who has completely controlled her hero.

source.title: Q&A Meditation in Raganuga Bhakti and When Applying Tilaka - 2024-11-11 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: Our Different lines have different types of tilaka, made of different substances, but our tilaka is gopī-candana. Sometimes there are some devotees from other lines, and they criticize, "Well, what is your tilaka? Why is this Why don't you wear black Rādhā-kuṇḍa tilaka or something?" But you know that Madhvācārya's iṣṭa-deva, Nartaka Gopāla, was found in a ball of gopī-candana. And so all the ācāryas in his line up to our Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha, and Mādhavendra Purī, Īśvara Purī, and Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they received gopī-candana tilaka. Caitanya Mahāprabhu (..) discovered Rādhā-kuṇḍa in his sannyāsa-līlā, in his prakaṭa-līlā. And he took some mud from there and applied it for a few days. But in the aprakaṭa-nitya-līlā of Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he never leaves Navadvīpa, and he always has gopī-candana tilaka. And (..) you can see in the Rādhā-Dāmodara temple that Rūpa Gosvāmī had only one dīkṣā disciple, Jīva Gosvāmī, and they are coming in that line. From Rūpa Gosvāmī, Jīva Gosvāmī, and their tilaka is exactly the same as ours.

source.title: Q&A Meditation in Raganuga Bhakti and When Applying Tilaka - 2024-11-11 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: The guru gives Tilaka. So now, unlike (..) the branding, we actually do this. And the guru gives tilaka to the disciple. We accept the same tilaka that our guru wears. I know that many devotees, oh Rādhā-kuṇḍa Tilaka, Rādhā-kuṇḍa is so high, let's wear Rādhā-kuṇḍa. Yeah, but my guru wears this tilaka, I wear this tilaka. Rādhā-kuṇḍa may be so high, that's great. But I'll never get to Rādhā-kuṇḍa unless I'm in the ānugatya of my guru. So I wear this, the gopī-candana. In Rāga-vartma-candrikā, Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura says that gopī-candana is favorable for Rāgānugā-bhakti. Why? Because it's the dust of the Gopīs' lotus feet. Someone may say, but Caitanya Mahāprabhu wore Rādhā-kuṇḍa tilaka. Yes, in his naimittika-līlā, after he took sannyāsa, he went to Vraja and did parikramā, he discovered Rādhā-kuṇḍa, took some clay and put it on. But actually, we don't worship the sannyāsa form of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Right? We worship him in his nitya-līlā in Navadvīpa.

source.title: Guru-tattva and Diksha Process - 2025-05-04 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: So, you know that our tilak is a yellow color. Other sometimes are wearing Rādhā-kuṇḍa tilak, it's gray. Sometimes they say, "Oh, why you wear this tilak from Dvārakā? We don't want to go to Dvārakā." Because our tilak comes from Dvārakā. But actually it's not from Dvārakā, it was imported to Dvārakā from Vṛndāvana. We're just exporting it back. So you can see that our Madhvācārya, he, (..) discovered the lost deity of Narta Gopāla. And how was he? He found Him in a big block of tilak, that means that Kṛṣṇa for 4,000 years was just immersed in gopīs' foot dust.

So, (..) (..) in the nitya-līlā, Mahāprabhu wears gopī-candana. Why? The gopī-candana is worn by the Mādhvas. It was Mādhvācārya who discovered the Dadhi-manthana Gopāla at the coast just close to Udupi. And where did he discover him? In a big block of gopī-candana.

[…]

So Mādhvācārya came and he touched that block of tilaka and it broke open and inside there was that Dadhi-manthana Gopāla from Dvārakā. So Krishna for more than four thousand years had been completely immersed in the foot dust of Vraja-gopīs. He was feeling, Krishna was feeling separation from Vraja-gopīs there in Dvārakā. And so He completely covered himself for four thousand years in foot dust of Vraja-gopīs to survive. What a bhāva. So Mādhvācārya wears gopī-candana tilaka from Dvārakā.

Now, what is gopī-candana? Gopī-candana is once Kṛṣṇa was in Dvārakā, and He had a headache. And Nārada came to Him, said, "My Lord, can I do something, how can I help You?" He said, "Only one thing can cure Me: the foot dust of My devotees." So then Nārada went to Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā and the queens, and said, "Oh, Kṛṣṇa has a headache, and the only thing that can cure Him is His devotees' foot dust, please give your foot dust." They said, "(..) No. We cannot put our foot dust on our husband's head." Why? Because in the married relationship, there's maryādā. There's maryādā, so it's not included in the pure line of rāga, rāgātmika, it's that's not a pure rāga. So they said, "We cannot, it's against dharma for the wife to put her foot dust on her husband's head." So then he came back to Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa said, "Oh Nārada, ask the gopīs of Vṛndāvana." So then Nārada, he went to Vṛndāvana and said to the gopīs, "Kṛṣṇa is suffering with a headache, and the only thing that can cure Him is foot dust of His devotees." So then the gopīs, they took the dust of Vraja. It was the dust of Vraja, and they rubbed it on their feet, and they said, "Nārada, take this." They're rubbing the dust of Vraja on their feet and giving it to Nārada. Nārada said, "Aren't you worried that you go to hell for this?" Gopīs said, "We may go to hell, but let Kṛṣṇa be happy." This is Vraja-gopīs' mood.

[…]

So this bhāva of the gopīs is in that dust. So then Nārada brought that dust to Dvārakā. And then Kṛṣṇa, He took that dust, and He put it on His head. And He felt some relief, because the headache was not really like a migraine. It was actually separation. He was feeling separation from Rādhikā and the Vraja-gopīs.

All the saints and sages in India wear tilaka. Sometimes it's slightly different shapes or colors, so... But if you see a temple of Viṣṇu, on the roof of the temple they have this shape. So, this tilaka signifies that my body is a temple and inside this temple along with my ātmā, my soul, is Paramātmā, God is there. When we see another person also wearing tilaka, it reminds us, "Oh, God is there."

source.title: Bhakti Yoga Retreat in Tenerife with Sri Prem Prayojan Prabhu, 18.07.2014, Morning class

content.content: After sitting on a clean ⟦āsana⟧ (seat), pour Ganges water into the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧. In the absence of Ganges water, put fresh water in the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧. Then, remembering the Ganges and other sacred rivers, touch this water, and chant the ⟦tīrtha-āvāhana-mantra⟧.

Use this water and ⟦gopī-candana⟧ to form a paste in the left hand. Then, with the twelve ⟦mantras⟧ beginning with ⟦oṁ keśavāya namaḥ⟧, apply ⟦tilaka⟧ to the twelve different parts of the body, beginning with the forehead, by drawing the ⟦ūrdhva-puṇḍra⟧ (two vertical lines) representing the temple of ⟦Śrī Hari⟧.

Starting from the centre of the eyebrows, form two vertical lines on the forehead that reach up to the beginning of the hairline. There must be a clean space in the middle of the ⟦ūrdhva-puṇḍra⟧. From just below the centre of the eyebrows extending to three-quarters of the way down the nose is called the ⟦nāsāmūla⟧. [This is where one forms the shape of a tulasī leaf.] The ⟦mantra⟧ to invoke remembrance of the twelve names of the Lord (⟦dvādaśa-nāma-smaraṇa-mantra⟧) is as follows:

content.sanskrit:
lalāṭe keśavaṁ dhyāyen
nārāyaṇam athodare
vakṣaḥ-sthale mādhavaṁ tu
govindaṁ kaṇṭha-kūpake

viṣṇuṁ ca dakṣiṇe kukṣau
bāhau ca madhusūdanam
trivikramaṁ kandhare tu
vāmanaṁ vāma-pārśvake

śrīdharaṁ vāma-bāhau tu
hṛṣīkeśaṁ ca kandhare
pṛṣṭhe tu padmanābhaṁ ca
kaṭyāṁ dāmodaraṁ nyaset

tat prakṣālana-toyaṁ tu
vāsudevāya mūrdhani
content.translation: When one marks the forehead with tilaka, one must remember Keśava. When one marks the lower abdomen, one must remember Nārāyaṇa. When marking the chest, one should remember Mādhava, and when marking the hollow of the neck one should remember Govinda. Viṣṇu should be remembered while marking the right side of the belly, and Madhusūdana should be remembered when marking the right arm. Trivikrama should be remembered when marking the right shoulder, and Vāmana should be remembered when marking the left side of the belly. Śrīdhara should be remembered while marking the left arm, and Hṛṣīkeśa should be remembered when marking the left shoulder. Padmanābha and Dāmodara should be remembered when marking the upper and lower back, and Vāsudeva should be remembered when marking the top of the head.
