content.wbw: lalāṭe — on the forehead; keśavaṁ — Keśava; dhyāyen — one should remember; nārāyaṇam — Nārāyaṇa; athodare — then on the lower abdomen; vakṣaḥ-sthale — on the chest; mādhavaṁ — Mādhava; tu — and; govindaṁ — Govinda; kaṇṭha-kūpake — in the hollow of the neck; viṣṇuṁ — Viṣṇu; ca — and; dakṣiṇe — on the right; kukṣau — side of the belly; bāhau — on the arm; ca — and; madhusūdanam — Madhusūdana; trivikramaṁ — Trivikrama; kandhare — on the shoulder; tu — and; vāmanaṁ — Vāmana; vāma-pārśvake — on the left side of the belly; śrīdharaṁ — Śrīdhara; vāma-bāhau — on the left arm; tu — and; hṛṣīkeśaṁ — Hṛṣīkeśa; ca — and; kandhare — on the shoulder; pṛṣṭhe — on the upper back; tu — and; padmanābhaṁ — Padmanābha; ca — and; kaṭyāṁ — on the lower back; dāmodaraṁ — Dāmodara; nyaset — one should apply; tat — that; prakṣālana-toyaṁ — water used for washing; tu — and; vāsudevāya — for Vāsudeva; mūrdhani — on the top of the head.

content.content: In accordance with the aforementioned ⟦smaraṇa-mantra⟧, chant the following ⟦mantras⟧ while touching each part of the body, either while applying the ⟦tilaka⟧ mark or after the ⟦tilaka⟧ has already been applied:
Drop a spoonful of water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ into the hand, to mix with the remnant ⟦gopī-candana⟧. Wipe the ⟦candana⟧ on top of the head, while chanting ⟦oṁ vāsudevāya namaḥ⟧.
Note: ⟦Tilaka⟧ paste is to be freshly made each time. Do not apply ⟦Tilaka⟧ in the bathroom.

subsections.title: Performing Ācamana, sipping water for purification

content.content: After applying ⟦tilaka⟧, one should perform ācamana. ⟦Vaiṣṇava⟧ ācamana is of two kinds: ordinary (⟦sādhāraṇa⟧) and specific (⟦viśeṣa⟧). Before performing any devotional activity, ordinary ācamana will suffice. However, at the time of bathing the deity or at the time of ⟦pūjā⟧, ⟦viśeṣa-ācamana⟧ is to be performed.
Sādhāraṇa-ācamana
Drop a spoonful of water [from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧, or ācamana cup] into the centre of the palm of the right hand (known as the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧) and chant

content.sanskrit: oṁ keśavāya namaḥ

content.content: Sip a little of the water [from the end of the palm] and throw the rest to the ground.
Purify the right hand [by dropping a new spoonful of water in the palm of the right hand and then throwing that water to the ground].
Repeat the above process of ācamana, this time while chanting

content.sanskrit: oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ

content.content: and then again while chanting

content.sanskrit: oṁ mādhavāya namaḥ

content.content: Viśeṣa-ācamana
Always perform ācamana before entering the Deity room to worship the Lord.

With an ⟦ācamana-pātra⟧ filled with water clean both hands by sprinkling them with water; holding the ācamana spoon in your left hand, pour a few drops into the right palm. While looking at the water chant the appropriate ⟦mantra⟧ and then silently sip the water from the base of the right thumb (the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧). The procedure for basic ācamana consists of the first three steps below. If time and circumstances permit, you may perform the complete ācamana:

items.label: ⟦oṁ keśavāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sip water from the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧ of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sip water from the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧ of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ mādhavāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sip water from the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧ of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ govindāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sprinkle water on your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ viṣṇave namaḥ⟧
items.value: sprinkle water on your left hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ madhusūdanāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your right cheek with the fingers of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ trivikramāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your left cheek with the fingers of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ vāmanāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: wipe above your upper lip with the base of your right thumb.

items.label: ⟦oṁ śrīdharāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: wipe below your lower lip with the base of your right thumb.

items.label: ⟦oṁ dāmodarāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sprinkle water on the top of your head.

content.content: While chanting the following ⟦mantras⟧, perform the hand motions:

items.label: ⟦oṁ vāsudevāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your upper and lower lips with the tips of the fingers of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ saṅkarṣaṇāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your right nostril with your right thumb and forefinger.

content.content: Now chant the following ⟦mantra⟧ from the ⟦Ṛig Veda⟧ while showing the ⟦praṇāma-mudrā⟧ (palms together in front of your heart):

content.sanskrit:
oṁ tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṁ padaṁ
sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ
divīva cakṣur-ātatam

tad viprāso vipanyavo
jāgṛvaṁ saḥ samindhate
viṣṇor yat paramaṁ padam
content.translation: Just as those with ordinary vision see the sun's rays in the sky, so the wise and learned devotees always see the supreme abode of Lord Vishnu. Because those highly praise-worthy and spiritually awake brāhmaṇas can see that abode, they can also reveal it to others. [Rig Veda Samhita]
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; tad — that; viṣṇoḥ — of Lord Viṣṇu; paramaṁ — supreme; padaṁ — abode; sadā — always; paśyanti — see; sūrayaḥ — wise and learned devotees; divīva — as in the sky; cakṣur-ātatam — the rays visible to ordinary sight; tad — that abode; viprāso — brāhmaṇas; vipanyavo — highly praiseworthy; jāgṛvaṁ — spiritually awake; saḥ — they; samindhate — reveal to others; viṣṇor — of Lord Viṣṇu; yat — which; paramaṁ — supreme; padam — abode.

sections.title: Daily Deity Schedule
sections.subtitle: Procedure for Waking up the Deities

content.content: The pūjārī should arrive no later than 3:20 a.m.
Perform ⟦Viśeṣa-ācamana⟧ (full ācamana)
Make up 1 tray with: Sweets, sweet rice, cup water, cup milk. Note: place tulasī on each preparation.
Make up āratī tray with: Incense, ghee lamp, flowers, handkerchief, water, cotton stick for perfume oil.

content.quote: At that time in the early morning, the mañjarīs, they were awake almost the whole night, but just towards the end of the night, they lie down on the—in the courtyard, just outside the kuñja. And then suddenly, (..) Maidservant wakes up and looks around because she's afraid, "Oh, did I oversleep? Did I miss my service?" And then she looks around, sees, "Oh, others are still resting, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are still sleeping." Sigh. Relief. "I thought—for a moment I was very anxious, but now I see there's still time." So then that devotee is remembering his spiritual form, will get up and go and wake up Gurudeva. Understand? That means wake up another sakhī, another other mañjarīs who are there. And then go to see, uṭho, nidrā chāḍi’ uṭha jīva, "Oh, my life and soul, wake up." And they'll go, and they look inside: "Oh, in this beautiful kuñja-bhavana, this pavilion of flowers in the forest of Vṛndāvana on the bank of Yamunā, see Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Śyāmasundara resting there."

source.title: The Story of Nachiketu, Vibhāvarī-Śeṣa with Explanation - 2024-04-07 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: Oh Kṛṣṇa, please wake up and cast Your merciful glance upon the world. "And when by Your glance You wake up the world, wake up in my heart summaṅgala-rati, very auspicious rati, that is bhāva." The appearance of the divine sentiment of love for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. So if you will undergo the inconvenience and austerity to wake up very early every morning and pray, "Oh my Lord, please wake up, open Your eyes, glance upon me, and wake up the rati in my heart," every day, every week, every month, every year, for years and years, what will happen? One day Kṛṣṇa will say, "Okay." He will awaken. "You asked Me so many times, you woke up so early every day for so many years, and you begged Me for this, take." And Kṛṣṇa will give, and then you can hear the birds are singing, cuckoo birds are calling, peacocks are calling, and the sweet nectarine beautiful atmosphere of Vraja, where Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa awaken.

source.title: Who really knows Srimad-Bhagavatam, Sri Prem Prayojan Prabhu in Barcelona, 24.07.2014

more.quote:
In the morning, when we wake up our deities,

[…]

You have to wake up and you touch the feet and wake, "Oh, my dear Ṭhākurajī, please wake up and glance at me with Your auspicious glance. And by that glance, wake up my ecstatic love for You."

source.title: 2016.08.24 Namashtaka, Nama Tattva, Guru & Disciple, Ghost of Nam Prabhu, Krishna Lila, Q&A

more.quote: So first of all, we bow down to Guru. And by his mercy, by his permission, we approach Gaurāṅga. And by the mercy of Gaurāṅga, when we bow down to his līlā, then internally, we have a sphūrti, or the awakening of the realization of Radha Krishna's līlā. When they explained to you, is called bhajana-cāturya. Cāturya means cunningness, cleverness, skill. Many persons, they cannot realize Radha and Krishna because they don't have skill. They don't know the art of how to do bhajana. So the art of how to enter into these confidential pastimes is hinted at here. First, remember Guru, the spiritual master. By his mercy, remember Gaurāṅga in the early morning. When Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu is waking up in the morning, tears are flowing from his eyes. Why? Because he's remembering how Radha and Krishna are waking up in the morning. So Gaura-līlā is called udbodhaka-līlā. Udbodhaka-līlā means the pastime that awakens your realization of Radha and Krishna's pastimes. So don't try to go directly to Radha and Krishna. First remember Guru, then remember Gaurāṅga, Caitanya Mahāprabhu. And then by his mercy, his mercy will awaken the remembrance of Radha Krishna.

content.content: Prayers to be chanted upon entering the Deity room
Remaining outside the Deity room, ring the bell.
Reciting following verses, pray to the Lord to awaken.

content.sanskrit:
so 'sāv adabhra-karuṇo bhagavān vivṛddha-
prema-smitena nayanāmburuhaṁ vijṛmbhan
utthāya viśva-vijayāya ca no viṣādaṁ
mādhvyā girāpanayatāt puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ
content.translation: Śrī Bhagavān, who is supreme and primeval, is unlimitedly merciful. I pray that He bless me with His smiling glance by opening His lotus eyes. He can uplift the entire cosmic creation and remove our grief and sorrow with the sweet words of instruction emanating from His lotus mouth. [SB 3.9.25]
content.wbw: so — He; 'sāv — that Lord; adabhra-karuṇo — unlimitedly merciful; bhagavān — Śrī Bhagavān; vivṛddha- — fully blossoming; prema-smitena — with a loving smile; nayanāmburuhaṁ — His lotus eyes; vijṛmbhan — opening wide; utthāya — rising; viśva-vijayāya — to uplift the entire cosmic creation; ca — and; no — our; viṣādaṁ — grief and sorrow; mādhvyā — sweet; girāpanayatāt — may He remove with words; puruṣaḥ — the Supreme Person; purāṇaḥ — primeval.

content.sanskrit:
deva prapannārti-hara prasādaṁ kuru keśava
avalokana-dānena bhūyo māṁ parayācyuta
content.translation: Keśava, O infallible one, O remover of the distress of the surrendered souls, kindly bestow Your mercy upon me by again awarding me with Your transcendental glance.
content.wbw: deva — O Lord; prapannārti-hara — O remover of the distress of the surrendered souls; prasādaṁ — mercy; kuru — kindly bestow; keśava — O Keśava; avalokana-dānena — by granting a glance; bhūyo — again; māṁ — upon me; parayācyuta — transcendental, O Acyuta.

content.sanskrit:
jaya jaya kṛpamaya jagatera nātha
sarva jagatere koro śubha-dṛṣṭī-pāta
content.translation: O Bhagavān! All glories, all glories unto You, O merciful Lord of the universe, please cast Your auspicious glance upon all the worlds.
content.wbw: jaya — all glories; jaya — all glories; kṛpamaya — O merciful one; jagatera — of the universe; nātha — O Lord; sarva — all; jagatere — upon the worlds; koro — please cast; śubha-dṛṣṭī-pāta — Your auspicious glance.

content.content: Then knock on the door and enter the Deity room.
Turn on a soft light and sit down on the ⟦āsana⟧.
Perform ⟦Sādhāraṇa-ācamana⟧ (ordinary ācamana) and, while ringing the bell, proceed to the place where ⟦Srī Gurudeva⟧ is resting. Awaken him by touching his feet and chant the following prayers.
Prayers in Deity's room
Touching the feet of ⟦Śrī Gurudev⟧, awaken Him by chanting:

content.sanskrit:
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha śrī guro
tyaja nidrāṁ kṛpāmaya
aiṁ gurave namaḥ
content.translation: O most merciful Gurudeva, please arise, please arise and give up your sleep.
content.wbw: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha — please arise, please arise; śrī — revered; guro — O Gurudeva; tyaja — give up; nidrāṁ — sleep; kṛpāmaya — most merciful one; aiṁ — bīja-mantra; gurave — unto Gurudeva; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.content: Then, touching the feet of ⟦Śrī Gaurāṅga⟧, awaken Him by chanting:

content.sanskrit:
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha gaurāṅga
jahi nidrāṁ mahāprabho
śubha-dṛṣṭi pradānena
trailokya-maṅgalaṁ kuru
klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
content.translation: O Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu, please arise, please arise and give up Your sleep. Please benedict the three worlds with Your auspicious glance.
content.wbw: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha — please arise, please arise; gaurāṅga — O Gaurāṅga; jahi — give up; nidrāṁ — sleep; mahāprabho — O Mahāprabhu; śubha-dṛṣṭi — auspicious glance; pradānena — by giving; trailokya-maṅgalaṁ — blessing of the three worlds; kuru — please bestow; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation “svāhā”.

content.content: Next, while touching the lotus feet of ⟦Śrī Rādhā Krsna⟧ awaken Them by chanting:

content.sanskrit:
go-gopa-gokulānanda
yaśodānanda vardhana
uttiṣṭha rādhayā sārddhaṁ
prātar āsīj jagat-pate
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: O joy of Gokula, the cowherd boys and the cows; O increaser of Mother Yaśodā's bliss; O Lord of the universe; please arise along with Śrī Rādhā, for it is almost morning.
content.wbw: go-gopa-gokulānanda — O joy of Gokula, the cowherd boys and the cows; yaśodānanda — O increaser of Mother Yaśodā's bliss; vardhana — increaser; uttiṣṭha — please arise; rādhayā — along with Śrī Rādhā; sārddhaṁ — together with; prātar — in the morning; āsīj — it is almost; jagat-pate — O Lord of the universe; śrīṁ — bīja-mantra; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.content: Afterward, meditate that these personalities have risen and taken their seat on the altar.
(Physically place the Deities on the altar if They were removed from there the previous night and placed in a bed.)
Carefully replace the Chota Deities on the altar, put crown on Deities.
Clean and cover the bed.

subsections.title: Washing the mouth of the Lord

content.content: Now, while chanting the following ⟦mantras⟧, one should first offer ācamana (water for cleansing the mouth) to ⟦Sri Guru⟧ and the deity. Then offer a twig for cleaning the teeth (⟦danta-kāṣṭha⟧), and again ācamana:

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.content: Note: Ācamana is offered by tipping a spoonful of water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ into an empty container (⟦visarjanīya-pātra⟧), while ringing the bell and saying the respective ⟦mantra⟧.

content.sanskrit:
eṣa danta-kāṣṭhaḥ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
eṣa danta-kāṣṭhaḥ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
eṣa danta-kāṣṭhaḥ śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.content: The above ⟦mantras⟧ signify the offering of a twig for cleaning the teeth (⟦danta-kāṣṭha⟧). This item is offered by mind rather than by offering the actual article. Generally, in the absence of any item, one may meditate on the particular item and, while saying the appropriate ⟦mantra⟧, offer water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ into the throw-out pot.
Now offer ācamana like before, but 12 times. (3 times is also acceptable.)

subsections.title: Cleaning the Deities and the altar

content.content: Wipe the face, hands and feet of each Deity with a clean cloth. After removing old garlands, tulasī leaves and flowers, clean the altar and then purify one's hands. Offer tulasī and decorate each Deity with the appropriate crown, flute and ornaments while chanting Their appropriate ⟦mūla-mantra⟧. Then perform ⟦maṅgala-ārati⟧.
Replace crowns and ⟦Kṛṣṇa⟧'s staff and water cups. Make bed. Place out sitting mats for ⟦bhoga⟧ offering and clean offering tables.

content.quote: But the problem is that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa cannot go home being decorated in the sambhoga-cihna. So they'll have to be, (..) (..) removed. And that's why the pujārī in maṅgala-ārati is coming with a water and a cloth. So first she puts the water in the conch, that means the maidservants are coming and putting some, (..) fresh, fragrant water on the bodies of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and taking the cloth and wiping away the sambhoga-cihna. But as they wipe away As this As these cihna are the signs of sambhoga meeting, then as they're being wiped away, that means it's as if they are erasing the pastime itself. And it's awakening the vipralambha-bhāva. When the sambhoga-cihna is wiped away, when meeting is wiped away, then you are left with separation. This is the bhāva of maṅgala-ārati. So the devotees are watching the ārati and seeing the offering of the water, the offering of the cloth like this, and the nectar of the union is being wiped away, and the pain of separation is rising up in the heart.

source.title: 2019.12.22 Meanings Of Japa And Mangala Arati

more.quote:
Some of the maidservants, they're taking some fragrant water and very soft cloth, and dipping it, and wiping away the various cosmetics from the faces of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa because Kṛṣṇa has Rādhikā’s lip gloss here, and some kājala, black kājala from Her eyes on His lips, and some cosmetics, some candana, kastūrī, and the musk and so on is smeared on the body of Rādhikā, so they're coming and with a cloth and wiping away, just like the pūjārī in the maṅgala-ārati is offering some water, and then taking a cloth and offering cloth and cleaning like this. This is the inner meaning of (..) the āratī. Another maidservant takes a dīpa and does āratī because āratī means that which brings auspiciousness. So they're thinking, “Oh, I am offering āratī to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, They will now get back to Their home without being caught, there should be no problems. No difficulties should come in Their life, and They should quickly again meet without any obstacles.” When a person offers āratī in a sweet mood, it means, “May whatever difficulties are there in your life, I'll let me take all of those difficulties on my head, and let you be free from any problems.” And this is the loving mood.

Some maidservants are then fanning with a cāmara. So in this cāmara, there are so many hairs, right? So these hairs, these are like the prāṇa. There are 72,000 nāḍīs in the body, so the hairs of the cāmara are like 72,000 nāḍīs with the prāṇa, that means, “Oh, worshipping Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa with all their prāṇa.” They're not thinking metaphysically, only this is (..) a bhāva that they're serving with all their prāṇa, just to please Rādhā. Their only happiness is lies in Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s happiness, and Kṛṣṇa’s happiness lies in Rādhārāṇī’s happiness, so we'll just focus on Her mainly. If Rādhikā is happy, Kṛṣṇa is happy, so we focus the service on Śrīmatī Rādhikā.

source.title: Meaning of Mangala Arati - 2021-07-23 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: And outside, a gentle breeze is blowing and causing the lotus flowers in the Yamunā and in the lakes to tremble, and carrying (..) their fragrance. So now Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa outside, and just now they'll have to return to their homes, but just to make sure that there's no obstacle, that there's no hitch, that they don't get seen or discovered on the way, then Lalitā-sakhī comes, and Lalitā-sakhī is doing ārati. Ārati means, because a general person who is in aiśvarya, they do ārati to the Deity, they have so many ideas: Supreme Lord is the creator of the universe, earth, water, fire, air, and ether, so I'm offering the incense because fragrance is the quality of earth, and I'm offering the dīpa because that is fire, and water, and like this, and air with the fan, like So this is people think about ārati in this sense. But in the Vedic culture, ārati means that we are performing this auspicious ritual, that whatever difficulty or problem may come in your life, may you not face that, let it come to me, and not to you. So, for example, like Mātā Yaśodā offers ārati to Kṛṣṇa when He comes back in the evening from taking the cows to graze, you think Mātā Yaśodā is saying, "I am worshiping You with all the elements"? So try to understand that ārati as a loving dimension of may you be happy and let all whatever calamity may fall upon you, I'll take it on my head. So in this way, Lalitā-sakhī and all the sakhīs, Lalitā-sakhī is leading the ārati, and this is maṅgala-ārati.

source.title: 2019.12.22 Meanings Of Japa And Mangala Arati

more.quote: It means may this auspicious maṅgala-ārati awaken in the hearts of the devotees. We are not practicing Kṛṣṇa consciousness to be forever in a state of no anubhāva, realization, anubhūti. We are searching for realization. And so in maṅgala-ārati we're praying, "(..) Oh Guru, Oh Gaurāṅga, Oh Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, sprinkle Your mercy upon me that this beautiful scene of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa's waking in the morning, the maṅgala-ārati, will rise up in my heart."

source.title: Sri Prem Prayojan - 2019-12-22 - Meanings of Japa and Mangala Arati

more.quote: So, soon Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa will have to secretly return to Their homes. So the mañjarīs bring the, all the paraphernalia for ārati, and Lalitā-sakhī performs the ārati ceremony. Yes. They bring all the paraphernalia. You see, the sakhīs, they don't do that kind of work, the mañjarīs, the maidservants do all the small things. (..) And she's offering ārati, (..) and we are experiencing this ārati in morning. The meaning of ārati is to make maṅgala, auspiciousness. In other words, "Oh, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, we are praying, and You can return to Your homes without anyone catching You and finding out what happened, and there'll be no obstacles, no problems." And who is offering the ārati and watching the ārati, they feel, "In my life, if I have any good karma, I am offering it all to You, so that You will not experience any suffering at all. Let the suffering come to me, but not to You." This is the meaning of ārati. Of course, (^)Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa, gopīs, they have no karma, but because Their pastime is the nara-vat, human-like pastimes, They don't know They are God or Goddess or anything. They play—it is a līlā—They play like humans. So they are thinking in this way. Oh, she's fanning with the cāmara. So the cāmara, it has thousands and thousands of hairs. And gopīs are thinking, "(..) Oh Kṛṣṇa, oh Rādhikā, we are serving You with our 72,000 nāḍīs. 72,000 prāṇas, we are worshipping You, that's our cāmara."

source.title: Sri Prem Prayojan - 2019-07-18 - Meaning of Mangala Arati

content.content: 4:10 a.m. Offer ⟦bhoga⟧ (follow the ⟦bhoga⟧ offering procedure).
4:25 a.m. Perform ⟦ācamanīyaṁ⟧. Remove plates. Clean tables. Bring in āratī tray. Light candle. Replace ⟦Kṛṣṇa⟧'s flute.
4:30 a.m. Blow conch, open curtain, offer ārati.
4:50 a.m. Finish ārati, blow conch. Offer devotees ⟦prasād⟧ flowers. Clean and put away ārati tray.
4:55 a.m. Offer scent. Clean floor.
Dressing Their Lordships (in progress)

content.quote: So each and every aspect of Rādhārāṇī's body, and cosmetics, and ornaments—ṣoḍaśa-śṛṅgāra, sixteen types of cosmetics, and dvādaśa-ābharaṇa, twelve types of golden ornaments—they're all various bhāvas of Śrīmatī Rādhikā. She's decorated in jewels; Her jewels are prema-vaicittya, (..) Her sparkling jewels are the separation She feels in Kṛṣṇa's presence. So all of these things make Her svarūpa beautiful. So when you're decorating your Deities, just remember that all the śṛṅgāra was not bought from Loi Bazaar. Forget that! This śṛṅgāra is actually the all the various aspects of Rādhikā's mahā-bhāva. And then your service becomes rasamayī sevā.

source.title: Sri Prem Prayojan - 2018-05-04 - Disappearance Day of Sri Ray Ramananda

more.quote:
So Śukadeva Gosvāmī is saying, "Mukunda-liṅgālaya-darśane dṛśau." Ambarīṣa Mahārāja lovingly take darśana of the Deity. Actually, we cannot see the vigraha. This is why when we come into the temple don't give praṇāma directly, in front of the Deity. You give praṇāma with the lying down with the left side to the Deity. If you give from the front, it will be one of the sevā-aparādhas. Why? Because when you face someone, you face them because you will look at them. So if you walk up to the Deity and give praṇāma directly, that means, "I've come to look at you." This is sevā-aparādha.

The material eyes cannot see spiritual things. So we approach the Deity and give praṇāma, lying down with the left side to the Deity. We give full daṇḍavat sideways, why? That means, "Oh, my Lord, I cannot see You, but You can see all of me. Here I am. I have come so that You can see me." So if one has this mood, then, after giving praṇāma, one can pray to the Deity. And then, by Kṛṣṇa's sweet mercy, He may show His beauty. Or by the blessing, if we have the blessing, the mercy of a very high-class of Vaiṣṇava, then we may see.

I am remembering once Kṛṣṇa, He was in Dvārakā, and there was a garden made by Viśvakarmā called Nava Vṛndāvana. And there was one deity of Kṛṣṇa, and Kṛṣṇa was walking and He saw the deity, and it was decorated in a wonderful way. The tilaka was all crooked, the garland was like a bit on one side. Kṛṣṇa saw, "This deity has being decorated, it looks like a careless way, but no, it means the person who was decorating the deity was so overwhelmed with love that their hand was trembling when they made the tilaka. They had tears in their eyes when they gave the garland, so they couldn't see whether it was straight or not." So Kṛṣṇa thought, "I want to see that person who decorated this deity of Me.

source.title: love for Guru and Krishna and Shikshastaka Verse 6, bhava, by Shree Prem Prayojan Prabhu

content.content: 7:10 a.m. The small Deities and Tulasī are placed on the altar. Clean floor. Light and offer incense. Offer mirror.
7:15 a.m. Blow conch, open curtain. Offer ⟦cāmara⟧ and peacock fan (not in winter).
7:50 a.m. Make up plate of: Daily sweet 2 piece; halava; kitchari; subji; puris 2 each; milk; water; fruit salad.
8:00 a.m. Close Deity curtain, use small bell during class. Clean tables and floor, set out sitting mats, bring in offering. Remove ⟦Kṛṣṇa⟧'s flute.
8:10 a.m. Breakfast Offering (follow the ⟦bhoga⟧ offering procedure).
8:25 a.m. Offer Deities ⟦ācamanīyaṁ⟧. Remove plates, pick up ⟦asana⟧, replace ⟦Kṛṣṇa⟧'s flute, bring in incense and flower plate for ārati.
8:30 a.m. ⟦Dhūpa-ārati⟧. Open Deity curtain. Offer incense; flowers; ⟦cāmara⟧ and peacock fan (not in winter) 10 mins. Clean altar.

content.quote: So, after receiving dīkṣā from guru, one is allowed to serve the vigraha. Because (^)the deity form of vigraha that (..) in which we see the vigraha, this is the manifestation in this world of the mantropāsanāmayī-līlā-pīṭha. We want to (..) enter into that līlā-pīṭha, but it's hard for us to meditate upon this, because you cannot see it. So, Guru said, “Oh, look, the Vigraha are here.” Now you can see. And even you can do this (..) yoga-pīṭha-sevā. Here is all the paraphernalia that the sakhī is used. So, under guidance of guru-rūpa-sakhī, you should meditate by the way you serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in this līlā-pīṭha, and bring your paraphernalia and do ārati. It includes the devotees doing ārati and those who are also watching; all take part and enter into this līlā-pīṭha. This is why in a temple, morning, noon, and evening ārati, three times a day, all the devotees are going to make this saṁskāra, (^)that gives the impression so that they can meditate on this.

more.quote: Kṛṣṇa reciprocates with everyone. So, the general mood is: "Kṛṣṇa, I am offering one light to You, You offer some light to me." That light by which we can see Kṛṣṇa is prema. So, it is a request for Kṛṣṇa to reciprocate that Kṛṣṇa should give us the light of prema that we can see Him. On a deeper level, (..) darkness is separation and light is meeting. So the more advanced devotee: "(..) Oh, Kṛṣṇa, I feel separation from You. So I am offering You this light. Please offer me the light of that I can meet You." Then, (..) those who have a very mādhurya-mood in rāga-mārga, when they offer ārati to Kṛṣṇa, they are not worshipping like those with aiśvarya-bhāva, who think: "I am offering, worshipping God with the five elements: earth, water, and fire, and air from the fan, water from the conch, earth from the fragrance of the incense, and fire from the dīpa." They don't think like this. This is the aiśvarya-mood. When Kṛṣṇa comes back from taking the cows to graze in the evening, Mother Yaśodā offers ārati to Kṛṣṇa. So, you think that she's worshipping Him? So the ārati ceremony is one type of reception or greeting which is reception which is a very, (..) auspicious. So Mother Yaśodā is offering the dīpas to Kṛṣṇa, thinking: "Oh, I am, whatever inauspiciousness is in Your life, I am removing all this. Whatever problem will come to You, let it come to me and You be happy."

content.content: 11:40 a.m. Pūjārī makes ⟦bhoga⟧ plates.
11:50 a.m. Close Deity curtain, wipe tables with wet cloth. Clean floor. Remove flute, place ⟦asanas⟧, put flower petals on them. Bring in offering plates.
11:55 a.m. Make offering ⟦bhoga⟧ (see offering procedure). Make up full āratī trays: incense; camphor lamp, ghee lamp; water; handkerchief; flowers; ⟦cāmara⟧ and peacock fan (not in winter).
12:25 p.m. Enter altar knocking the door, remove plates, replace flute.
12:30 noon. Blow conch and open curtains. Offer full ārati.
12:55 p.m. Finish ārati.
Sweep and wash the floor.
Close curtains.
Uncover beds.
After this, offer fragrant drinks, ⟦tāmbūla⟧ with camphor, a garland and some flowers. [Or one may simply place a fresh glass of water before the Deities.]
Chant prayers for putting Deities to rest while touching Their lotus feet.

subsections.title: Procedure for Putting the Deities to Rest (Noon)

content.quote: If you serve your deities you can realize this. Vigraha. Because, though Kṛṣṇa, He can do everything Himself, but in the form of vigraha He stands very still. "You have to do everything for Me. You can make Me lie down, make Me stand up, bring Me food." Out of love He's not moving. But in your mind you thinking, "He's not moving because He's made out of metal." Don't think! You're thinking, "Kṛṣṇa's not talking." Why? Because He's remembering Rādhārāṇī, His voice is choked, He cannot say. If you serve your Ṭhākurajī you can realize it.

When they become tired, then the sakhī say, "Now take rest." and then they rest. When the sakhī see that they recovered a little bit, they say, "Oh, now you your tiredness has gone away and now again play. So the sakhī are just telling them to do everything.

3:40 p.m. Make offering (see offering procedure).

content.quote:
So, the cāmara, this cāmara-sevā, so beautiful! Why is this cāmara-sevā so beautiful? Sometimes they don't even do the cāmara-sevā with a cāmara, they just open their hair and do it with their braids. And this cāmara-sevā is so beautiful because the cāmara has thousands and thousands of hairs. So, this cāmara or the braid represents (^)there are 72,000 nāḍīs in the body, you know, according to Vedānta-sūtra, there are 72,000 nāḍīs, they're the channels through which all your prāṇa moves. So, the mañjarīs are thinking, "This cāmara, all these hairs, these are my 72,000 nāḍīs, and I am serving Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa with all my prāṇas."

[…]

These are the signs of the emperor. There may be (..) many kings, but only the emperor and the empress, (^)the king and queen of the world are allowed to have the white cāmara and the white parasol. So, when the mañjarīs, they take the white cāmara and they fan Rādhikā... Ah!

[…]

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura said if someone has abhimāna, that is a pride, so proud, "I am so proud to be the dāsī of Rādhikā," then they very easily attain Kṛṣṇa. Nothing to do, there's nothing to do to attain Kṛṣṇa. He'll be included in that like a free gift, (..) if someone just has the pride in the greatness of Rādhikā. So, this cāmara-sevā is just the hearts of the mañjarīs are exploding. Rādhikā is the empress of Vṛndāvana. There was the coronation, so (..) the rāja-abhiṣeka of Rādhikā when She became Vṛndāvaneśvarī. So proud of this. So, this is done with a great abhimāna.

more.quote:
So every evening, when we do Gaura-ārati, it's not just one of those (..) rituals that the Hare Krishnas do, but rather Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura and our ācāryas are inviting us to participate in a very intense meditation upon the Māyāpura yoga-pīṭha. That is the point of entry into Gaura-līlā, the mantrōpāsanāmayī-līlā-pīṭha of the Gaura-līlā. And then, by meditating deeply upon that, then what will be the results? It's the udbodhaka-līlā. So when the Gaura-ārati comes to an end, what happens? The whole Māyāpura-līlā-pīṭha transforms and becomes

[…]

One becomes transported from the Māyāpura-līlā-pīṭha, yoga-pīṭha, to the Vṛndāvana yoga-pīṭha of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. And this is the purpose, and necessity, and power, and potential of our Gaura-ārati that we perform everyday. Very wonderful, profound, mystic ceremony allowing the living entities to log on to the very (..) inconceivable, inscrutable, almost impossible to realize pastimes of Kṛṣṇa through the mantrōpāsanāmayī-līlā-pīṭha of the yoga-pīṭha in Māyāpura. This is the meaning of Gaura-ārati.

So when you worship Mahāprabhu alone, or whether you worship Gaura-Nitāi, you should always think Mahāprabhu is with the Pañca-tattva, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, and all their associates, because always worship is going on (..) in the yoga-pīṭha. So yoga-pīṭha means Supreme Lord is there, surrounded by His associates in one layer, two layers, three layers, seven layers, seven āvaraṇas, like that. Because He (..) so the ārati is always related to yoga-pīṭha. So when you worship Mahāprabhu, especially in the evening, it's the sandhyā-ārati on the bank of the Jāhnavī (..) in Māyāpur, Navadvīpa. And Mahāprabhu is golden, and His golden effulgence is spreading out, but this golden effulgence is Rādhārāṇī's effulgence. And that's why when a person has the vision of that, and is touched by that golden effulgence, then because Rādhārāṇī's mood (..) is mahābhāva, and the spreading out of Her effulgence is called yāvad-āśraya-vṛtti, that means Her own mood is spreading out. So by worshipping Mahāprabhu, having darśana, seeing this mood, and being touched by His effulgence during ārati, that means that one is being becoming pervaded with Rādhārāṇī's mood. So that's why it says that Mahāprabhu is distributing the mañjarī mood of the maidservants. How? He's not doing anything, only His effulgence is spreading. That's why Rūpa Gosvāmī said,

So who is singing this song? Rūpa Mañjarī, a very proud citizen of the kingdom of Vṛndāvana, all ready to die for her queen. How proud they are!

"Cāmara ḍulāye." That means Rādhikā is brindan— The cāmara has, oh, thousands and thousands of hairs. So in the same way, in your body, the prāṇa is moving in 72,000 nāḍīs. So the mañjarīs are fanning Rādhikā gently with the cāmara as if they are serving Rādhikā with every one of their 72,000 prāṇas. In rāgānugā-bhakti, those who are serving their Deities like that, and others are trying to, (..), chase away flies. So try to follow the moods of our Gosvāmīs. This service, "Cāmara ḍulāye." "Rādhā-kṛṣṇa-ārati kare cāmara ḍulāye." So beautiful, full of abhimāna. "Rādhikāra dāsī yadi hoy abhimāna, śīghra milāiba tomāye gokula-kān." If a person has the identity, pride in the identity, "I am Rādhikā's dāsī," then Kṛṣṇa is included in that like a free gift.

Nārada sings, but here Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura is saying Nārada can't sing. Why? Because his throat is just choking with love, (..) he's g adagada, not only Nārada, but Śukadeva Gosvāmī and also Lord Śiva. And Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura is seeing this, and therefore we are singing this song and meditating on this amazing explosion of transcendental love in the form of the āratī of (..) Gauracandra in the Navadvīpa yoga-pīṭha. And then, just as our meditation upon (..) the Navadvīpa yoga- , the Māyāpur, sorry, yoga-pīṭha (..) (..) is complete, then what happens?

[…]

All of a sudden, Navadvīpa transforms and becomes (..) Vṛndāvana yoga-pīṭha, and there Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are together and the āratī is being performed by Lalitā and the sakhīs like this. So this is the method by which the followers of Caitanya Mahāprabhu can enter into Vraja-līlā through Gaura-līlā. Gaura premānande! Haribol! So, meditating on the (..) yoga Navadvīpa yoga-pīṭha, let us have a kīrtana, and then we conclude our program this evening. Early evening.

Here, now you understand why he says Vṛndāvaneśvari. Because the white cāmara is actually the emblem of an emperor. Only an emperor is allowed to have a white chattra, umbrella, and white cāmara. So when the mañjarīs have a white cāmara and they're fanning Rādhikā, they are so proud, "Oh, Vṛndāvaneśvari, she is the empress of the forest of Vṛndāvana."

7:25 p.m. Finish ārati.
7:45 p.m. Make offering plate: 1 subji; 2 puris; 1 halava; 1 milk; water; 2 daily sweets.

8:10 p.m. Offer ⟦bhoga⟧.

Undress Deities.
Dress simply with little jewellery.
Small Deities putting to bed.
Bring in and offer kheer and water.
Put Deities to rest with prayers and ⟦mantras⟧.

subsections.title: Procedure for Putting the Deities to Rest (Evening)

content.quote: And then in this verse, Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, he's realizing in his heart, when he puts his deities to take rest at night, "Oh, my Gurudeva as Tulasī Mañjarī made this very beautiful bed. And now Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are reclining there after taking fresh fruits, and I'm massaging the feet of Rādhikā." So what began as following vaidhī-bhakti internally (..) became rāgānugā-bhakti and spontaneous realization.

more.quote: So that boy, his name was Praṇava. So Praṇava was thinking, "I am very sick, but I don't want to tell my mother and father because they'll stop me from doing the sevā in the morning." Well, after some hours because he was in pain, finally he fell asleep. Then, in his dream he saw Gopīnātha. Gopīnātha said, "I'm cold. Why did you not give My blanket tonight?" So then Praṇava woke up. "Oh, Gopīnātha! I forgot to give Your blanket." And quickly he ran into the temple room. And saw the deities of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa were lying on their beds, but he had not given the blanket. And he was crying. And begging, "Oh, please, forgive me." And took a very warm blanket and covered Kṛṣṇa. And then when Kṛṣṇa was warm then his fever went away.

sections.subtitle: Ṣoḍaśopacāra-pūjā

content.quote: Then they made a deity of Kātyāyanī from clay on the bank of the river, here. And they offered 16 articles. And with every article, they were thinking of Kṛṣṇa. When they offered the incense, "O Kātyāyanī-devī, we're offering you this fragrant incense, please offer to our nostrils the fragrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa." "O Devī, we're offering this dīpas, these lights to you, please give us the shining light of the eyes of Kṛṣṇa." Like this, with every article that they're offering, they were begging Kātyāyanī to fulfill their desire to meet Kṛṣṇa.

more.quote:
Rules help us in our spiritual life; if we neglect them, we lose something. But if you just follow rules without knowing why you're doing it, it will also not have a good effect. So everything that we do in bhakti, whether it's putting on tilaka, or bowing down, or offering incense and flowers to Kṛṣṇa, everything has a very deep meaning, so it should not be done mechanically.

[…]

So what benefit is there? If you think, "I'm not going to make any offering. I'll just put some money in the machine." You have to do the bhakti yourself. But doing it, don't be like that machine. One's heart has to be involved in that offering. So the offering has a very deep meaning.

Along with the dīkṣā-mantra, the guru gives some process of arcana, of worship of the deity. And this consists of several things: waking the deity in the morning, putting deity to rest in evening, and offering prasādam, and give the seats, idam āsanam, sprinkling like this, and offer them seats, wash their feet, wash their hands and mouth, and offer them prasādam, etc., as if you're serving a guest in your home, very beautiful.

content.content: Outside the Deity room (Pujari room) perform ācamana and offer obeisances to your spiritual master.
Pujari collects the necessary paraphernalia for the worship of Deities.
To avoid interrupting the worship, see to it that the following items are present before beginning:
Enter in the Deity room, clean the area where you will do the worship and place an ⟦asana⟧ on the floor.
Carry all required paraphernalia into the Deity room.
Place the ⟦asana⟧ in position for performing the worship and, while kneeling, with joined palms (⟦pranama-mudra⟧) chant:

content.sanskrit:
pṛthvi tvayā dhṛtā lokā
devi tvaṃ viṣṇunā dhṛtā
tvaṃ ca dhāraya māṃ nityaṃ
pavitraṃ kuru cāsanam
content.translation: O Mother Earth, O goddess, you support all the world's people, and Lord Visnu sustains you; please be merciful today and support me as I sit to worship the Lord.
content.wbw: pṛthvi — O Mother Earth; tvayā — by you; dhṛtā — supported; lokā — the worlds; devi — O goddess; tvaṃ — you; viṣṇunā — by Lord Viṣṇu; dhṛtā — are supported; tvaṃ — you; ca — and; dhāraya — support; māṃ — me; nityaṃ — always; pavitraṃ — pure; kuru — make; cāsanam — and the seat.

content.content: While thinking of your spiritual master sitting on an ⟦asana⟧ in position for performing the worship, sit on your own ⟦asana⟧.
Arrange the items in such a way that you can easily reach them without touching offered to un-offered items.

Place the bell (on a plate) to your left and place the bathing conch on a stand so you can easily lift and replace it several times. The waterpot, flowers, ⟦candana⟧, and tulasī leaves should be within easy reach.

Use the throw-out pot (⟦visarjanīya-pātra⟧) for offered ācamana and ⟦arghya⟧, or you may pour these liquids into the bathing receptacle (⟦snāna-pātra⟧) if it is a receptacle which has a drain. You may use a second ⟦visarjanīya-pātra⟧ for offered flower petals, cotton swabs, etc.
Bathing towels should be placed on a tray, table or the altar, not on your lap or directly on the floor. This applies to all paraphernalia; nothing should be placed on the lower cloth or the floor.

subsections.title: Requesting the Spiritual Master's and Previous Ācāryas' Blessings (guru-paṅkti-namaskāra)

content.content: Preliminary Worship
Begin the ⟦arcana⟧ of ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧ by seeking the permission and mercy of ⟦Sri Guru⟧ and ⟦Śrī Gaurāṅga⟧:
Chant:

content.sanskrit:
Tvaṁ gopikā vṛṣa-raves tanayāntike ‘si...
Oṁ ajñāna-timirāndhasya...
Nāma-śreṣṭhaṁ manum api śacī-putram atra svarūpaṁ...
Vāñchā-kalpa-tarubhyaś ca...
Maha mantra

content.content: ⟦Śrī Gurudeva⟧ is a confidential servant and an intimate friend (⟦sakhī⟧) of ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧. ⟦Gurudeva⟧ is engaged in the direct service of ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧. Meditating like this and remembering one's incapability, perform ⟦arcana⟧.
Draw the attention of your spiritual master by placing flowers before him while chanting

content.sanskrit: eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ aiṁ gurave namaḥ

content.content: Then, meditating on your spiritual master's service to the previous ⟦ācāryas⟧, show the ⟦praṇāma-mudrā⟧ (joined palms) and pray for his blessings to assist in the worship of the Lord.
Offer ⟦praṇāma⟧ to the ⟦guru-paramparā⟧, situated on the altar, then recite:

content.sanskrit: aiṁ gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to my spiritual master.
content.wbw: aiṁ — bīja-mantra; gurave — to the spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: aiṁ parama-gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to my grand spiritual master.
content.wbw: aiṁ — bīja-mantra; parama-gurave — to my grand spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: aiṁ parameṣṭhi gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to my great grand spiritual master.
content.wbw: aiṁ — bīja-mantra; parameṣṭhi — great-grand; gurave — to the spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: aiṁ śrī guru-paramparāyai namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to śrī guru-paramparā.
content.wbw: aiṁ — bīja-mantra; śrī — glorious, revered; guru-paramparāyai — to śrī guru-paramparā; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: oṁ sarva-gurūttamāya śrī kṛṣṇa-caitanyāya namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to the topmost of all gurus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya.
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; sarva-gurūttamāya — to the topmost of all gurus; śrī — revered; kṛṣṇa-caitanyāya — to Kṛṣṇa Caitanya; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.content: Wash your hands with water from the waterpot.
Sprinkle the flowers with ⟦Samānya-arghya⟧ (holy rivers) water while chanting:

content.sanskrit: oṁ astrāya phaṭ

oṁ puṣpe puṣpe mahā-puṣpe
su-puṣpe puṣpa-sambhave
puṣpe cayavākīrṇe ca
huṁ phaṭ svāhā
content.translation: O flowers, O great and auspicious flowers who have appeared from a budding creeper, may you be purified.
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; puṣpe — O flowers; puṣpe — O flowers; mahā-puṣpe — O great flowers; su-puṣpe — O auspicious flowers; puṣpa-sambhave — who have appeared from a flower; puṣpe — O flowers; cayavākīrṇe — arisen from a budding creeper; ca — and; huṁ — protective bīja-mantra; phaṭ — protective exclamation; svāhā — offering exclamation "svāhā".

content.content: Sprinkle all the paraphernalia lightly with ⟦samānya-arghya⟧ water while chanting:

content.sanskrit: oṁ astrāya phaṭ

content.content: Purifying the bodily elements by identifying oneself as the eternal servant of the servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa

Before ⟦arcana⟧, one purifies oneself by thinking: "By constitution I am an eternal servant of ⟦Śrī Kṛṣṇa⟧, but by some misfortune, I became averse to Him since time immemorial. Having thus identified myself as a material body in this illusory existence and having been trapped in this repeated cycle of birth and death, I was burning in the blazing fire of the threefold miseries. However, by great fortune -- that is, by the mercy of ⟦Sri Guru⟧ -- I have come to understand my identity as a minute, atomic spiritual particle, an eternal servant of ⟦Śrī Kṛṣṇa⟧, completely aloof from the gross and subtle bodies. Now, by the order of ⟦Sri Gurudeva⟧, under his shelter, I have obtained the fortune of serving ⟦Śrī Guru-Gaurāṅga⟧ and ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārījī⟧."

content.sanskrit:
nāhaṁ vipro na ca nara-patir nāpi vaiśyo na śūdro
nāhaṁ varṇī na ca gṛha-patir no vana-stho yatir vā
kintu prodyan-nikhila-paramānanda-pūrṇāmṛtābdher
gopī-bhartuḥ pada-kamālāyor dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ
content.translation: I am not a brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya or śūdra, nor am I a brahmacārī, gṛhastha, vānaprastha or sannyāsī. Being transcendental to this gross and subtle body, I am the servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of the master of the gopīs, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the ultimate shelter of everyone, full of transcendental bliss and an ocean of unlimited nectar. [Padyāvalī 74]
content.wbw: nāhaṁ — I am not; vipro — a brāhmaṇa; na — not; ca — and; nara-patir — a kṣatriya; nāpi — nor; vaiśyo — a vaiśya; na — not; śūdro — a śūdra; nāhaṁ — I am not; varṇī — a brahmacārī; na — nor; ca — and; gṛha-patir — a gṛhastha; no — nor; vana-stho — a vānaprastha; yatir — a sannyāsī; vā — or; kintu — but; prodyan-nikhila-paramānanda-pūrṇāmṛtābdher — of the ocean of nectar, full of rising, unlimited transcendental bliss; gopī-bhartuḥ — of the master of the gopīs; pada-kamālāyor — of the lotus feet; dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ — the servant of the servant of the servant.

content.quote: I am sitting at the lotus feet of my guru. I'm wearing a divyaṁ śrī-hari-mandira-tilakam, beautiful tilaka. Harināma-subhagaṁ, my body is made with sandalwood paste (..) and the holy names, Radheshyam or Gaura Gadadhara or Hare Krishna painted on my body in sandalwood paste. I'm wearing very clean cloth and I'm sitting at the feet of guru and I am overwhelmed with intense enthusiasm to serve. This is called the ātma-jñāna mantra.

source.title: First Aid for Chanting part 1 - 2025-05-03 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote:
But if when you sit down to chant, what do you do? Well, first you do ācamana. Oṁ keśavāya namaḥ, oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ. You do ācamana. And then you pray,

[…]

You do the bhūta-śuddhi mantra. I am not Vaiśya, Kṣatriya, Śūdra, Brāhmaṇa. I am not Brahmacārī, Vānaprastha, Gṛhastha or Sannyāsī. I am just gopī-bhartuḥ pada-kamalayor dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ, servant of the servant of the servant of Gopīnātha. This mantra, bhūta-śuddhi. Then you do the ātma-jñāna, you know all this right? Then you do the ātma-jñāna mantra before remembering Gāyatrī. You have to meditate on the self.

source.title: First Aid for Chanting part 1 - 2025-05-03 - Sri Prem Prayojan

content.sanskrit:
divyaṁ śrī-hari-mandirāḍhya-tilakaṁ kaṇṭhaṁ sumālānvitaṁ
vakṣaḥ śrī-harināma-varṇa-subhagaṁ śrī-khaṇḍa-liptaṁ punaḥ
pūtaṁ sūkṣmaṁ navāmbaraṁ vimalatāṁ nityaṁ vahantīṁ tanuṁ
dhyāyet śrī-guru-pāda-padma-nikaṭe sevotsukaṁ cātmanaḥ
content.translation: I meditate on myself as being surrendered at the lotus feet of śrī guru and possessing great determination to serve him. I meditate on myself, with my forehead adorned with beautiful tilaka, representing the temple of Śrī Hari. I am wearing a beautiful necklace of tulasī beads. My chest is marked with the holy name and anointed with sandalwood pulp. I am dressed in fine and pure cloth, and within, I am constantly absorbed in ever-fresh spiritual sentiments.
content.wbw: divyaṁ — divine; śrī-hari-mandirāḍhya-tilakaṁ — tilaka representing the temple of Śrī Hari; kaṇṭhaṁ — neck; sumālānvitaṁ — adorned with a beautiful necklace; vakṣaḥ — chest; śrī-harināma-varṇa-subhagaṁ — beautified by the letters of the holy name of Śrī Hari; śrī-khaṇḍa-liptaṁ — anointed with sandalwood pulp; punaḥ — moreover; pūtaṁ — pure; sūkṣmaṁ — fine; navāmbaraṁ — fresh cloth; vimalatāṁ — purity; nityaṁ — constantly; vahantīṁ — bearing; tanuṁ — body; dhyāyet — one should meditate; śrī-guru-pāda-padma-nikaṭe — near the lotus feet of Śrī Guru; sevotsukaṁ — eager to serve; cātmanaḥ — and of oneself.

content.content: Note: In brief, before one begins ⟦arcana⟧, one should clean the altar and the paraphernalia. Place the articles in a convenient place. It is important to sanctify the water in the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ with the ⟦mantra⟧ "⟦gaṅge ca yamune caiva...⟧" and to purify flowers with the ⟦mantra⟧ "⟦puṣpe puṣpe mahā-puṣpe...⟧". ⟦Pādya⟧, ⟦arghya⟧ and ⟦ācamanīya⟧ are usually substituted with pure water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧. Similarly, if any item cannot be procured, it can be substituted by meditation and the offering of water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ or conch shell.
While offering the bell a flower petal dipped in ⟦candana⟧, chant:

content.sanskrit: ete gandha-puspe oṁ jaya-dhuani-mantra-matāh svāhā

content.content: Now affix the flower petal to the body of the bell with the ⟦candana⟧. Then ring the bell briefly with your left hand and replace it on the plate, all the while thinking of the bell as a servant of the Lord.
While offering flowers and ⟦candana⟧ to the Lord's bathing conch, chant:

content.sanskrit:
ete gandha-puspe
oṁ hum hum hum namah maha-sankhaya svāhā

content.content: See "⟦Arcana⟧ of ⟦Sri Guru⟧" section.
Then chant the ⟦prema-dhvani⟧ for your spiritual master: ⟦jaya oṁ viṣṇupāda⟧ [name of your spiritual master] ⟦kī jaya⟧.

subsections.title: Worshipping Lord Caitanya and Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa with sixteen upacāras (bāhya-pūjā)

content.content: Meditation on Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma

content.sanskrit:
tato vṛndāvanaṁ dhyāyet paramānanda-vardhanam
kālindī-jala-kallola- saṅgi-māruta-sevitam
nānā-puṣpa-latā-baddha- vṛkṣa-ṣaṇḍaiś ca maṇḍitam
koṭi-sūrya-samābhāsaṁ vimuktaṁ ṣaṭ-taraṅgakaiḥ
tan-madhye ratna-khacitaṁ svarṇa-siṁhāsanaṁ mahat
content.translation: Meditate on a great golden throne studded with jewels within the divine realm of Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma. A place of ever-increasing bliss, Vṛndāvana-dhāma is served by breezes cooled by the touch of the Yamunā's waves and is decorated with various types of flowers, creepers and trees. Its splendour is equal to that of millions of suns, and it is ever free from the six waves of material nature (namely, lust, anger, greed, envy, false ego and illusion).
content.wbw: tato — thereafter; vṛndāvanaṁ — Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma; dhyāyet — one should meditate upon; paramānanda-vardhanam — ever-increasing bliss; kālindī-jala-kallola- — of the waves of the Yamunā's waters; saṅgi-māruta-sevitam — served by breezes that touch them; nānā-puṣpa-latā-baddha- — adorned with various flowers and creepers; vṛkṣa-ṣaṇḍaiś — with groups of trees; ca — and; maṇḍitam — decorated; koṭi-sūrya-samābhāsaṁ — possessing the splendour of millions of suns; vimuktaṁ — free; ṣaṭ-taraṅgakaiḥ — from the six waves of material nature; tan-madhye — within it; ratna-khacitaṁ — studded with jewels; svarṇa-siṁhāsanaṁ — a golden throne; mahat — great.

content.content: Meditation on Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa

content.sanskrit:
dīvyad-vṛndāraṇya-kalpa-drumādhaḥ
śrīmad-ratnāgāra-siṁhāsana-sthau
śrī-śrī-rādhā-śrīla-govinda-devau
preṣṭhālībhiḥ sevyamānau smarāmi
content.translation: In the shining land of Śrī Vṛndāvana, in a temple composed of jewels, Śrī Rādhā-Govinda are seated on an effulgent throne beneath a kalpa-vṛkṣa tree, accepting service from Their beloved sakhīs. I meditate upon Them. [Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi-līlā 1.16]
content.wbw: dīvyad-vṛndāraṇya-kalpa-drumādhaḥ — beneath a kalpa-vṛkṣa tree in shining Śrī Vṛndāvana; śrīmad-ratnāgāra-siṁhāsana-sthau — seated on a splendid throne in a temple of jewels; śrī-śrī-rādhā-śrīla-govinda-devau — Śrī Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Govindadeva; preṣṭhālībhiḥ — by Their beloved sakhīs; sevyamānau — being served; smarāmi — I meditate upon.

content.sanskrit:
sat-puṇḍarīka-nayanaṁ meghābhaṁ vaidyutāmbaram
dvi-bhujaṁ veṇu-vaktrābjaṁ vana-mālinam īśvaram
divyālaṅkāraṇopetaṁ sakhībhiḥ pariveṣṭitam
cid-ānanda-ghanaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ rādhāliṅgita-vigraham
content.translation: I meditate on Śrī Kṛṣṇa (seated on the jewelled throne), who possesses beautiful lotus eyes, whose bodily hue resembles that of a fresh raincloud, who wears a yellow silken dhotī, who has two arms, who plays the flute, who wears beautiful forest garlands, who is adorned with glittering ornaments, who is surrounded by the gopīs, who embraces Śrīmatī Rādhikā and whose body is composed of transcendental consciousness and bliss.
content.wbw: sat-puṇḍarīka-nayanaṁ — possessing beautiful lotus eyes; meghābhaṁ — whose bodily hue resembles a fresh raincloud; vaidyutāmbaram — wearing yellow silken garments; dvi-bhujaṁ — two-armed; veṇu-vaktrābjaṁ — playing the flute with His lotus mouth; vana-mālinam — wearing beautiful forest garlands; īśvaram — the Supreme Lord; divyālaṅkāraṇopetaṁ — adorned with divine glittering ornaments; sakhībhiḥ — by the gopīs; pariveṣṭitam — surrounded; cid-ānanda-ghanaṁ — whose body is composed of transcendental consciousness and bliss; kṛṣṇaṁ — Śrī Kṛṣṇa; rādhāliṅgita-vigraham — whose body is embraced by Śrīmatī Rādhikā.

content.sanskrit:
śrī kṛṣṇaṁ śrī-ghana-śyāmaṁ
pūrṇānanda-kalevaram
dvi-bhujaṁ sarva-deveśaṁ
rādhāliṅgita-vigraham
content.translation: I meditate on Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose bluish-black colour resembles that of a fresh raincloud, whose body is full of transcendental bliss, who has a two-armed form, who is the Lord of all the demigods and who is embraced by Śrīmatī Rādhikā.
content.wbw: śrī — Śrī; kṛṣṇaṁ — Kṛṣṇa; śrī-ghana-śyāmaṁ — whose bluish-black colour resembles a fresh raincloud; pūrṇānanda-kalevaram — whose body is full of transcendental bliss; dvi-bhujaṁ — who has a two-armed form; sarva-deveśaṁ — the Lord of all the demigods; rādhāliṅgita-vigraham — whose form is embraced by Śrīmatī Rādhikā.

content.quote: Actually, when a pūjārī, the priest who is serving the deity, offers any articles to the deity, actually, he should offer the articles first by in the mind. And so, he's thinking, "Oh, in my svarūpa with my guru-rūpa-sakhī, my Gurudeva in Her svarūpa, and I am passing the articles and together we are serving Rādhikā." So when you do ṣoḍaśopacāra-pūjā, worship with 16 articles, each one is done by mind first, and then the actual physical article is done.

source.title: Sri Radhastami part 2 - 2024-09-11 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: So, all these phrases like upacāra and pūjā indicate vaidhi-bhakti. Vaidhi-bhakti. There's no pūjā in rāgānuga-bhakti. If someone serves the Deity in rāgānuga-bhakti, it's not called pūjā; it's called sevā. It's different.

content.content: After meditating in this way, chant ⟦Śrī Śrī Gāndharvikā-Giridhārī Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārījī kī jaya⟧ three times. First perform worship within the mind (⟦mānasa-pūjā⟧), and then, with external items, perform worship of the Divine Couple -- in the form of the Deity. Offer each item first to Lord ⟦Śrī Kṛṣṇa⟧, then ⟦Śrīmatī Rādhārānī⟧.
Reception
While ringing a bell, chant:

content.sanskrit: eṣa puṣpāñjali klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Offer flower petals to Their Lordship's lotus feet.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ āsanaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.content: Offer an ⟦āsana⟧ for Their Lordships to sit on. Escort Them to the place of worship with a gesture of your hands. Offer a flower dipped in ⟦candana⟧ into the ⟦snāna-pātra⟧ for the purpose of offering an ⟦āsana⟧.

content.sanskrit:
svāgataṁ su-svāgatam klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām
namaḥ

content.content: With joined palms welcome Their Lordships and see to Their comfort.

content.sanskrit:
etat pādyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.content: Offer ⟦padya⟧ water to wash Their Lordships' lotus feet.

content.sanskrit: idaṁ arghyam klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Offer ⟦arghya⟧ to Their Lordships in Their hands so that They can sprinkle it over Their heads.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.content: Offer Their Lordships water for sipping.

content.sanskrit: eṣa madhuparkaḥ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Offer cups of ⟦madhuparka⟧ to Their Lordships.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ punar-ācamanīyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Again, offer water for sipping.
Bathing and Dressing

⟦Mūrti-śuddhi⟧: carefully remove the Deities' clothes and ornaments being careful not to scratch or harm Them in any way. Do not drag the clothes across Their faces. Cleanse Their Lordships with a soft cloth or sponge dampened with warm water, wiping off the ⟦candana⟧, tulasī leaves, and so on.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ sugandha-tailam klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Massage Their Lordships with fragrant oil.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ snānīyam klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Bathe Their Lordships by pouring water from the conch (filling it at least three times with water) while ringing the bell and chanting the ⟦Brahma-saṁhitā⟧ and other appropriate prayers.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ aṅga-vastram klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Dry Their Lordships with soft cloths.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.content: Offer Their Lordships water for sipping.

content.sanskrit: idaṁ vastram klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Offer fresh clothing to Their Lordships. (dhoti)

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Offer Their Lordships water for sipping.

content.sanskrit: idaṁ upavītam klīṁ gaurāya svāhā klīṁ kṛṣṇāya namaḥ

content.content: Offer ⟦upavīta⟧ to Lord ⟦Caitanya⟧ and ⟦Sri Kṛṣṇa⟧.

content.sanskrit: idaṁ tilakam klīṁ gaurāya svāhā klīṁ kṛṣṇāya namaḥ

content.content: Offer ⟦ūrdhva-puṇḍra tilaka⟧ to Lord ⟦Caitanya⟧ and ⟦Sri Kṛṣṇa⟧ before putting on upper cloth.
Note: When offering ⟦tilaka⟧ you may also chant the names of ⟦Viṣṇu⟧, as when applying ⟦tilaka⟧ on yourself: ⟦oṁ keśavāya namaḥ⟧ for the forehead, etc.

content.quote: Simple service. If you are a pūjārī and you serve the Deities, then every day then you have to take the jewelry and put the jewelry on the Deities, even in vaidhī-bhakti. But those who are in rāga-mārga, they also decorate the Deities every day, but remembering these beautiful verses, like Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī: kiṁ te syamantaka-maṇiṁ taralīkaromi(32). "When will I place this beautiful jewel as the main pendant on your necklace around your neck, like this?" But this is a bhāva-sevā, bhāva-sevā. That means it's not only dressing, but dressing Rādhikā in such a way that She becomes inspired, She's (..) inflamed with more and more desires to serve Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

content.quote: Ucchiṣṭa means remnant. If Gurudeva is eating, then what is left on his plate, this is ucchiṣṭa, and the disciple wants to take the ucchiṣṭa, the remnant of Gurudeva. But the actual desire of taking the ucchiṣṭa is: "Oh, Gurudeva, when will you give me your ucchiṣṭa-sevā, the remnant of your service to Rādhikā?" So, this prayer, śrī-rūpa-mañjarī-karārcita-pāda-padma, is (..) very sweet, because Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī is praying for the ucchiṣṭa-sevā of his śikṣā-guru, Rūpa Gosvāmī. It is extraordinarily beautiful and sweet because it is the extremity of ānugatyamayī-sevā, being in ānugatya. Not only to serve under the guidance, but actually to take up the remnant of the very service. So, this is the picture of rūpānuga-bhajana.

more.quote: He said, "Out of all the types of suffering, actually there's no suffering, only one thing is suffering. What is that? Separation from the Vaiṣṇava." When we don't have the chance to be with Vaiṣṇava, we have no chance to see Vaiṣṇava, we have no chance to give mahā-prasāda to any Vaiṣṇava, to serve any Vaiṣṇava, when no one will accept our service, we don't have the chance to hear the hari-kathā of Vaiṣṇava and do kīrtana with Vaiṣṇavas, then, oh, this is the only suffering, there's no other suffering, and this is the greatest suffering.

content.content: Chant the ⟦aparādha-śodhana mantras⟧ (Prayers Begging Forgiveness for Offences).

content.quote: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself had said, "Oh, don't serve Me first, serve your Gurudeva first. Worship your Gurudeva first, and then after that, you can worship Me. If you do this, then there's no doubt you'll attain siddhi, you'll become perfected. But if one does not worship his Gurudeva first, then everything is niṣphala, has no fruit at all." Why? Because we cannot trespass, we cannot force our way into the divine realm. Everything is by permission, by permission only. So first, we seek permission from Gurudeva to serve Gaurāṅga, and then we seek permission from Gaurāṅga to serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Only when They open the door to divine, (..) divine plane and accept us as Their near and dear one, as Their associate, then we can enter, otherwise not, by our own power it is completely impossible.

more.quote: which means that we want to be the servant of our Gurudeva, and Gurudeva is serving Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī and they serve Śrī Rādhā, so we should be the servant of the servant of the servant. This element is included in our arcana. This mood is included in our arcana, how we serve the deities.

And at that time, those who are dāsīs, the maidservants of Śrīmatī Rādhikā. Then suddenly they open their eyes and sit up in anxiety. In great anxiety. Why? This is the first emotion of the morning, anxiety. Did I oversleep? Did I miss my service? Did Rādhā Krishna already wake up? And they was not there to serve them. So the first thing, as soon as the devotee opens his eyes, ah, anxiety. So then, (..) the maid servants of the Rādhā and Krishna, they quickly get up and the also, he thinks, oh, his guru rūpaki. He goes and wakes up also guru rūpaki. Don't go to Rādhā Krishna alone. And so then that devotee, in his spiritual form, along with guru in his spiritual form, they quickly get up and they go to see, did Rādhā Krishna wake up yet or not? Did we miss our service?

more.quote: Guru is direct manifestation of Supreme Lord, and (..) Rūpa Gosvāmī said that all the aṅgas of bhakti can be practiced in relation to Guru also. But there's some vyāvahārika consideration as well. And there'll be some For example, the (..) pūjārī every day, he's undressing the Deity and then giving bath, and but Guru himself is doing all these things. No need for the disciples to the give the shower to Gurudeva and everything (..) Okay, when Mādhavendra Purī was very old, Īśvara Purī had to do these things. But generally speaking, (..) how you would serve the Deity, you will not serve Kṛṣṇa like that. (..) And (..) then there are some considerations that you can put tulasī on Kṛṣṇa's feet, but (..) you cannot even offer tulasī directly to Guru. You can give Gurudeva Kṛṣṇa's mahā-prasāda tulasī, or if (..) the tulasī is not mahā-prasāda, you can put it in Gurudeva's right hand for him to offer to Kṛṣṇa as a service like that. So (..) all the aṅgas of bhakti can be performed in relation to Guru and Vaiṣṇavas, but there's some also depend (..) some nuances. Certain things you can do and not do, or you have to do them in a different way, because Guru is a category, Vaiṣṇava is a category, Kṛṣṇa Mahāprabhu is a category, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Though Mahāprabhu Himself is Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, but you can serve Him as the Kṛṣṇa Himself, but higher than that is to serve Him as a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, because that's His own mood. Then you're serving Him according to His own mood. So one person will put tulasī (..) you can put tulasī on the feet of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. But in rāgānugā-bhakti, we'll put the tulasī in His right hand, because we serve Him according to His own mood. Just like in Purī, when Mahāprabhu was cleaning the Guṇḍicā temple, one devotee came (..) and poured water on His feet and drank the caraṇāmṛta while He was on the altar of Lord Jagannātha before Lord Jagannātha had arrived there. Mahāprabhu became angry. So inwardly He was pleased, because there's nothing wrong, because He is Kṛṣṇa Himself. That's okay. (..) But He Himself, His mood is, "I am a devotee," and we don't want to (..) disturb that. So Kṛṣṇa wears a peacock feather, but we should not give a peacock feather to Caitanya Mahāprabhu. So (..) and Gurudeva is the sākṣād-dhari, but you don't give Gurudeva a peacock feather or a flute or anything like this. So in principle, the aṅga of bhakti is the same (..) but there are some considerations according to tattva and according to rasa also. Gaura-premānande hari haribol!

content.content: Keeping this conception within the heart, one should worship ⟦śrī gurudeva⟧ according to one's capacity, with sixteen articles.

⟦Śrī Gaurasundara⟧ is sitting on a jewel-studded altar at the ⟦Yogapīṭha⟧ in ⟦Māyāpura⟧, which is part of the transcendental realm of ⟦Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma⟧. ⟦Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu⟧ is standing to His right side, ⟦Śrī Gadādhara⟧ to His left, ⟦Śrī Advaita Prabhu⟧ is standing before Him with folded hands, and ⟦Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita⟧ is standing behind Him, holding an umbrella. [Just below the jewelled altar of ⟦Śrī Gaurasundara⟧, there is another altar, upon which ⟦śrī gurudeva⟧ is sitting.]
Offer ⟦praṇāma⟧ to the ⟦guru-paramparā⟧, situated on the altar to the left of the deity, then recite:

content.sanskrit: aiṁ gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to my spiritual master.
content.wbw: aiṁ — bīja-mantra; gurave — to my spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.translation: I offer obeisances to my grand spiritual master.
content.wbw: aiṁ — bīja-mantra; parama-gurave — to my grand spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: aiṁ parameṣṭhi gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to my great grand spiritual master.
content.wbw: aiṁ — bīja-mantra; parameṣṭhi — great grand spiritual master; gurave — to the spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: aiṁ śrī guru-paramparāyai namaḥ

content.wbw: aiṁ — bīja-mantra; śrī — revered, auspicious; guru-paramparāyai — to the guru-paramparā; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: oṁ sarva-gurūttamāya śrī kṛṣṇa-caitanyāya namaḥ

subsections.title: Mantra to meditate on Śrī Gurudeva

content.sanskrit:
prātaḥ śrīman navadvīpe
dvi-netraṁ dvi-bhujaṁ gurum
varābhaya-pradaṁ śāntaṁ
smaret tan nāma-pūrvakam
content.translation: In the early morning, chant śrī gurudeva's name while remembering him as being situated in Śrī Navadvīpa or Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma, and as possessing two eyes and two arms. He bestows fearlessness and is the embodiment of peacefulness.
content.wbw: prātaḥ — early in the morning; śrīman — glorious; navadvīpe — in Śrī Navadvīpa; dvi-netraṁ — possessing two eyes; dvi-bhujaṁ — possessing two arms; gurum — śrī gurudeva; varābhaya-pradaṁ — bestowing boons and fearlessness; śāntaṁ — the embodiment of peacefulness; smaret — one should remember; tan — him; nāma-pūrvakam — with his name first.

content.content: After reciting this ⟦mantra⟧, say the name of one's own ⟦śrī gurudeva⟧ three times, saying '⟦jaya⟧!' after each time. First worship ⟦śrī gurudeva⟧ within the mind (⟦mānasa-pūjā⟧). Then, pray for his mercy and worship him with the external items, while reciting the ⟦guru-mantra⟧ received at the time of ⟦dīkṣā⟧.

content.quote: Only offering a pile of flowers will not do. The flower is a symbol. The flower is very soft and fragrant. So, our heart should be very soft and fragrant like a flower. Fragrance means emanating so many loving moods. So, flower has no power to offer itself. But if the flower is in the hand of Śrī Guru, he can offer to the Deities. So, with an affectionate heart, we understand that we cannot move closer to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. But rather, if we offer our affectionate heart into the hand of Śrī Guru, then he can offer us to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. So, this is the meaning of offering a puṣpāñjali on Vyāsa-pūjā day.

more.quote: When a pūjārī is worshiping his Iṣṭadeva, then what does he do? First of all, eṣā puṣpāñjaliḥ, and offers the flowers. So when Kṛṣṇa comes here to Govardhana, then the flowers fall from the trees and offered at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.
Esha pushpanjali. First I have to give flowers, then offer the asana, then invite the deity to sit down, to wash their feet. Give them the offer them argya and madhuparka like this.

content.content: While offering the following articles, meditate that, having called upon ⟦śrī gurudeva⟧ to sit in the ⟦snāna-pātra⟧, one is bathing him.

content.translation: Place tulasī in his right hand. [If necessary, use candana to make it adhere.]

content.sanskrit: eṣa dhūpaḥ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
content.translation: (13) dhūpa (incense) — Offer water to signify incense.
content.wbw: eṣa — this; dhūpaḥ — incense; aiṁ — bīja-mantra; gurave — to the guru; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: eṣa dīpaḥ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
content.translation: (14) dīpa (ghee lamp) — Offer water to signify a ghee lamp.
content.wbw: eṣa — this; dīpaḥ — dīpa (ghee lamp); aiṁ — bīja-mantra; gurave — to the guru; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ naivedyaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
idaṁ pānīyaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
idaṁ punar ācamanīyaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
content.translation: (15) naivedya (foodstuffs) — Offer foodstuffs, water, and ācamana.
content.wbw: idaṁ — this; naivedyaṁ — foodstuffs; aiṁ — bīja-mantra; gurave — to the guru; namaḥ — obeisances; idaṁ — this; pānīyaṁ — water; aiṁ — bīja-mantra; gurave — to the guru; namaḥ — obeisances; idaṁ — this; punar — again; ācamanīyaṁ — water for ācamana; aiṁ — bīja-mantra; gurave — to the guru; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ tāmbūlaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
idaṁ mālyaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
idaṁ sarvaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
content.translation: (16) mālya (garland) — Offer tāmbūla, garland, and all remaining items.

content.content: After this, chant ⟦guru-gāyatrī⟧ ten times and offer him prayers and obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
tvaṁ gopikā vṛṣa-raves tanayāntike 'si
sevādhikāriṇi guro nija-pāda-padme
dāsyaṁ pradāya kuru māṁ vraja-kānane
śrī rādhāṅghri-sevana-rase sukhinīṁ sukhābdhau
content.translation: O Gurudeva! You are immersed in an ocean of bliss and you can award transcendental service. You are a dear most gopikā of Śrīmatī Rādhikā. Please bestow upon me the shelter of your lotus feet, so that I can be blissfully engaged in the transcendental service of the Queen of Vraja, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
