content.content: Obeisances to Śrī Gurudeva

content.sanskrit:
oṁ ajñāna-timirāndhasya jñānāñjana-śalākayā
cakṣur unmīlitaṁ yena tasmai śrī-gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer my most humble daṇḍavat-praṇāma to śrī guru, who has opened my eyes, blinded by the darkness of ignorance, with the torchlight of knowledge.
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; ajñāna-timirāndhasya — of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance; jñānāñjana-śalākayā — with the torchlight of knowledge; cakṣur — the eyes; unmīlitaṁ — opened; yena — by whom; tasmai — to him; śrī-gurave — to śrī guru; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
rādhā-sammukha-saṁsaktiṁ
sakhī-saṅga-nivāsinīm
tvām ahaṁ satataṁ vande
mādhavāśraya-vigraham
content.translation: O spiritual master, I continually offer my obeisances unto you, who are always in the presence of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and very much devoted to Her. You always reside in the association of Her confidantes, the gopīs, and you are the abode of loving devotion to Śrī Mādhava.
content.wbw: rādhā-sammukha-saṁsaktiṁ — very much devoted to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; sakhī-saṅga-nivāsinīm — always residing in the association of Her confidantes, the gopīs; tvām — unto you; ahaṁ — I; satataṁ — continually; vande — offer my obeisances; mādhavāśraya-vigraham — the abode of loving devotion to Śrī Mādhava.

content.sanskrit:
nāma-śreṣṭhaṁ manum api śacī-putram atra svarūpaṁ
rūpaṁ tasyāgrajam uru-purīṁ māthurīṁ goṣṭhavāṭīm
rādhā-kuṇḍaṁ giri-varam aho rādhikā-mādhavāśāṁ
prāpto yasya prathita-kṛpayā śrī-guruṁ taṁ nato 'smi
content.translation: I bow down to the beautiful lotus feet of my spiritual master, by whose causeless mercy I have obtained the supreme holy name, the divine mantra; the service of the son of Sacīmātā; the association of Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara, Rūpa Gosvāmī, and his older brother, Sanātana Gosvāmī; the supreme abode of Mathurā; the blissful abode of Vṛndāvana; the divine Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Govardhana Hill; and the desire within my heart for the loving service of Śrī Rādhikā and Mādhava in Vṛndāvana.
content.wbw: nāma-śreṣṭhaṁ — the supreme holy name; manum — the divine mantra; api — also; śacī-putram — the son of Sacīmātā; atra — here; svarūpaṁ — Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara; rūpaṁ — Rūpa Gosvāmī; tasyāgrajam — his older brother, Sanātana Gosvāmī; uru-purīṁ — the great city; māthurīṁ — Mathurā; goṣṭhavāṭīm — the blissful abode of Vṛndāvana; rādhā-kuṇḍaṁ — divine Rādhā-kuṇḍa; giri-varam — Govardhana Hill; aho — oh; rādhikā-mādhavāśāṁ — the desire for loving service to Śrī Rādhikā and Mādhava; prāpto — I have obtained; yasya — by whose; prathita-kṛpayā — renowned causeless mercy; śrī-guruṁ — the beautiful lotus feet of my spiritual master; taṁ — to him; nato — bowing down; 'smi — I am.

content.content: Obeisances to the Vaiṣṇavas

content.sanskrit:
vāñchā-kalpa-tarubhyaś ca kṛpā-sindhubhya eva ca
patitānāṁ pāvanebhyo vaiṣṇavebhyo namo namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to the Vaiṣṇavas, who, just like desire trees, can fulfil the desires of everyone and who are full of compassion for the conditioned souls.
content.wbw: vāñchā-kalpa-tarubhyaś — to the desire trees that fulfil desires; ca — and; kṛpā-sindhubhya — to the oceans of compassion; eva — indeed; ca — and; patitānāṁ — of the fallen conditioned souls; pāvanebhyo — to the purifiers; vaiṣṇavebhyo — to the Vaiṣṇavas; namo — obeisances; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.content: Mahā-mantra

content.sanskrit:
hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare
hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare

content.quote:
...and I am assisting him. So, just like Dhyānacandra Gosvāmī in the Rādhākānta Maṭha, in the Gambhīrā, actually has a Deity of his Gurudeva. And he would bring the Deity... and sit the Deity where actually... think he's the Deity is doing offering. So even today Gopāla Guru Gosvāmī sits on his āsana, and when it's time for the bhoga offering, the pūjārī picks up the Deity, carries him, and he does the pūjārī does everything, but the idea is that Gopāla Guru Gosvāmī is doing it. So that mood is there.

[…]

So this is the, um, ceremony for offering mahā-prasāda correctly for those who have the second initiation, because it's the beginning of the mānasī-sevā. That you're actually serving Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. It's not that, uh, you get the food and you're giving and sending by a delivery very far away. But no, you are there in the kuñja with Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and you are serving them with guru in the sakhī form, and other sakhīs as well. So it's beginning the internal services, manifested through the expression of arcana.

source.title: Darshan of Śrī Prem Prayojan Prabhu on offering bhoga, Vrindavan
source.note: recording of Satkirti prabhu; transcript in the project archive

more.quote: Now the mantra that we use, this is important. If you have Deity of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, but no Gaurāṅga, but you should still think Gaurāṅga is there. We never worship Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa without Mahāprabhu first. And, uh, if you have Gaurāṅga, then you think that Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa is there. And you this, so the mantra is this, you hear: Eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ. So this mantra it's there on your sheet. So it's a combined it combines the mantra to Gaura and the man- and mantra to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in one. Though you are on the level of vaidhī-bhakti, though we are teaching vaidhī-bhakti, we are teaching the vaidhī-bhakti in such a way that it's one-pointed, it will turn into rāgānugā-bhakti. Because in the in the ordinary vaidhī-bhakti, you do the offering to Gaurāṅga, and a separate offering to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. But because we are going one-pointed to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and seeing Gaurāṅga as our śikṣā-guru, so we don't make a separate offering. Or you can think that, uh, Mahāprabhu is the rasarāja-mahābhāva-svarūpa, the combined form of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa when Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in the prema-vilāsa-vivarta. He's a prema-vilāsa-vivartamayi mūrti. So only one mantra, not separate mantras. That's pure vaidhī-bhakti. So you're doing vaidhī-bhakti, but the vaidhī-bhakti you are learning is exactly focus to enter very smoothly into rāgānugā-bhakti.

source.title: Darshan of Śrī Prem Prayojan Prabhu on offering bhoga, Vrindavan
source.note: recording of Satkirti prabhu; transcript in the project archive

more.quote:
So you should be meditating, while you're doing the, uh, the when you're making offering, that Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa come, they sit down and they're actually eating everything. Right?

[…]

So now Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, they've eaten, they've washed, they've taken the tāmbūla, and they're happy.

source.title: Darshan of Śrī Prem Prayojan Prabhu on offering bhoga, Vrindavan
source.note: recording of Satkirti prabhu; transcript in the project archive

more.quote: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura said, "Mahāprabhu is the most merciful incarnation of the Supreme Lord, but He will not accept even water from a person who does not chant 64 rounds." This is why we don't offer bhoga to Kṛṣṇa. We pray, "Gurudeva, you please offer this bhoga to Kṛṣṇa and I will assist you." Then, Mahāprabhu will accept.

source.title: Festival of Jagannātha Miśra - 2024-03-25 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote:
So, then what can you do? Because guru is giving Harinam and dīkṣā and then you have to offer your food to Krishna. So that means we don't offer the bhoga to Krishna. We pray, oh Gurudeva, I am not qualified to offer this bhoga to Krishna. You please offer this bhoga and I am here as your assistant in this sevā. So all the arcana to the deity is done under (..) in the ānugatya, under the guidance of guru because Gurudeva and our paramparā, they are janting (..) lakhs harinam for many, many years.

So, in this way, Krishna will accept the offering if it's done according to vidhi and in the ānugatya of śuddha-vaiṣṇavas.

Then how can any disciple take praśādam? Because the praśādam is not offered by you, it's offered by guru. Right? You take the picture of guru and you take (..) the bhoga, the naivedya, and you pray Gurudeva, I am not qualified, Gurudeva, you please offer this to Krishna, I am your assistant.

"Give Me some water, but with love. A flower, some fruit, a leaf—tulasī leaf." These things are inexpensive and available everywhere. Yet if we can offer this to Kṛṣṇa with whatever devotion we can muster in the heart. Or especially the advanced devotee—they feel, "I have no bhakti." So they will tell, "Kṛṣṇa, please accept, may You be pleased. I have no love. I am offering this that my Gurudeva will offer it to You. So You must accept, because my Gurudeva is offering, and I am only assisting my Gurudeva. So surely You will accept."

content.content: The procedure for offering foodstuffs (⟦bhoga⟧) is the same throughout the day.

The devotee should consider himself fallen and unworthy, not qualified to offer ⟦bhoga⟧ to the Lord, but should pray to ⟦Gurudev⟧, knowing that he is a worthy servant. One should offer ⟦asana⟧ to ⟦Gurudev⟧ and call out to him: "Please offer this ⟦bhoga⟧ to the Deities you worship." (We ask the ⟦Guru⟧ to offer food to ⟦Rādhā⟧ and ⟦Kṛṣṇa⟧, but we do not offer it for him to eat).

Although the ⟦guru⟧ offers food, the disciple, while chanting the ⟦mantras⟧, meditates on being helped by him. The ⟦gaura-mula-mantra⟧ is always chanted along with the ⟦mula-mantra⟧ of ⟦Śrī Śrī Rādhā Kṛṣṇa⟧, even when the ⟦vigraha⟧ of Lord ⟦Caitanya⟧ is not present.
We should offer the ⟦bhoga⟧ with a feeling that ⟦śrī gurudeva⟧ himself is offering the ⟦bhoga⟧ to ⟦Śrīman Mahāprabhu⟧ and ⟦Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧.

content.quote:
So, um, even here it's described how to offer flowers to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, invite them to come on the seat, and wash their hands and feet. So, but, uh, I'd like to add something which is not here. It's, but it's a very simple thing, and a basic thing. And that is that you do this ceremony first to guru.

[…]

Then you take, and then you offer them: eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ aiṁ gurave namaḥ. Offer the puṣpāñjali at the feet of Gurudeva. Then you take an āsana. So usually they have like this, some small seats. Um, if you only have pure Deities, it's okay, you can do by mind to guru, but if you have for guru, you can also use. So then, uh, ringing the bell and place the āsana in front of Gurudeva: idam āsanaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ. Then, uh, inviting Gurudeva: āvāhayāmi, that means come, and then sit down, sthāpayāmi, and then welcome: prabhu kṛpayā svāgataṁ kuru. Āvāhayāmi sthāpayāmi prabhu kṛpayā svāgataṁ kuru. And you meditate that from the picture of Gurudeva or the Deity of, he is coming now and sitting on the āsana. Understand? Now Gurudeva is there.

source.title: Darshan of Śrī Prem Prayojan Prabhu on offering bhoga, Vrindavan
source.note: recording of Satkirti prabhu; transcript in the project archive

more.quote:
And then and now this start begins here. So, um, you should, uh, remove the flute of Kṛṣṇa and, uh, do the same thing: eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ...

[…]

So first: eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ. You offer the flower. Then you offer the āsana: idam āsanaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ. Then you invite them to come and take their seat: āvāhayāmi sthāpayāmi prabhu kṛpayā svāgataṁ kuru. Then ringing the bell and taking the ācamana, you wash their feet: etat pādyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ. And you offer water three times to the feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Then you wash their hands and mouth: idam ācamanīyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ. And three times you drop the water in the visarjana-pātra.

source.title: Darshan of Śrī Prem Prayojan Prabhu on offering bhoga, Vrindavan
source.note: recording of Satkirti prabhu; transcript in the project archive

more.quote:
Then you take a small conch which is on the tripod on the on the tripod, the three legs.

[…]

Don't, uh, drown everything in water. It's just some tiny drops, that if during the time of making the preparations, there were some faults, there was some impurity, any anything like this, it has to be removed before offering to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. So, then, a, uh, idam you sprinkle the water, and as you're sprinkling, you say very softly: idam naivedyaṁ sa-tulasī-pānīyājalaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ. "I am offering this naivedya, bhoga, along with, uh, tulasī leaves and some water." Like this. And then you put your hand over the top of the offering and your other hand covering that. You can also cover with your cloth, don't dip it in the dāl. So, you cover your hand like this and you remember Gopāla-mantra eight times. Eight times, okay?

source.title: Darshan of Śrī Prem Prayojan Prabhu on offering bhoga, Vrindavan
source.note: recording of Satkirti prabhu; transcript in the project archive

more.quote:
And then you come out from the Deities' room, and then you sit, and you remember the Kāma-gāyatrī ten times and Gaura-gāyatrī ten times.

[…]

So then, by the time you finish your mantras, ten minutes or so have gone by, then you come back into the Deities' room and clap your hands three times above the offering, and then you take it off the altar.

source.title: Darshan of Śrī Prem Prayojan Prabhu on offering bhoga, Vrindavan
source.note: recording of Satkirti prabhu; transcript in the project archive

more.quote:
Now this, uh, um, uh, plate with the mahā-prasāda of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, before you can give to anyone, you have to distribute to the prominent personalities. So then with the pañca-pātra, you take and you hold at the mouth of Gurudeva, picture of guru is on the altar: idam mahā-prasādam aiṁ gurave namaḥ, and drop it. And then again you hold, and you meditate that you're giving to your guru-paramparā. Who are the guru-paramparā? They're all the sakhīs. Idam mahā-prasādam oṁ sarva-sakhībhyo namaḥ.

[…]

The plate you can take, put the preparations back into the pots, mix with what was not on the altar, everything becomes mahā-prasāda. Wash Kṛṣṇa's plate, put it away, and then you can distribute to all the Vaiṣṇavas.

source.title: Darshan of Śrī Prem Prayojan Prabhu on offering bhoga, Vrindavan
source.note: recording of Satkirti prabhu; transcript in the project archive

more.quote: He is offering his bhoga to Śrī Kṛṣṇa every day. Or first offering flowers at the feet of Gurudeva, and inviting Gurudeva, "Please, take your seat," and washing the lotus feet of Gurudeva, and then praying for permission to offer that bhoga to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, offering flowers at Their lotus feet, offering Them an āsana to sit, and requesting His deities, "Please come and be seated," washing the lotus feet of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, washing Their hands and mouth, offering the bhoga with tulasī leaves. He is doing this every day. In his heart he is relishing joy, realizing how Gurudeva in the form of a very dear priya-sakhī of Rādhikā, or maidservant of Rādhikā, Gurudeva is there and under the guidance of that maidservant of Rādhikā, they are actually serving Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are enjoying their offerings.

And that means that when the devotee is making the offering to Kṛṣṇa, if that devotee is not feeling distressed, then Kṛṣṇa he'll you he will not realize Kṛṣṇa's friendship. In other words, when that devotee puts the bhoga in front of Kṛṣṇa and prays, "Oh Kṛṣṇa, I have made this for You, please accept My offering." "If You will not accept what I've made for You, then what is the use of being alive?" Feeling pain in the heart if Kṛṣṇa will not accept. So when the devotee is so eager to serve Kṛṣṇa in this mood, then Kṛṣṇa becomes hungry. Otherwise Kṛṣṇa is not hungry, He's Bhagavān, He's ātmārāma, āpta-kāma, all of His desires are fulfilled. He's maintaining all of the universes. He doesn't need our bhoga offerings. But when the devotee is ārta, feel suffering, feeling separation, "Kṛṣṇa, please accept this, if You don't accept, my life is useless," then Kṛṣṇa is ārta-bandhu, He's the friend of that devotee. And when the devotee makes the offering, his eagerness to serve Kṛṣṇa causes Kṛṣṇa suddenly to feel a empty stomach. And the food looks very delicious to Him. Then, when Kṛṣṇa takes that offering of His devotee, Kṛṣṇa feels satisfaction. And yasmin tuṣṭe jagat tuṣṭam, when the Supreme Lord is pleased, then the jīva becomes the soul becomes pleased. So, premnaiva bhakta-hṛdayaṁ sukha-vidrutaṁ syāt. When the offering is made with love, then the devotee's heart melts with happiness. Why? Because the eagerness to serve Kṛṣṇa makes Kṛṣṇa's hunger. If you're not hungry, you'll not enjoy eating. So because Kṛṣṇa's hungry, He enjoys the offering, and when Kṛṣṇa feels happiness, then the soul is automatically happy. So the happiness of the devotee lies in the happiness that Kṛṣṇa feels.

So at that time, Rādhikā is watching from a balcony through a lattice window. Because only the wife has the opportunity to cook, (..) and give that food to her husband, and then watch and relish how her husband is relishing. But Rādhikā is having the same feeling, but because this is parakīya, it is hidden, so She's watching from a balcony and relishing how Kṛṣṇa is relishing Her cooking. And the maidservants of Rādhikā, they're watching Rādhikā, how Rādhikā is watching Kṛṣṇa relish. When Kṛṣṇa tastes the preparations, then in these preparations all the feelings, all the thoughts that Rādhikā was having while She was cooking, they appear in Kṛṣṇa's heart. So cooking is a very intimate service. Kṛṣṇa's body is made of that which Rādhikā has made with Her own hand.

So bhakti should not be done only mechanically, following the rules and regulations, but one's heart should be in it, one should be very attentive, and there should be some bhāva—that means offered with feeling. Kṛṣṇa is called bhāva-grāhī Janārdana; means actually it's not the thing that you're offering that He takes, but it's the feeling that you offer it with—that's what He's relishing. If you cook some food for Kṛṣṇa, maybe you're not the best cook in the world, it doesn't taste that good, but if you offer it with feeling, Kṛṣṇa will taste your feelings. He's not thinking, "Oh, great potatoes today." He's not interested in your potato; it's the loving feeling with which you're making the offering. So niyamāgrahaḥ means you spoil your bhakti when you do the activities of devotion in a mindless way without your emotional involvement.

And what about Caitanya Mahāprabhu? Someone can say, “If I have to be one-pointed to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, then what about Caitanya Mahāprabhu?” Caitanya Mahāprabhu is our bhajana-śikṣā-guru. So Caitanya Mahāprabhu is our bhajana-śikṣā-guru, you are worshiping Him by following His instructions to completely focus on Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. This is the bhajana-praṇālī for those who are in rāgānugā-bhakti. In vaidhi-bhakti, they offer bhoga like one plate for Kṛṣṇa, for Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and one plate for Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. And different separate mantras for offering. But in rāgānugā-bhakti, one plate for Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and then that mahā-prasādam you can offer to bhajana-śikṣā-guru Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu. So... Or you can have one mantra with Mahāprabhu and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa together. Mahāprabhu is distinct and non-different, Mahāprabhu is Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa combined. Gurudeva... And Gurudeva, when you are serving Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, then Gurudeva is also there serving Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and under her guidance... So by this verse, Śrī Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī is showing how to be one-pointed to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, but including the service of Guru and Gaurāṅga.

source.title: Sri Prem Prayojan - 2018-01-09 - What Sadhu-Sanga can give

content.content: First purify yourself by performing ācaman by reciting the following ⟦mantras⟧:

content.sanskrit: oṁ keśavāya namaḥ
oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ
oṁ mādhavāya namaḥ

content.content: Make ⟦bhoga⟧ plates.
Close Deity curtains, wipe tables with wet cloth.
Clean floor.
Remove crown and flute, place ⟦asanas⟧, put flower petals on them.
Bring in offering plates.
While ringing the bell and chanting the following ⟦mantras⟧, invite Deities to ⟦āsanaṁ⟧. Offer ⟦puṣpāñjali⟧ (a few flower petals) at the lotus feet of each deity:

content.sanskrit:
eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

idaṁ āsanaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: Offer āsana (a seat).
content.wbw: idaṁ — this; āsanaṁ — āsana, seat; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation “svāhā”; śrīṁ — bīja-mantra; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
etat pādyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: Offer pādya (washing the lotus feet).
content.wbw: etat — this; pādyaṁ — pādya, water for washing the lotus feet; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation “svāhā”; śrīṁ — bīja-mantra; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: Offer ācamana (sipping water).
content.wbw: idaṁ — this; ācamanīyaṁ — water for ācamana; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation “svāhā”; śrīṁ — bīja-mantra; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ naivedyaṁ sa tulasī pānīya jalam klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: Offer naivedya with tulasī and water.
content.wbw: idaṁ — this; naivedyaṁ — naivedya offering; sa — with; tulasī — tulasī; pānīya — drinking; jalam — water; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation “svāhā”; śrīṁ — bīja-mantra; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.content: Place a Tulasī leaf on each dish offered. Hold the right hand over the ⟦bhoga⟧ plate, place the left hand on top of the right hand and repeat the ⟦gopāla-mantra⟧ 8 times.
Come out of the Deity room. Chant the ⟦gaura-gāyatrī⟧ ten times as well as the ⟦kāma-gāyatrī⟧ ten times and wait for some time for the Lord to take His meal.
After some time pujari knocks on the door and enters the Deity room. Invite the Deities to rinse their mouths with the following ⟦mantras⟧:

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: Offer mouthwash.
content.wbw: idaṁ — this; ācamanīyaṁ — water for rinsing the mouth; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation “svāhā”; śrīṁ — bīja-mantra; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ tāmbūlaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: Offer tambula (betel).
content.wbw: idaṁ — this; tāmbūlaṁ — tāmbūla, betel preparation; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation “svāhā”; śrīṁ — bīja-mantra; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ āsanaṁ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā
śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: Offer āsana (a seat).
content.wbw: idaṁ — this; āsanaṁ — seat; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation "svāhā"; śrīṁ — bīja-mantra; klīṁ — bīja-mantra; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

subsections.title: Offer mahā-prasād to Gurudev and others

content.quote: So for pure devotees tasting mahā-prasāda is very ecstatic. Because, when Rādhikā is cooking, then all Her ecstatic love goes into those preparations. And when Kṛṣṇa tastes that, then what Rādhikā was feeling appears in His heart. And then He has new love for Rādhikā. Then (..) when Kṛṣṇa's remnants are taken back to Rādhikā... And Rādhikā tastes the remnant of Kṛṣṇa... Then She has a sphūrti, She has a realization... Of what Kṛṣṇa was realizing... When He was realizing what Rādhikā was realizing when She was cooking. So in this way, through mahā-prasādam, there is very beautiful meeting of the hearts of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. And then, when the mañjarīs, they take the remnant of Rādhikā... Then they realize what Rādhikā was realizing, when She was realizing what Kṛṣṇa was realizing, when He was realizing what She was realizing when She was... So in this mood we take prasādam. Then you are really, actually honoring prasādam and not just eating like feeding time at the farm.

more.quote: Why is Rūpa Gosvāmī saying, oh, this is essential teaching, six exchanges of love and affection with Vaiṣṇavas. Why? Because by serving, by giving something, by receiving something, by opening the heart in confidence, inquiring confidentially, by the preparing the bhoga and offering to Rādhā and Krishna and giving mahā-prasādam, and also taking some remnant from the Vaiṣṇava. Then these are the various ways in which the Hlādinī-śakti is transferred to a jīva who is weak and has no power to overcome the anarthas, especially the final anartha, pratiṣṭhā.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ mahā-prasādaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ
idaṁ mahā-prasādaṁ oṁ sarva sakhibhiyo namaḥ
idaṁ mahā-prasādaṁ oṁ vrindayai namaḥ
idaṁ mahā-prasādaṁ oṁ paurnamasyai namaḥ
idaṁ mahā-prasādaṁ oṁ sarva vaiṣṇavebhyo namaḥ
idaṁ mahā-prasādaṁ oṁ sarva vaiṣṇavībhyo namaḥ
idaṁ mahā-prasādaṁ oṁ sarva vrajavāsībhyo namaḥ

content.content: Then at the end, after the offering, we meditate that your spiritual master, where appropriate, are taking the remnants both in ⟦Kṛṣṇa-līlā⟧ and ⟦Gaura-līlā⟧ after all the associates have taken.
After the food offering, while singing the Holy name of the Lord in a mood of servitude, clean the Deity room with water. Then clean the paraphernalia used in the worship of the Lord.
After the ⟦bhoga⟧ offering, place the crown and flute back on the Deities, open Deity curtains and perform ārati.
Note: It should be understood that by the mercy of the spiritual master, we are able to engage in the service of the Lord in His ⟦Arcā-vigraha⟧, like offering ⟦bhoga⟧.
Other variations

⟦idaṁ naivedyaṁ⟧
⟦idaṁ pānīya-jalam⟧
⟦idaṁ anna-vyañjana-pānīyādikaṁ sarvaṁ⟧
⟦idaṁ miṣṭānna-pānīyādikam⟧

content.quote: We say this mantra as we take caraṇāmṛta. Oh, it destroys all kleśa, it destroys all of our sins, śuddha-bhakti-dam, and causes the appearance of pure devotion, the sphūrti of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and the sphūrti of all the pastimes, of the various cosmetics that were transferred from the body of Kṛṣṇa to the body of Rādhikā, and from the body of Rādhikā to the body of Kṛṣṇa, all these cosmetics of the beautiful pastimes have been washed into this caraṇāmṛta, and it can manifest those beautiful pastimes.

more.quote: If a person thinks that the water that has washed the lotus feet of the deity or the water that has washed the lotus feet of a Vaiṣṇava is ordinary water. Because when the ingredients are offered in pūjā to the Supreme Lord, then the same thing happens, the spiritual energy manifests there. And so caraṇāmṛta of the deity and caraṇāmṛta of Vaiṣṇavas. It is aprākṛta, supernatural. Even though it looks like ordinary water to the material senses.

So a pure devotee, when they taste a tulasī leaf, when they take Ṭhākurjī's caraṇāmṛta, when they take Mahāprasādam, then it has unlimited power and two things happen, the sphūrti of Krishna and the sphūrti of love for Krishna at the same time immediately. This is honoring Mahāprasādam.

source.title: Q&A Prasadam, Chaturmasya and Japa - 2025-04-05 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: So when he would do abhiṣeka of the Deity, and then the tulasī would wash off Kṛṣṇa's feet and into the caraṇāmṛta, then he would take caraṇāmṛta and become absorbed in remembering Kṛṣṇa's pastimes with Vraja-gopīs. All the vastu, all the substances connected with Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His Deity are actually connected to His pastimes. This is why the pure devotee is eager to taste some prasādam, some tulasī leaves, to smell the flowers, because it has a spiritual power to awaken the realization of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes.

content.content: Sanskrit term ⟦Caraṇāmṛta⟧ meaning "the nectar of the feet." It refers to the sacred water or liquid that has been used to wash the feet of a deity, spiritual master, or saint. It is considered highly purifying and spiritually potent, imbued with divine blessings.

content.sanskrit:
akāla-mṛtyu-haraṇaṁ
sarva-vyādhi-vināśanam
viṣṇoḥ pādodakaṁ pītvā
śirasā dhārayāmy aham
content.translation: I drink the water from the lotus feet of Śrī Viṣṇu, which destroys all diseases and removes the chance of untimely death, and I also take that water on my head.
content.wbw: akāla-mṛtyu-haraṇaṁ — which removes untimely death; sarva-vyādhi-vināśanam — which destroys all diseases; viṣṇoḥ — of Śrī Viṣṇu; pādodakaṁ — water from the lotus feet; pītvā — having drunk; śirasā — on the head; dhārayāmy — I take; aham — I.

subsections.title: Mantra for honouring the caraṇāmṛta of Śrī Gurudeva

content.sanskrit:
aśeṣa-kleśa-niḥśeṣa-kāraṇaṁ śuddha-bhakti-dam
guroḥ pādodakaṁ pītvā
śirasā dhārayāmy aham
content.translation: I drink the water from the lotus feet of śrī gurudeva, which bestows pure bhakti and which causes the destruction of unlimited miseries and pains. I also take that water on my head.
content.wbw: aśeṣa-kleśa-niḥśeṣa-kāraṇaṁ — the cause of the destruction of unlimited miseries and pains; śuddha-bhakti-dam — bestowing pure bhakti; guroḥ — of śrī gurudeva; pādodakaṁ — the water from the lotus feet; pītvā — having drunk; śirasā — on my head; dhārayāmy — I place; aham — I.

subsections.title: Mantra for honouring the caraṇāmṛta of Śrī Gaurāṅgadeva

content.sanskrit:
aśeṣa-kleśa-niḥśeṣa-kāraṇaṁ śuddha-bhakti-dam
gaura-pādodakaṁ pītvā
śirasā dhārayāmy aham
content.translation: I drink the water from the lotus feet of Śrī Gaurasundara, which bestows pure bhakti and which causes the destruction of unlimited miseries and pains. I also take that water on my head.
content.wbw: aśeṣa-kleśa-niḥśeṣa-kāraṇaṁ — that which causes the destruction of unlimited miseries and pains; śuddha-bhakti-dam — bestowing pure bhakti; gaura-pādodakaṁ — the water from the lotus feet of Śrī Gaurasundara; pītvā — having drunk; śirasā — on my head; dhārayāmy — I take and place; aham — I.

subsections.title: Mantra for honouring the caraṇāmṛta of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa

content.sanskrit:
śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādodakaṁ
prema-bhakti-daṁ mudā
bhakti-bhareṇa vai pītvā
śirasā dhārayāmy aham
content.translation: The water from the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa is the source of pure bhakti to Them. Having drunk that water with great joy and devotion, I also take that water on my head.
content.wbw: śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādodakaṁ — water from the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; prema-bhakti-daṁ — the giver of pure bhakti; mudā — with great joy; bhakti-bhareṇa — with great devotion; vai — indeed; pītvā — having drunk; śirasā — on the head; dhārayāmy — I take and place; aham — I.

content.quote: How blissful it was (..) to do the abhiṣeka of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. By doing the abhiṣeka, that means showering Kṛṣṇa, then everyone felt that they were abhiṣikta, that means they themselves, they were taking shower in amṛta. Anyone can experience this. If you do abhiṣeka of Kṛṣṇa's deity or you do abhiṣeka of your own deities, then though you are showering Kṛṣṇa, you feel yourself as if your heart is being showered with nectar.

more.quote: Abhiṣeka means (..) bathing ceremony, and this is done at different times. A person may be bathed in Vedic culture when they graduate from the gurukula, when they're studying in the school of their spiritual master; when they graduate, there's a bathing ceremony to indicate that they are snāta. (..) Snāta means (..) bathed in knowledge. So to indicate that they are bathed in knowledge, there's a bathing ceremony: guru bathes the disciple, and then he leaves and goes to his home. So another bathing is at the time of a wedding. But (..) the biggest bathing ceremony is a coronation. When a young prince is about to become the king, or a princess is about to become the queen, then they have a spectacular abhiṣeka, bathing ceremony. Conch shells are blowing, cāmaras are waving, fans are waving, and there's massaging fragrant oils, and then fragrant water, and milk, and yogurt, and ghee, and sugar, and honey, and fruit juice, and all kinds of delicious things. And then after that they're dried, and then decorated, painted with pictures in sandalwood, candana, and kastūrī musk, and decorated with beautiful cloth and ornaments, flowers and jewels, and then there's āratī. So we are doing this, the coronation abhiṣeka of Śrī Rādhā.

source.title: Radha-Tattva, part 2, Sri Prem Prayojan Prabhu

more.quote: But on Janmāṣṭamī, though we may not have a realization of our constitutional position, everyone can experience that at the time when we make the abhiṣeka to Kṛṣṇa, and we just try to please and satisfy Kṛṣṇa, suddenly we feel complete satisfaction, and all our senses become blissful, and there's no feeling of the, (..) insufficiency or deficiency at all. And then every devotee, even any new person who doesn't know anything, who comes here and celebrates Janmāṣṭamī today, they can practically have this realization, that I am part and parcel of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and (..) only by giving happiness to Kṛṣṇa, I can experience complete happiness myself.

content.content: Before the ⟦abhisheka⟧ begins, ask the assembled devotees to chant ⟦Kirtan⟧, warn ⟦Kirtaniyas⟧ that during the beginning and end of the ⟦abhisheka⟧ the ⟦Kirtan⟧ should be loud.
Prepare all paraphernalia (wash and dry beforehand):

Jugs for liquids
Large container for ⟦charinamrita⟧
Table for ablution, ⟦Snana Vedi⟧
Deity stand
Conch shells for bathing
Dowel, ⟦Sahasra-dhara⟧
Fruit garlands
Stands and mats
Paper napkins for hands
Ācamana, ⟦chamara⟧ and bell
Tray with 9 wicks and 9 bases (made of dough - flour, milk, sugar) arranged in lotus shape decorated with flowers, ⟦Pishta-pradipa⟧
A mixture of dried banana powders (1), rice flour (1), flour (0.5), barley flour (1) urad dal flour (1) and ⟦kunkum⟧, ⟦sindur⟧ (1)
Purification brush
A bowl of fresh Tulasī leaves
Cup with sandalwood paste
Petals of 5 kinds of flowers, ⟦Pushpa⟧
Prepare the liquids:

⟦Madhuparka⟧ in a cup with a spoon
Fragrant oil, ⟦Tailam⟧
A mixture of ground sesame (sesame) with water, ⟦Tila-udvartanam⟧
Boil milk (3 liters) and let it cool down
Yogurt (3 liters) at room temperature, whisk to a smooth liquid
Ghee butter (50 mm), melted
Honey (0.5 L), melted, can be mixed a little with water
Sugar syrup (2-3 L, boil 1 liter of water / 18 scoops of sugar) at room temperature
Sweet juices (3-4 liters)
Water (5-6 liters) at room temperature
Coconut water (or fresh coconuts)
Rose water (1 liter)
Add tulasī to all the ingredients for ⟦abhisheka⟧.
In the pujari room (behind the closed curtains of the altar), change the Deities into ⟦gamchas⟧ and put on day garlands.
Purification of the paraphernalia (dravya-śuddhi)
Lightly sprinkle water from the ācaman on the paraphernalia and repeat:

content.sanskrit: oṁ astrāya phaṭ

content.content: Preparation of Snana vedi
Wash and decorate the ⟦Snāna vedi⟧, the place of bathing well with cloths, fruits and flowers.
Draw a ⟦Goloka yantra⟧ at the place where the Deities will be bathed and offer flowers and Tulasī to the place where the Deities will stand.
Bell worship (ghanta-puja)
Offer flower petals with sandalwood paste to the bell ringer and repeat:

content.sanskrit: ete gandha-puspe oṁ jaya-dhuani-mantra-matāh svāhā

content.content: Attach the flower petal to the body of the bell with a ⟦chandana⟧. Then ring the bell lightly with the left hand and place it on the plate, while thinking of the bell as a servant of the Lord.
Worship of the Conch shell (sarkha-puja)
Offer flower petals with sandalwood paste to the shell and repeat:

content.sanskrit:
ete gandha-puspe
oṁ hum hum hum namah maha-sankhaya svāhā

content.content: Open the curtains of the altar, ringing the bell and trumpeting the conch shells, escort the Deities to ⟦Snana vedi⟧.
Offer:

content.sanskrit:
esa puspanjalih...
idaṁ āsanaṁ...
etat pādyaṁ...
idaṁ arghyam...
idaṁ acamaniyam...
esa madhuparkah...
idaṁ punar-acamaniya...

content.content: Welcome arati - Pista dipa
By ringing the bell and trumpeting the conch shells, offer ⟦Pista-pradipah⟧ to the Deities.
Massage
Remove the flower garlands from the Deities.
Rub the Deities with oil (⟦idaṁ sugandha-tailam...⟧).
Then rub the Deities with sesame paste 3/4 (⟦idaṁ tila-udvartanam...⟧).
Wash the Deities with water and sesame paste through the sink 1/4 (⟦idaṁ til-snaniyam...⟧).
Offer fruit garlands to the Deities (⟦idaṁ phala-malayam...⟧).
Panchamrta snana

Milk (⟦idaṁ ksira-snaniyam...⟧)
Yogurt (⟦idaṁ dadhi-snaniyam...⟧)
Ghee (⟦idaṁ ghrta-snaniyam...⟧)
Honey (⟦idaṁ madhu-snaniyam...⟧)
Syrup (⟦idaṁ sita-snaniyam...⟧)
Powders
Using a cow's tail as a brush, apply a mixture of powders on the Deities.
Clean the Deities with a brush.
Wash the Deities with plain water (⟦idaṁ jala-snaniyam...⟧).
Phalam
Bathe the Deities with fruit juices (preferably 5 sweet kinds) (⟦idaṁ phala-snaniyam...⟧).
Sugar powder
Using a cow's tail as a brush, apply sugar powder on the Deities.
Clean with a brush.
Wash with plain water (⟦idaṁ jala-snaniyam...⟧).
Gandha
Cover the Lord's body with Sandal paste (⟦idaṁ gandha...⟧).
Bathe with water diluted with sandal paste (⟦idaṁ gandha-snaniyam...⟧).
Sahasrada dhar Showers
Offer pure water through a shower (⟦idaṁ sahasrada-snaniyam...⟧).
Concluding activities
Wipe the Deities with towels and wrap Them (⟦idaṁ anga-vastram...⟧).
Sprinkle with petals from 5 kinds of flowers (⟦idaṁ puspa-snaniyam...⟧).
Offer ācaman (⟦idaṁ acamaniyam...⟧).
By ringing the bell and blowing the conch shells, escort the Deities to the pujari room.
Recite the ⟦mantras⟧ of forgiveness for offenses.
Remove everything from the place of bathing.
In Pujari room clean, bath and dress the Deities.
Offer ⟦Bhoga⟧ plate and Arati to the Deities.

⟦Śrī Śrī Guru-Gaurāṅga Gāndharvikā-Giridhārī Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārījī kī jaya⟧!
⟦Oṁ viṣṇupāda aṣṭottara-śata śrī rūpanugācārya Śrī Prema Prayojana Prabhu⟧

content.quote: Aparādha-sahasra-bhājanam, "Oh Hari, I am very offensive, I am guilty of thousands and thousands of offenses, and I am fit to be punished. I am drowning in this fierce ocean of material existence. I am completely lost. Please make me Your own, ātmasāt kuru." Ātmasāt kuru. That means ātmasāt means that. (..) "I am Yours. I am not independent from You. I am completely dependent on You. May my heart be one with Your heart, ātmasāt. You have promised to deliver anyone who takes shelter of You. Therefore, please deliver me."

source.title: Bhajana Rahasya part 6 - 2021-06-07 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: So with a great honor and with great repentance we give praṇāma and take the water of this Govinda-kuṇḍa upon our head praying, "Oh Govinda, oh Kṛṣṇa, please forgive my offenses and engage me in the service of Your lotus feet."

content.quote: In rāga-mārga, one has to follow the associates. What is the mood of the sakhīs when they are offering ārati to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa? You see, even Mother Yaśodā, when Kṛṣṇa returns in the evening from taking the cows to graze, Mother Yaśodā and all the elderly mothers, they also offer ārati to Kṛṣṇa. So it cannot be because they think He's God. So (..) there's another meaning to ārati. Ārati is a reception when you receive someone, you welcome them in this way. But the bhāva of the, when a person is offering ārati, is that, "Oh my beloved, more dear to me than my prāṇa, whatever obstacles may come—you have overcome so many obstacles to be here together—but in the future if any obstacles will come due to fate, then let all those problems, let all those obstacles, may all those difficulties fall on my head, but let you be free from all inconveniences. You should not suffer." So when the sakhīs are offering ārati to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, it is, they're offering their own lives. This is a gesture that, "You should be happy, you should not have any problem, you, no ill-fate should come to you. Whatever ill-fate was meant to come to you, it should come to me instead, but let you be happy." This is the meaning of (..) the mood of ārati in Vraja, whether Mother Yaśodā is offering or whether Lalitā and the sakhīs are offering to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. It's such an expression of love.

source.title: Specialities of Vrindavana Lila - 2023-01-15 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: I remember once my Gurudeva was on parikramā and he was meeting with one of his godbrothers. And this godbrother, he saw that Śrīla Gurudeva, he was having a pastime of some illness, but at the same time he was preaching and inspiring people all over the world. Whereas that godbrother, out of his humility, he was thinking, "I am not doing such service. I cannot inspire others, but I am quite healthy." So then when he was speaking, he said, "Oh, I am praying to Kṛṣṇa that whatever is left of my life and my health, oh, let it be taken away and give it to my godbrother, Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, so that he will be health and preach everywhere." Very sweet, (..)? So if the sādhakas in this world can have such a feeling for each other of love, then what to speak of the sakhīs in Vṛndāvana? Such selfless prema. So jaya jaya rādhā-kṛṣṇa yugala-milana, all the obstacles are over. Ārati karaye lalitādi-sakhī-gaṇa, and may there be no more obstacles. The sakhīs, "We will take everything on us, but let Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa be happy." Because their happiness is our happiness only. There's no separate interest.

source.title: Specialities of Vrindavana Lila - 2023-01-15 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote:
Ārati is one ceremony in Vedic culture. And as devotees coming from Western culture, when we think of ārati, we always think of worship to a Deity. But if we were in Vedic culture, we'll understand that the ceremony of ārati is a very common ceremony performed whenever you welcome someone for whom you have love or respect. So, for example, Mother Yaśodā would offer ārati to Kṛṣṇa. It is said for the when we offer ārati it is for the (..) those who are in vaidhī-bhakti, if they are worshiping God by the ārati, they're thinking, "Oh, this is fire, I've offered fire, water, (..) and earth, and so on. Worshiping God with all the five elements. They are His energy like this." And they think aiśvarya. But in laukika-sad-bandhuvat-sambandha, in an actual (..) friendly relationship, if you offer ārati, the spirit is that this is (..) creating auspiciousness for the person you're offering ārati to. So the mood is that, "Oh, by offering this ārati I am (..) taking whatever problems and difficulties will come in your life, I take them all on my own head, so that you can be happy." So if Mother Yaśodā would offer ārati to Kṛṣṇa, she's thinking, "Oh, whatever difficulties or problems may come in the life of my boy, oh, let me take all those problems on my own head. And if I have done any dharma or good karmas, I am giving it to Him so He will be happy." So the sakhīs, they offer ārati to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and they're thinking, "Oh, whatever obstacles are there to your meeting together, then I want to take all those obstacles on my head, that you will always be able to meet together and never feel separation from each other."

One can think for each article in the ārati ceremony, beginning with the incense and then the ghee wicks, and then the (..) water, and the cloth, a flower, and the cāmara, and fan, you go through this (..) ritual, one can think a different meditation for each article. (..) But not necessarily. Because if when Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa meet in the forest, then Lalitā-sakhī will organize the other sakhīs to offer ārati, and they do it very quickly, only to make auspicious that they get on with their pastimes. So, of course, and in rāgānugā, it may be just (..) they offer ārati and they're just feeling very deeply, overjoyed, that now Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa have come together and we are receiving them, and now their pastimes will begin. It's like very simple. Very easy. It's like if Gurudeva came and sat down here, then we will get ārati paraphernalia and we're not thinking about, (..) this is incense, this is the ghee wick, this is We thinking, "Gurudeva is here!" So for those who have fully entered into rāgānugā-bhakti, how they will feel, it will be spontaneous, their own feeling. Each time, different feeling. But for those who want to enter into rāgānugā-bhakti, they may think if they're offering incense, then they may think, "Oh, I am offering this fragrance to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa." And they meditate that the fragrance of Rādhikā is going into the Kṛṣṇa is taking the fragrance of Rādhikā, and Rādhikā is taking the fragrance of Kṛṣṇa, like this. Then they think, "I'm offering ghee wicks." This (..) light is (..) like meeting because separation is darkness. So when they think, "Oh Rādhikā, I'm offering this light (..) with the deepest desire that you and Kṛṣṇa will always meet and I will my whole life will be dedicated to make sure that you are never parted from her." Oh, we can (..) offer water. In the early morning in the niśānta-līlā, there the kuñja is (..) somewhat dark. So they all have ghee wicks to look, to see how Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa their bodies are covered with the their cosmetics from each other. And so when they offer the water, they can think, "Oh, (..) when will I have the chance to be there and looking with the ghee wicks to see where there are marks on the body of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, then taking water and putting water there, and taking cloth, and because after water they offer the cloth and then wiping, so that when they go home they won't have the very obvious marks." So, these are some meditations. They are examples. Because rāgānugā is very spontaneous.

This is not anything fixed, because śāstra doesn't say anything. So it's natural (..) in vaidhi-bhakti a person follows the rules and regulations. So generally they then they think that if you offer incense, this represents earth, because fragrance is the quality of earth. And then if you offer dip, then this is offering fire, and if you offer a fan, this is air. So they have some aiśvarya, sometimes aiśvarya conceptions like this. But in rāgānugā-bhakti there's no fixed conception, otherwise it would not be rāgānugā-bhakti. Then it will be vaidhi-bhakti again, "Now you have to think like this, now you have to think like this." Rāgānugā-bhakti is (..) spontaneous. Outwardly it looks the same, but inwardly it's according to (..) the taste and the realization of that particular devotee on that day. Yes. Everyone wants to know, "(..) How do I do rāgānugā-bhakti?" you know? Cannot. "How? Please show me how to be spontaneous." "What are the three steps to become to be spontaneous?" You cannot, this is not a question. But wh- when we listen with a from our Gurudeva, here's a spontaneous mood then...

Because it depends on the ārati, if the ārati is maṅgala-ārati, then (..) in the rāgānugā-bhakti the devotee thinks of the niśānta-līlā, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa waking up. So then it's a bit (..) not very light in the kuñja, because only the first morning light of the sun is coming. So if the devotee is offering the dip, then they'll think, "Oh, some maidservants of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are looking with the dip in the dark to see if there any evidence of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa's meeting on their bodies." And then they're giving water to wash it, and then a cloth to wipe it away like this, so when they go home no one will suspect that they were meeting in the night time, like this. So (..) but obviously if you think, "Well, this is what you have to meditate on ārati," then in noon ārati or in the evening ārati, then it's not applicable, because that's applicable only to that time of the day. Also anyway (..) the sakhīs of Rādhikā, like Lalitā, they offer ārati to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, not thinking about any meanings. Why? Because ārati means that (..) to (..) drive away all inauspiciousness. So for example, if Kṛṣṇa is coming back from tending the cows in the day, some demons have attacked or anything, then Mother Yaśodā will come and offer ārati to Kṛṣṇa to remove any inauspiciousness that may you know He may have come in contact with during the day. When Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa meet in the kuñja, then so that Candrāvalī will not try to disturb anything, that Jaṭilā will not come, or Kuṭilā or Abhimanyu or anything, Lalitā is offering ārati to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa to remove any inauspiciousness. Also the mood of the ārati can be that whatever you see success, happiness comes from your piety. So whatever piety, whatever happiness I have (..) this I'm offering to you so that you can be happy. So Mother Yaśodā will do she's Mother Yaśodā is not worshipping Kṛṣṇa that "You are Bhagavān," or anything like that. It's to remove inauspiciousness and offer all her piety that you will have a happy and long and successful life. So then the actual articles, they don't have a meaning in that sense. It's just that the ārati itself (..) is an expression of care, an expression of protection, an expression of (..) wishing the very best for that person.

But in rāgānugā-bhakti, those who are focusing on the attainment of Krishna's service in Vṛndāvana, then they can never think in this way, but rather, they remember how when Radha Krishna wake up, the mañjarīs, the maidservants of Radha Krishna who enter into the kuñja, they are offering ārati. They take the dīps, and they offer ārati to Radha Krishna, and it's not exactly a worship. You see, Mother Yaśodā also offers ārati to Krishna when he returns in the evening from taking the cows to grace. So why would his mother worship him? So that's not the meaning. Ārati means to receive someone or show the expression of love to someone. And the meaning is that when we offer ārti, one of the moods is that whatever difficulty or whatever problem or obstacle is there in your life, may I take that difficulty upon my head and may you be happy. This is why Mother Yośodā offers the dīp to her son. It's not worshipping her son. It's a mood of oh, such selfless love that you should be happy and you should have no difficulties and let all these difficulties come to me. This is (..) the mood of ārti, understand?

Arrange the items in such a way that you can easily reach them without touching offered to un-offered items:

Place the bell on a plate to your left, and place the bathing conch on a stand so you can easily lift and replace it several times.
The waterpot, flowers, ⟦candana⟧, and tulasī leaves should be within easy reach.
Use the throw-out pot (⟦visarjanīya-pātra⟧) for offered ācamana and ⟦arghya⟧, or you may pour these liquids into the bathing receptacle (⟦snāna-pātra⟧) if it is a receptacle which has a drain. You may use a second ⟦visarjanīya-pātra⟧ for offered flower petals, cotton swabs, and so on.
Bathing towels should be placed on a tray, table or the altar, not on your lap or directly on the floor.
Purifying Hands (kara-śuddhi)
Wash your hands with water or smear them lightly with ⟦candana⟧.
Purifying the Flowers (puṣpa-śuddhi)
Sprinkle the flowers with ⟦samānya-arghya⟧ water while chanting:

content.sanskrit: oṁ astrāya phaṭ

oṁ puṣpe puṣpe mahā-puṣpe
su-puṣpe puṣpa-sambhave
puṣpe cayavākīrṇe ca
huṁ phaṭ svāhā
content.translation: O flowers, O great and auspicious flowers who have appeared from a budding creeper, may you be purified.
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; puṣpe — O flowers; puṣpe — O flowers; mahā-puṣpe — O great flowers; su-puṣpe — O auspicious flowers; puṣpa-sambhave — arisen as flowers; puṣpe — O flowers; cayavākīrṇe — covered with clusters of buds; ca — and; huṁ — protective bīja-mantra huṁ; phaṭ — protective exclamation phaṭ; svāhā — offering exclamation svāhā.

content.content: Purifying the Lord’s Paraphernalia (dravya-śuddhi)
Sprinkle all the paraphernalia lightly with ⟦samānya-arghya⟧ water while chanting:

content.sanskrit: oṁ astrāya phaṭ

content.content: Purifying the Bodily Elements (bhūta-śuddhi)

Do ⟦prokṣaṇa⟧ by sprinkling yourself lightly with ⟦samānya-arghya⟧ water while chanting the ⟦Gopāla-mantra⟧ (the sixth guru-given ⟦mantra⟧) once. Recite the following prayers, meditating on their meaning:

"By constitution I am an eternal servant of ⟦Śrī Kṛṣṇa⟧, but by some misfortune, I became averse to Him since time immemorial. Having thus identified myself as a material body in this illusory existence and having been trapped in this repeated cycle of birth and death, I was burning in the blazing fire of the threefold miseries. However, by great fortune -- that is, by the mercy of ⟦śrī guru⟧ -- I have come to understand my identity as a minute, atomic spiritual particle, an eternal servant of ⟦Śrī Kṛṣṇa⟧, completely aloof from the gross and subtle bodies. Now, by the order of ⟦śrī gurudeva⟧, under his shelter, I have obtained the fortune of serving ⟦Śrī Guru-Gaurāṅga⟧ and ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārījī⟧."
With this mood, while meditating on the soul within, recite the ⟦mantra⟧ for purification of oneself. (⟦bhūta-śuddhi-mantra⟧)

content.sanskrit:
nāhaṁ vipro na ca nara-patir nāpi vaiśyo na śūdro
nāhaṁ varṇī na ca gṛha-patir no vana-stho yatir vā
kintu prodyan-nikhila-paramānanda-pūrṇāmṛtābdher
gopī-bhartuḥ pada-kamālāyor dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ
content.translation: "I am not a brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya or śūdra, nor am I a brahmacārī, gṛhastha, vānaprastha or sannyāsī. Being transcendental to this gross and subtle body, I am the servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of the master of the gopīs, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the ultimate shelter of everyone, full of transcendental bliss and an ocean of unlimited nectar." [Padyāvalī 74]
content.wbw: nāhaṁ — I am not; vipro — a brāhmaṇa; na — not; ca — and; nara-patir — a kṣatriya; nāpi — nor; vaiśyo — a vaiśya; na — not; śūdro — a śūdra; nāhaṁ — I am not; varṇī — a brahmacārī; na — not; ca — and; gṛha-patir — a gṛhastha; no — nor; vana-stho — a vānaprastha; yatir — a sannyāsī; vā — or; kintu — but; prodyan-nikhila-paramānanda-pūrṇāmṛtābdher — of the ocean of unlimited nectar, brimming with all supreme transcendental bliss; gopī-bhartuḥ — of the master of the gopīs; pada-kamālāyor — of the two lotus feet; dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ — the servant of the servant of the servant.

content.content: Meditation on the self (ātma-dhyāna-mantra)

content.sanskrit:
divyaṁ śrī-hari-mandirāḍhya-tilakaṁ kaṇṭhaṁ sumālānvitaṁ
vakṣaḥ śrī-harināma-varṇa-subhagaṁ śrī-khaṇḍa-liptaṁ punaḥ
pūtaṁ sūkṣmaṁ navāmbaraṁ vimalatāṁ nityaṁ vahantīṁ tanuṁ
dhyāyet śrī-guru-pāda-padma-nikaṭe sevotsukaṁ cātmanaḥ
content.translation: I meditate on myself as being surrendered at the lotus feet of śrī guru and possessing great determination to serve him. I meditate on myself, with my forehead adorned with beautiful tilaka, representing the temple of Śrī Hari. I am wearing a beautiful necklace of tulasī beads. My chest is marked with the holy name and anointed with sandalwood pulp. I am dressed in fine and pure cloth, and within, I am constantly absorbed in ever-fresh spiritual sentiments.
content.wbw: divyaṁ — divine; śrī-hari-mandirāḍhya-tilakaṁ — tilaka representing the temple of Śrī Hari; kaṇṭhaṁ — neck; sumālānvitaṁ — adorned with a beautiful necklace; vakṣaḥ — chest; śrī-harināma-varṇa-subhagaṁ — beautified with the letters of Śrī Hari’s holy name; śrī-khaṇḍa-liptaṁ — anointed with sandalwood paste; punaḥ — furthermore; pūtaṁ — pure; sūkṣmaṁ — fine; navāmbaraṁ — fresh cloth; vimalatāṁ — purity; nityaṁ — constantly; vahantīṁ — bearing; tanuṁ — body; dhyāyet — one should meditate upon; śrī-guru-pāda-padma-nikaṭe — near the lotus feet of śrī guru; sevotsukaṁ — eager to serve; cātmanaḥ — and one’s own self.

content.content: Note: In brief, before one begins ⟦arcana⟧, one should clean the altar and the paraphernalia. Place the articles in a convenient place. It is important to sanctify the water in the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ with the ⟦mantra⟧ "⟦gaṅge ca yamune caiva...⟧" and to purify flowers with the ⟦mantra⟧ "⟦puṣpe puṣpe mahā-puṣpe...⟧". ⟦Pādya⟧, ⟦arghya⟧ and ⟦ācamanīya⟧ are usually substituted with pure water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧. Similarly, if any item cannot be procured, it can be substituted by meditation and the offering of water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ or conch shell.

This chapter opens the part “Festivals and Vows.” It describes the four-month vow of Cāturmāsya, Kārttika, its final month, and Puruṣottama-māsa—the additional month of the lunar calendar—as they are observed in our lineage. A source is given for each rule. A reference guide with dates for 2026–2046 is provided at the end of the chapter.

subsections.title: What Cāturmāsya Is and When It Is Observed

content.quote: So many persons they begin their Cāturmāsya vrata today, but following Prabhupāda Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, we begin our Cāturmāsya from after four days time on the appearance day of Śrīla Vyāsadeva, Guru Pūrṇimā. Why? Because the final month is Kārtika, that is Dāmodara vrata, and that is the month dedicated to the sevā of Śrīmatī Rādhikā. So the month of Kārtika goes from Pūrṇimā to Pūrṇimā. So if we will begin the our Cāturmāsya on the Ekādaśī, then we'll have to complete the Cāturmāsya on the Ekādaśī but there is still four more days left in the month of Kārtika. Or even though the option (..) has been given to begin on this day, but out of the great honor and desiring, intensely desiring to attain Rādhā dāsyam, the service of Śrīmatī Rādhikā, we will begin our Cāturmāsya vrata from the Guru Pūrṇimā and finish on the Kārtika Pūrṇimā.

source.title: Śayana Ekādaśī & Bhakti Vijñana Bharati Maharaja's Appearance Day - 2025-07-06 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote:
So today is the first day of Cāturmāsya. Four months, beginning today on the Pūrṇimā until the Pūrṇimā at the end of Kārtika. The observance of Kārtika-vrata is described, (..), in the description of the aṅgas of bhakti. But Cāturmāsya is not described. So some persons think we should not observe Cāturmāsya; this is connected to karma. We should observe only Kārtika. However, we are the followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Gauḍīyas, all followers of Śrī Caitanya... We aspire to be Gauḍīyas, the servants of the servants of Gauḍīyas.

So our Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, when He, (..), left Navadvīpa Dhāma and came to Jagannātha Purī, after a few months, He went on the tour of South India. And then He arrived in Śrīraṅgam. When He was there, Cāturmāsya began. So then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He accepted the invitation of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa to stay in his home for the four months of Cāturmāsya. So Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself observed this, (..), vrata, this vow.

content.content: Cāturmāsya (“four months”) is the period of the rainy season and autumn when Lord Viṣṇu rests in yoga-nidrā: He lies down on Śayana Ekādaśī in the month of Āṣāḍha and awakens on Utthāna Ekādaśī in the month of Kārttika. During these months, sannyāsīs cease travelling and remain in one holy place, observing special rules and austerities; each month has its own restrictions (Gurudev, lectures no. 2228, 8 July 2017, and no. 3331, 8 August 2018).

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself observed Cāturmāsya: during His journey through South India, He spent all four months in Śrīraṅgam, at the home of Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa. Therefore, Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas, His followers, observe all four months, not only Kārttika (Gurudev, lectures no. 6557, 13 July 2022, and no. 9183, 10 October 2025).
The Starting Day
Hari-bhakti-vilāsa quotes Sanat-kumāra: the Cāturmāsya vow may be taken on Ekādaśī (Śayana Ekādaśī), on Karkaṭa-saṅkrānti (the Sun’s entry into Cancer), or on Āṣāḍha-pūrṇimā.

content.sanskrit:
ekādaśyāṁ tu gṛhṇīyāt saṅkrāntau karkaṭasya tu
āṣāḍhyāṁ vā naro bhaktyā cāturmāsyoditaṁ vratam
content.translation: One should devotedly take the vow prescribed for Cāturmāsya on Ekādaśī, on Karkaṭa-saṅkrānti, or on Āṣāḍha-pūrṇimā. (Hari-bhakti-vilāsa 15.59; Śyāmācaraṇa Kaviratna edition, p. 948)

content.content: Our lineage begins Cāturmāsya on Guru-pūrṇimā (Vyāsa-pūrṇimā, the full moon of Āṣāḍha) and concludes it on Kārttika-pūrṇimā (Rāsa-pūrṇimā). This was the practice of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura and Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja. Gurudev explains the reason as follows: Kārttika lasts from pūrṇimā to pūrṇimā; if the vow begins on Ekādaśī, it must also end on Ekādaśī, leaving four days of Rādhikā’s month still remaining (lecture no. 9643, 6 July 2025; see “Gurudev’s Mood”). The same rule is given in the Russian edition of Arcana-dīpikā: “Cāturmāsya begins on Vyāsa-pūrṇimā (Guru-pūrṇimā)—approximately the beginning of July—and ends at the end of the month of Kārttika—approximately the beginning of November” (translated from the Russian) (Supplement to the Russian edition, pp. 122–123).

According to the Vaiṣṇava calendar, the months of Cāturmāsya are Śrīdhara (Śrāvaṇa), Hṛṣīkeśa (Bhādra), Padmanābha (Āśvina), and Dāmodara (Kārttika). The calendar months end on pūrṇimā, while in our lineage each successive month of the vow begins on the day of pūrṇimā itself—this is how it is marked in the Caitanya Academy calendar.
Saṅkalpa—Taking the Vow
The vow is taken before the Deity. Hari-bhakti-vilāsa gives the following mantra for this purpose:

content.sanskrit:
caturo vārṣikān māsān devasyotthāpanāvadhi
imaṁ kariṣye niyamaṁ nirvighnaṁ kuru me 'cyuta
content.translation: For the four months of the rainy season, until the Lord awakens, I shall observe this vow. O Acyuta, please make it free from obstacles. (Hari-bhakti-vilāsa 15.59, same edition)

content.content: Why All Four Months

On the first day of ūrjā-vrata in 1959, Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja instructed: “Kārtika-vrata niyama-sevā is a part of cāturmāsya-vrata. Fully mature bhakti, which is the fruit of observing cāturmāsya-vrata, will not develop if one only honours ūrjā-vrata and not the full four months. In fact, this negligence actually reveals disrespect for cāturmāsya-vrata.” (Ācārya Kesarī Keśava Gosvāmī: His Life and Teachings, Moscow, 2004, p. 243; English edition, GVP 2013, p. 151).

content.quote: Now, in this strict performance of Cāturmāsya, for the whole four months, one should not eat tomato, eggplant, the loki, parmal, (..), sesame, honey, etc. Honey. I said. Sesame. So, and but Śrīla A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda, when he came to the West, he thought to introduce everything is will be too much. So, he just gave certain restrictions within each month. So the first month is one should refrain from taking green leafy vegetables: spinach, cabbage, and so on. And, then, yogurt, milk, and urad dāl. In the other months. Śrīla Gurudeva, this was Śrīla Prabhupāda's standard. But my Gurudeva, he insisted all the devotees, especially the devotees who are staying in India, they should follow Cāturmāsya very strictly. And if they're in the West, then they can try as best they can.

more.quote: It means that if you're sick, you don't have to follow all the rules and regulations. And if you're traveling, you don't have to follow all the rules and regulations because it just (..) the things that you need or the things you have to avoid just might not be possible when you're traveling. Just like I remember once it was during (..) Cāturmāsya and we Gurudeva went to Russia for a festival. And (..) it was the month no green leaves. But in Russia at that time, and not (..) and (..) no tomato. In Russia at that time, all they had was basically cabbage and tomatoes. That was like practically all they had. And the festival organizers said, "Well, what do we do? Because this is the main crop at this time of the year and it's all we have." Gurudeva said, "Okay, you can. You can take like that." So, (..) Gurudeva, He encouraged everyone to follow Cāturmāsya. Everyone must follow Kārttika very strictly. And He encouraged everyone to follow Cāturmāsya, but there were certain occasions, times, (..) when He allowed some, (..) some leniency or some concession, let's say.

source.title: Q&A Radhika's Favourite Raga, Chaturmasya and Sphurti - 2025-04-05 - Sri PremPrayojan

content.content: Rules in Our Lineage

In our lineage, Cāturmāsya is observed as described by the Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti (purebhakti.com, “The Beginning of Caturmasya”, 2012, updated in 2023); the same rules are given in the Russian edition of Arcana-dīpikā (Supplement to the Russian edition, Yaśodā Kumāra Prabhu, pp. 122–123) and in the Vaiṣṇava calendar of the Caitanya Academy. Gurudev lists them in his lectures: throughout all four months, no tomatoes, eggplants, laukī, parmal or honey (lecture no. 6557, 13 July 2022), and during Kārttika, no sesame or mustard, including their seeds and oils (lectures no. 5589, 31 October 2020, and no. 8032, 16 October 2024; see “Gurudev’s Mood”).
All four months: do not eat aubergines, tomatoes, laukī, parmal (potol), urad dal, or honey.

1st month (Śrīdhara, Śrāvaṇa): no leafy vegetables—spinach, any lettuce, any cabbage, kale, leafy herbs (coriander, mint, parsley, dill, curry leaves), dried herb powders, or herbal teas made from leaves.
2nd month (Hṛṣīkeśa, Bhādra): no yoghurt. If it is needed for health reasons, it should be diluted with water.
3rd month (Padmanābha, Āśvina): no milk. If one cannot do without it, a drop of lemon juice should be added to it.
4th month (Dāmodara, Kārttika): no mustard oil or sesame (the Academy’s calendar specifies sesame and mustard seeds and oils).
Clarifications

Dairy products. The restriction applies to milk itself and yogurt itself: Arcana-dīpikā includes among the foods that may always be eaten, even on Ekādaśī and during Cāturmāsya, “any dairy products, except milk and yogurt during their respective months” (translated from the Russian) (ibid., p. 120). The same passage also permits fruit, nuts, potatoes, pumpkin, courgettes, beetroot and cucumbers.

Concessions. If it is difficult to give up cabbage during the first month (for health reasons or because few other vegetables are available locally), one need not abstain from it; the same applies to tomatoes (Arcana-dīpikā, ibid., p. 123). Gurudev explains that someone who is ill or travelling is not obliged to follow all the rules, and recalls how, during Cāturmāsya at a festival in Russia, where at that time almost the only vegetables available were cabbage and tomatoes, Śrīla Gurudeva (Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja) allowed them to be eaten: he urged everyone to observe Cāturmāsya, and Kārttika very strictly, but allowed concessions in special circumstances (lecture no. 8943, 5 May 2025; also no. 6557, 13 July 2022).
Basis in Śāstra
Hari-bhakti-vilāsa quotes the basis for the monthly vows from the Skanda Purāṇa:

content.sanskrit:
śrāvaṇe varjayec chākaṁ dadhi bhādrapade tathā
dugdham āśvayuje māsi kārttike cāmiṣaṁ tyajet
content.translation: In the month of Śrāvaṇa, one should abstain from śāk (leafy vegetables); in Bhādrapada, from yoghurt; in Āśvina, from milk; and in Kārttika, from meat (āmiṣa). (Hari-bhakti-vilāsa 15.61, from the Skanda Purāṇa, Nāgara-khaṇḍa; Śyāmācaraṇa Kaviratna edition, p. 949)

content.content: Gurudev stresses that the power of the vow does not lie in the foods themselves: “it’s not some special biological formula”; we observe Cāturmāsya because Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and our ācāryas observed it, and by following them we strengthen ⟦mamatā⟧—the feeling of belonging to them, the foundation of prema (lectures no. 8943, 5 May 2025, and no. 5994, 26 July 2021).
Differences between Traditions

When Śrīla A. C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda came to the West, he introduced a simplified standard—one restriction per month: leafy vegetables, yoghurt, milk, and urad dal (Gurudev, lecture no. 6557, 13 July 2022). This standard is also reflected in the GCal calendar (ISKCON): abstaining from urad dal in the fourth month. In our lineage, urad dal is already excluded for all four months, so the fourth month entails abstaining from mustard oil and sesame. Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja insisted that devotees, especially those living in India, observe Cāturmāsya very strictly, and that those in the West observe it as far as possible (ibid.).

content.quote: Now, you have to understand this. The reason we follow Cāturmāsya, it's not that these particular things, as we mentioned before in regard to the sesame seeds, it's not some special biological formula that at that time it will help with your bhakti. But the thing is this, that Caitanya Mahāprabhu did it. Our Parama Gurudeva did it, our Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura did it. And so because they did it, when we follow them, we accept their ānugatya, it increases our mamatā for them. It increases our possessiveness for them. This is what my Gurudeva did. This is what my paramparā does. This is what my Caitanya Mahāprabhu has done. Just like in the middle of Cāturmāsya, in (..) the full moon (..) in the middle, it's the Viśvarūpa Mahotsava. So it's not the day that Viśvarūpa took sannyāsa. It's not even the day that he passed away. But it's the day that Caitanya Mahāprabhu when He was on tour and He was in Paṇḍharpura, He heard the news that (..) His brother Viśvarūpa had passed away in Paṇḍharpura. He actually entered into the date of Viṭṭhala there. But (..) the because Mahāprabhu heard that His brother had passed away at that time, then He shaved His head. Right? Because if a family member passes away, then you shave your head. So we also, even though you're not supposed to shave for the whole Cāturmāsya, but we shave our heads on the full moon in the middle of Cāturmāsya. Why? Because Mahāprabhu did. To have that mamatā that we're in the family of Mahāprabhu. And His elder brother is so dear to Him passed away. So it's not the regulation itself that has the potency, but it's obeying the regulation that (..) nourishes our possessiveness, our mamatā for Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

source.title: Q&A Radhika's Favourite Raga, Chaturmasya and Sphurti - 2025-04-05 - Sri PremPrayojan

more.quote:
So in Cāturmāsya, the brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs, they don't shave for four months. But in the middle... (..) In the middle of Cāturmāsya, you can (..) shave. There is Viśvarūpa-mahotsava. Viśvarūpa-mahotsava is the day that when Caitanya Mahāprabhu was in Pandharpur, He discovered that His brother Viśvarūpa, who had taken sannyāsa and became Śaṅkarāraṇya Svāmī, he had passed away in Pandharpur. So in the middle of Cāturmāsya, discovering that His brother had passed away there, He shaved His head. So if someone in your family passes away, you shave the head. So you can shave in the middle of Cāturmāsya, why? Because we are in Gaura-parivāra, the family of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. So (..) this nourishes our mamatā, our possessiveness for Caitanya Mahāprabhu. So in the middle, you can shave. So Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, because his beard was growing, he would... he told devotees, "Oh, bring a photographer, take a photograph! I want a photograph with a big beard, because in the future people will say, 'Oh, we don't need to follow Cāturmāsya.'" And that's why you can see, look on the altar here, yes, here and here, Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura with a big beard, to make sure that in the future devotees will not say, "Oh, no need to follow Cāturmāsya."

So we follow this Cāturmāsya, the real essence is mamatā, possessiveness for our guru-varga. "My Prabhupāda, Bhaktisiddhānta... my Prabhupāda did it, so I will follow it because I am his, I belong to him." "My Mahāprabhu (..) followed this (..) vrata as well." So the essence is mamatā for our guru-paramparā, mamatā for Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and mamatā is the foundation of prema.

source.title: 2021.07.26 Q&A - Next Acharya, Jat Gosai, Chaturmasya, Hemalata, Nirupadhi, Recordings, Pancharatra

more.quote: Śrīla, (..), Bhakti-siddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura and also Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja, they made sure that at the, towards the end of Cāturmāsya, they had a very thick beard, that a photographer should take a photograph of them, and then all devotees will see it. Otherwise, in the future someone will say, "Oh no, no, no, our ācāryas did not observe Cāturmāsya." Because for brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs, they should shave today and but they should, (..), not shave after that. Then they shave again on the Pūrṇimā at the end of Cāturmāsya. But there's (..) one concession that the Pūrṇimā in the middle of Cāturmāsya, this is a Viśvarūpa-mahotsava. And Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He shaved then because He had discovered that His brother Viśvarūpa had passed away and Mahāprabhu shaved in the middle of the Cāturmāsya one time. So also remembering Mahāprabhu and His love for Viśvarūpa, (..), the brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs, they may also shave in the middle of Cāturmāsya.

content.content: Brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs shave on the first day of Cāturmāsya, and then shave neither their heads nor their faces for all four months; they shave again on the pūrṇimā at the end of Cāturmāsya—Kārttika-pūrṇimā (Gurudev, lectures no. 6557, 13 July 2022, and no. 5994, 26 July 2021). Arcana-dīpikā applies this rule to sannyāsīs, brahmacārīs and vānaprasthas living in a maṭha (Supplement to the Russian edition, p. 123).
Viśvarūpa-mahotsava

The exception is the pūrṇimā in the middle of Cāturmāsya, Viśvarūpa-mahotsava (Bhādra-pūrṇimā). This is neither the day Viśvarūpa accepted sannyāsa nor the day of his departure, but the day when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, while travelling through South India, learned in Paṇḍharpur that His elder brother Viśvarūpa (Śaṅkarāraṇya Svāmī in sannyāsa) had left this world—and shaved His head, as one does when a family member passes away. Therefore, on this day brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs may also shave: in this way they nourish ⟦mamatā⟧—the feeling that we belong to Mahāprabhu’s family, the Gaura-parivāra (Gurudev, lectures no. 8943, 5 May 2025, no. 5994, 26 July 2021, and no. 6557, 13 July 2022; Arcana-dīpikā, p. 123). The Vaiṣṇava calendar of the Caitanya Academy notes that on this day brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs may shave if they wish. The date of Viśvarūpa-mahotsava for each year is given in the reference table at the end of the chapter—it is the day the third month begins.

Towards the end of Cāturmāsya, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura and Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja would ask to be photographed with their grown-out beards—so that no one in the future could say that our ācāryas did not observe Cāturmāsya (Gurudev, lectures no. 6557, 13 July 2022, no. 5994, 26 July 2021, and no. 9183, 10 October 2025).

content.quote:
By the causeless mercy of Śrī Guru and Gaurāṅga, during this month of Kārtika, every day we come before Śrī Kṛṣṇa with a dīpa in our hand and we offer the dīpas to His lotus feet, and we sing the Śrī Dāmodarāṣṭakam. Because this injunction has been given in Hari-bhakti-vilāsa, and there, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmīpāda said this is an essential part of the Dāmodara-vrata.

This month of Kārtika is also known as Dāmodara-māsa, the month of Dāmodara. Because dāma means rope and udara means belly. Dāmodara is the name of Kṛṣṇa who was bound around the belly by a rope, by His mother, Yaśodā. Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is unlimited and infinite, yet He is bound, not by rope, but by prema. So, those who, in this Dāmodara-māsa, month of Dāmodara, will sing the Dāmodarāṣṭakam with a pure heart, then they can please Lord Dāmodara and they can please Śrīmatī Rādhikā, and by the mercy of Śrīmatī Rādhikā, then Kṛṣṇa can be bound with the ropes of love in the heart of that devotee. So, this Dāmodara-vrata is extremely powerful, such that the all-powerful Supreme Lord becomes helpless in the presence of the devotee who follows this vrata.

source.title: Day 3 - Sri Damodarashtakam part 1 - 2020-11-02 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: So, actually, the Kārtika-vrata, it can be observed from the (..) ekādaśī or the dvādaśī or the pūrṇimā, the first day—the ekādaśī, dvādaśī, and pūrṇimā that come after Rāma-vijaya-daśamī. That is the fourth month of Cāturmāsya. So, our Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura and Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Mahārāja, they used to honor from pūrṇimā to pūrṇimā, because there are still the (..) if you finish on the ekādaśī, there're still some days of the month of Kārtika left, which is Rādhikā's month, and that is also Bhīṣma-pañcaka. And so we follow from pūrṇimā to pūrṇimā. The Kārtika-vrata is (..) the fourth month of Cāturmāsya.

So during this month, we'll have to fast from sesame seeds. And sesame oil. Don't take anything with mustard seeds. Or mustard oil. No tomatoes. No eggplants. No laukī, parmal, or urad dāl. And no honey. Brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs, they should not shave. We will have to make a vow to sing everyday Śrī Dāmodarāṣṭakam of Satyavrata Ṛṣi. And certain bhajanas are part of our vrata. We will sing everyday Namāmi Nanda-nandanam. Why? To please Rādhikā. And Rādhā-kṛpā-kaṭākṣa-stotra-ratna, the glories of Rādhikā, to please Śrī Kṛṣṇa. And in all of these activities, we'll perform them to attain our goal of life, prayojana.
